name: benazepril
uses: Hypertension. Used alone or in combination with other antihypertensives.
action: Decreases rate of conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II, a potent vasoconstrictor. Results in lower levels of angiotensin II, causing an increase in plasma renin activity and decreased aldosterone secretion. Result: Lowers BP.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to benazepril. History of angioedema with or without previous treatment with ACE inhibitors. Use with aliskiren in patients with diabetes. Coadministration with or within 36 hrs of switching to or from a neprilysin inhibitor (e.g., sacubitril). Caution: Renal impairment. Caution: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy without flow tract obstruction. Caution: severe aortic stenosis. Caution: before, during, or immediately following major surgery.
sideEffects: Cough, headache, dizziness, fatigue, drowsiness, nausea, rash, fever.
adverseEffects: Excessive hypotension (“first-dose syncope”) may occur in patients with HF, severe salt or volume depletion. Angioedema, hyperkalemia occur rarely. Agranulocytosis, neutropenia may be noted in patients with renal impairment, collagen vascular disease (scleroderma, systemic lupus erythematosus). Nephrotic syndrome may occur in patients with history of renal disease.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC before therapy begins and q2wks for 3 mos, then periodically thereafter. Obtain BP immediately before each dose, in addition to regular monitoring (be alert to fluctuations). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Assist with ambulation if dizziness occurs. Monitor BP, renal function, urinary protein, serum potassium. Monitor CBC with differential if.

name: bendamustine
uses: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). Indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma (NHL) that has progressed during or within 6 mos of treatment with riTUXimab or a riTUXimab-containing regimen. First-line treatment for follicular lymphoma. Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia.
action: Alkylates and cross-links double-stranded DNA. Result: Inhibits tumor cell growth, causes cell death.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to bendamustine. (Bendeka only): polyethylene glycol 400, or propylene glycol mono-thioglycerol. Caution: Baseline cytopenias, hepatic/renal impairment, conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds). Caution: dermatologic disease, HF, dehydration. Caution: patients at high risk for tumor lysis syndrome (high tumor burden). Caution: history of hepatitis B virus infection, herpes zoster infection.
sideEffects: Note: Frequency and occurrence of side effects may vary depending on indication of treatment, nausea, fatigue, vomiting, anorexia, diarrhea, pyrexia, constipation.
adverseEffects: Grade 3–4 myelosuppression reported in 98% of patients. Infections including sepsis, septic shock, herpes zoster, upper respiratory tract infection, UTI, sinusitis, pneumonia, febrile neutropenia, oral candidiasis, nasopharyngitis were reported. Reactivation of cytomegalovirus, hepatitis B virus, mycobacterium tuberculosis, herpes zoster was reported. Tumor lysis syndrome may present as acute renal failure, hypocalcemia, hyperuricemia, hyperphosphatemia.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BMP, LFT; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Screen for active infection. Assess usual bowel movement patterns, stool characteristics. Ensure adequate hydration in. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC for myelosuppression; BMP; LFT for hepatotoxicity; renal function (CrCl, GFR). Hematologic nadirs usually occur in 3rd wk of therapy. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s at risk for tumor lysis syndrome. Question history of hepatic/renal impairment; history of hepatitis B virus infection, herpes zoster infection.

name: benralizumab
uses: Add-on maintenance patients with severe asthma, aged 12 yrs and older, and with an eosinophilic phenotype.
action: Inhibits signaling of interleukin-5 cytokine, reducing production and survival of eosinophils responsible for asthmatic inflammation and pathogenesis. Result: Prevents inflammatory process; relieves signs/symptoms of asthma.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to benralizumab. Caution: History of helminth (parasite) infection. Caution: long-term use of corticosteroids. Caution: Not indicated for treatment of other eosinophilic conditions. Caution: relief of acute bronchospasm or status asthmaticus.
sideEffects: Headache, pyrexia.
adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis, angioedema, bronchospasm, hypotension, urticaria, rash were reported. Hypersensitivity reactions typically occurred hrs to days after administration. Infections including bacterial/viral pharyngitis may occur. Unknown if treatment will influence the immunological response to helminth (parasite) infection.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain apical pulse, oxygen saturation. Auscultate lung fields. Question history of parasitic infection, hypersensitivity reaction. Pts with preexisting helminth (parasite) infection should be treated prior to initiation. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor rate, depth, rhythm of respirations. Assess lungs for wheezing, rales. Monitor oxygen saturation. Interrupt or discontinue treatment if hypersensitivity reaction, opportu.

name: bethanechol
uses: Acute postoperative and postpartum nonobstructive urinary retention, neurogenic atony of urinary bladder with retention.
action: Stimulates parasympathetic nervous system, increasing bladder muscle tone and causing contractions, which initiates urination. Also stimulates gastric motility, increasing gastric tone, and may restore peristalsis. Result: May initiate urination, bladder emptying.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to bethanechol. Mechanical obstruction of GI/GU tract, GI or bladder wall instability, hyperthyroidism, asthma, peptic ulcer disease, epilepsy, pronounced bradycardia or hypotension, parkinsonism, CAD, vasomotor instability, bladder neck obstruction, spastic GI disturbances, acute inflammatory lesions of the GI tract, peritonitis, marked vagotonia. Caution: Bladder reflux infection.
sideEffects: Belching, changes in vision, blurred vision, diarrhea, urinary urgency or frequency, dyspnea, chest tightness, bronchospasm.
adverseEffects: Overdose produces CNS stimulation (insomnia, anxiety, orthostatic hypotension), cholinergic stimulation (headache, increased salivation/diaphoresis, nausea, vomiting, flushed skin, abdominal pain, seizures).
nursingConsiderations: INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor urine output. Palpate bladder for evidence of urinary retention. Obtain bladder scan to assess urinary volume. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING . - Report nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, diaphoresis, increased salivary secretions, irregular heartbeat, muscle weakness, severe abdominal pain, difficulty breathing.

name: bevacizumab
uses: Cervical Cancer: Persistent, recurrent, or metastatic cervical cancer (in combination with paclitaxel and cisplatin or paclitaxel and topotecan). Colorectal Cancer: Metastatic colorectal cancer in combination with fluorouracil-based therapy for first-or second-line treatment. Metastatic colorectal cancer in combination with fluoropyrimidine-irinotecan– or fluoropyrimidine-oxaliplatin–based therapy for patients having progressed on a first-line bevacizumab regimen. Epithelial Ovarian, Fallopian Tube, .
action: Binds to and neutralizes vascular endothelial growth factor, preventing association with endothelial receptors. Result: Inhibition of microvascular growth retards growth of all tissue, including metastatic tissue.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to bevacizumab. Caution: Cardiovascular disease, acquired coagulopathy, preexisting hypertension, patients at risk of thrombocytopenia. Caution: Pts with CNS metastasis. Caution: Do not administer within 28 days of major surgery or active bleeding. Caution: Pts at risk for hemorrhage (e.g., history of GI bleeding, fistulas, coagulation disorders, recent trauma.
sideEffects: Asthenia, vomiting, anorexia, hypertension, epistaxis, stomatitis, constipation, headache.
adverseEffects: Fatal GI perforations reported in up to 3% of patients. Serious fistula formations in bladder, biliary, bronchopleural, tracheoesophageal, renal, vaginal sites may occur. Necrotizing fasciitis due to poor wound healing complications, GI perforation may occur. Severe bleeding events including CNS hemorrhage, GI bleeding, epistaxis, hemoptysis, hematemesis, pulmonary hemorrhage, vaginal bleeding were reported.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, serum potassium, sodium levels at regular intervals during therapy. Assess for proteinuria with urinalysis. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC for myelosuppression; renal function (CrCl, GFR). Monitor for GI perforation, GI bleeding, bloody stool; symptoms of intracranial bleeding (aphasia, blindness, confusion, facial droop, hemiplegia, seizures); symptoms of MI (chest pain, diaphoresis, left arm/jaw pain, increased serum troponin, ST segment elevation), CVA (aphasia. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s with 2+ or greater urine dipstick reading, a 24-hr urine collection is advised. Question history as listed in Precautions. Screen for active infection. Offer emotional support.

name: bexagliflozin
uses: Adjunct treatment to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
action: Inhibits SGLT2, the transporter responsible for reabsorption of the majority of glucose from the renal glomerular filtrate in the proximal renal tubule, reducing reabsorption of filtered glucose and lowering the renal threshold for glucose. Result: Increases urinary excretion of glucose; lowers serum glucose levels.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to bexagliflozin; other SGLT2 inhibitors; patients on dialysis. Caution: Mild to moderate renal impairment (CrCl greater 30 mL/min), hypovolemia/dehydration, elderly. Caution: patients at risk for lower leg amputation (diabetic foot ulcers, peripheral vascular disease). Caution: recent genital mycotic infection. Caution: patients at risk for diabetic ketoacidosis (insulin dose reduction, acute febrile illness, reduced calorie intake, surgery, alcohol abuse).
sideEffects: Increased urination, thirst, vaginal pruritus.
adverseEffects: Symptomatic hypotension (orthostatic hypotension, postural dizziness, syncope) may occur, especially in patients who are elderly, use concomitant loop diuretics, or have baseline systolic hypotension. Intravascular volume depletion may cause acute kidney injury requiring dialysis. Hypoglycemic events were reported, especially in patients using concomitant hypoglycemic medications. Fatal cases of ketoacidosis were reported.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain BUN, serum creatinine, eGFR, CrCl, blood glucose level, Hgb A1c; BP. Assess hydration status. Correct volume depletion prior to initiation. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BUN, serum creatinine, eGFR, CrCl, blood glucose level, Hgb A1c; BP periodically. Monitor for hypoglycemia (anxiety,. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s’s understanding of diabetes management, routine home glucose monitoring. Obtain dietary consult for nutritional education. Question history of hepatic/renal impairment, type 1 diabetes, ketoacidosis. Receive full medication history and screen for interactions.

name: bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir
pharmacoClass: Integrase inhibitor, nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor, nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitor
uses: Indicated as complete regimen for HIV-1 infection in adults and pediatric patients weighing 14 kg or more who are antiretroviral naive or to replace the current antiretroviral regimen in patients who are virologically suppressed (HIV-1 RNA < 50 copies/mL) on a stable antiretroviral regimen with no history of treatment failure and no known substitutions associated with resistance to the individual components of bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir.
action: Bictegravir inhibits strand transfer activity of HIV-1 integrase, essential for viral replication. Emtricitabine inhibits HIV-1 reverse transcriptase by competing with natural substrates, resulting in chain termination. Result: Interferes with HIV replication, slowing progression of HIV infection.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to bictegravir/emtridtabtaefenofovir. Concomitant use of dofetilide, rifampin. Caution: Mild to moderate hepatic/renal impairment. Caution: History of depression, suicidal ideation. Caution: hepatitis B or C virus infection. Caution: Concomitant use of nephrotoxic medications.
sideEffects: Diarrhea, nausea, headache, fatigue, abnormal dreams, dizziness, insomnia, vomiting.
adverseEffects: If therapy is discontinued, patients coinfected with hepatitis B virus have an increased risk for viral replication, worsening of hepatic function, and may experience hepatic decompensation and/or failure. May induce immune reconstitution syndrome (inflammatory response to dormant opportunistic infections, such as Mycobacterium avium, cytomegalovirus, PCP, tuberculosis, or acceleration of autoimmune disorders such as Graves’ disease, polymyositis, Guillain-Barré). Acute renal failure, Fanconi syndrom.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain BUN, serum creatinine, creatinine clearance, GFR; CD4+ count, viral load, HIV-1 RNA level; urine glucose, urine protein. Obtain serum phosphate level in. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CD4+ count, viral load, HIV-1 RNA level for treatment effectiveness. Monitor renal function as clinically indicated. An increase in serum creatinine > 0.4 mg/dL from. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s with chronic kidney disease.

name: binimetinib
uses: Patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a BRAF V600E or V600K mutation (in combination with encorafenib).
action: Potent and selective inhibitor of mitogen-activated extracellular kinase (MEK) pathway. Reversibly inhibits MEK1 and MEK2, which are upstream regulators of the ERK pathway. Result: Increases apoptosis and reduces tumor growth.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to binimetinib. Caution: Baseline cytopenias. Caution: patients at risk for hemorrhage (e.g., history of GI bleeding, coagulation disorders, recent trauma. Caution: concomitant use of anticoagulants, NSAIDs, antiplatelets), hepatic/renal impairment, pulmonary disease, cardiovascular disease, HF. Caution: History of thromboembolism (deep vein thrombosis [DVT], pulmonary embolism [PE]).
sideEffects: Fatigue, nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, abdominal pain, constipation, rash, visual impairment.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (anemia, leukopenia, lymphopenia, neutropenia) is an expected response to therapy. Cardiomyopathy reported in 7% of patients. DVT reported in 6% of patients. PE reported in 3% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Confirm presence of BRAF V600E or V600K mutation in tumor specimen before initiation. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC for cytopenias; LFT for hepatotoxicity (bruising, hematuria, jaundice, right upper abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, weight loss); CPK for rhabdomyolysis.

name: bisoprolol
uses: Hypertension, alone or in combination with other medications.
action: Selectively blocks beta1-adrenergic receptors. Result: Slows sinus heart rate, decreases BP.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to bisoprolol. Cardiogenic shock, marked sinus bradycardia, overt HF, second-or third-degree heart block (except in patients with pacemaker). Caution: Concurrent use of digoxin, verapamil, diltiaZEM, HF, history of severe anaphylaxis to allergens, renal/hepatic impairment, hyperthyroidism, diabetes, bronchospastic disease, myasthenia gravis, psychiatric disease, peripheral vascular disease. Caution: Raynaud’s disease.
sideEffects: Fatigue, headache, dizziness, arthralgia, peripheral edema, rhinitis, pharyngitis, diarrhea.
adverseEffects: Overdose may produce profound bradycardia, hypotension. Abrupt withdrawal may result in diaphoresis, palpitations, headache, tremors. May precipitate HF, MI in patients with cardiac disease, thyroid storm in patients with thyrotoxicosis, peripheral ischemia in those with existing peripheral vascular disease. Hypoglycemia may occur in previously controlled diabetes.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess BUN, serum creatinine; GFR. Assess BP, apical pulse immediately before drug is administered (if pulse is 60/min or less or systolic BP is < 90 mm Hg, withhold medication, contact physician). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BP, pulse for quality, irregular rate, bradycardia. Assist with ambulation if dizziness occurs. Assess for peripheral edema. Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Do not abruptly discontinue medication. - Compliance with therapy regimen is essential to control hypertension. - If dizziness occurs, sit or lie down immediately. - Avoid tasks that requ.

name: blinatumomab
uses: Adults and children with CD19-positive B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) in first or second complete remission with minimal residual disease (MRD) ≥ 0.1%. Relapsed or refractory CD19-positive B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL).
action: Binds to CD19 expressed on B cells and CD3 expressed on T cells. Activates endogenous T cells, forming a cytolytic synapse between a cytotoxic T cell and the cancer target B cell. Result: Inhibits tumor cell growth and metastasis in ALL.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to blinatumomab. Caution: Baseline cytopenias. Caution: active infection or patients at increased risk of infection (diabetes, indwelling catheters), hepatic/renal impairment, high tumor burden, history of cognitive or seizure disorders, syncope, elderly.
sideEffects: Pyrexia, headache, peripheral edema, nausea, tremor, constipation, diarrhea, cough.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (anemia, leukopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia) is an expected outcome of treatment. Cytokine release syndrome (CRS) may be life threatening or fatal. Symptoms of CRS may include asthenia, hypotension, nausea, pyrexia. Elevated ALT/AST, bilirubin.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BMP, LFT, serum magnesium, phosphate, ionized calcium, vital signs. Consider electrolyte correction before starting treatment. Screen for home medications requiring narrow therapeutic index. Screen for active infection, history of seizures, hepatic/renal impairment, cognitive disorders. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, LFT, serum electrolytes (correct as indicated), vital signs. Monitor closely for cytokine release syndrome, neurologic toxicities, serious infection, tumor lysis syndrome, hepatic i.

name: bortezomib
uses: Relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma. Multiple myeloma. Antibody-mediated rejection in cardiac transplantation, relapsed/refractory follicular lymphoma.
action: Inhibits proteasomes (enzyme complexes regulating protein homeostasis within the cell). Result: Produces cell-cycle arrest, apoptosis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to bortezomib, boron, or mannitol; intrathecal administration. Caution: Concomitant use of CYP3A4 inhibitors, history of syncope, concomitant use of antihypertensives. Caution: dehydration, diabetes, hepatic impairment, preexisting cardiac disease, neuropathy.
sideEffects: Fatigue, malaise, asthenia, nausea, diarrhea, anorexia, constipation, fever.
adverseEffects: Thrombocytopenia reported in 40% of patients. GI, intracerebral hemorrhage are associated with drug-induced thrombocytopenia. Anemia occurs in 32% of patients. New onset or worsening of existing neuropathy occurs in 37% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC. Ensure adequate hydration prior to initiation of therapy. Antiemetics, antidiarrheals may be effective in preventing, treating nausea, vomiting, diarrhea. Offer emotional support. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Routinely assess BP; monitor. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s for orthostatic hypotension. Maintain strict I&O. Monitor CBC, especially platelet count, throughout treatment. Monitor renal, hepatic, pulmonary function throughout therapy.

name: bosutinib
uses: Adults and patients 1 yr of age and older with chronic phase Ph+ chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML), newly-diagnosed or resistant or intolerant to prior therapy. Adults with chronic phase (CP), accelerated phase (AP), or blast phase (BP) Ph+ CML with resistance or intolerance to prior therapy.
action: Inhibits Bcr-Abl tyrosine kinase, a translocation-created enzyme, created by the Philadelphia chromosome abnormality noted in chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML). Inhibits Src-family kinase, including Src, Lyn, and Hck. Result: Inhibits cancer cell growth and proliferation in chronic, accelerated, or blast phase CML.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to bosutinib. Caution: Baseline cytopenias. Caution: hepatic impairment, recent diarrhea, pulmonary edema, HF, fluid retention. Caution: History of pancreatitis, moderate to severe renal impairment. Caution: Avoid concurrent use of CYP3A4 inducers/inhibitors.
sideEffects: Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, rash, pyrexia, fatigue, headache.
adverseEffects: Severe fluid retention may result in pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, pulmonary edema, ascites. Neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, anemia is an expected response of drug therapy. Severe diarrhea may result in fluid loss, electrolyte imbalance, hypotension. Hepatotoxicity occurred in 7%–9% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BMP, LFT; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential,. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Weigh daily and monitor for unexpected rapid weight gain, edema. Monitor for changes in serum electrolytes, LFT during treatment. Offer antiemetics for nausea, vomiting. Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency.

name: brentuximab vedotin
uses: Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma (cHL): adults with relapsed or refractory classical Hodgkin’s lymphoma after failure of autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) or after failure of at least two prior multiagent chemotherapy regimens or in patients who are not transplant candidates. Classical Hodgkin’s lymphoma, previously untreated stage III or IV in combination with doxorubicin, vinblastine, and dacarbazine. Adults with classical Hodgkin’s lymphoma in ad.
action: Binds to CD30-expressing cells, allowing the antibody to direct the drug to a target on lymphoma cells, disrupting the microtubule network within the cell. Result: Induces cell cycle arrest, cell death.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to brentuximab. Avoid use with bleomycin (increased risk for pulmonary toxicity). Caution: Renal/hepatic impairment, peripheral neuropathy, infusion reactions, neutropenia, tumor lysis syndrome. Caution: Stevens-Johnson syndrome, pregnancy.

name: brexpiprazole
uses: Adjunct for antidepressants for the major depressive disorder in adults. Schizophrenia. Agitation associated with dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease.
action: Provides partial agonist activity at DOPamine and serotonin (5-HT1A) receptors and antagonist activity at serotonin (5-HT2A) receptors. Result: Diminishes schizophrenic, depressive behavior.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to brexpiprazole. Caution: Concurrent use of CNS depressants (including alcohol), antihypertensives. Caution: disorders in which CNS depression is a feature. Caution: cardiovascular or cerebrovascular disease (may induce hypotension). Caution: Parkinson’s disease.
sideEffects: Headache, nasopharyngitis, dyspepsia, akathisia, somnolence, tremor, constipation, fatigue.
adverseEffects: May increase risk of death in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis. Most deaths appeared to be cardiovascular (e.g., HF, sudden death) or infectious (e.g., pneumonia) in nature. Increased incidence of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in patients 24 yrs and younger was reported. May increase risk of neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS).
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain BMP, capillary blood glucose, vital signs; CBC in. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor weight, BMP, capillary blood glucose, vital signs. Diligently monitor for extrapyramidal symptoms, tardive dyskinesia, hypotension, syncope, cerebrovascular or cardiovascular dysfunction, NMS. Assess for therapeu. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s with preexisting low WBC or history of leukopenia or neutropenia. Receive full medication history and screen for drug interactions. Assess behavior, appearance, emotional state, response to environment, speech pattern, thought content. Correct dehydration, hypovolemia.

name: brigatinib
uses: First-line patients with anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)– positive metastatic non–small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
action: A broad-spectrum kinase inhibitor (activity against EGFR, ALK, ROSI, IGF-1R and FLT-3). Inhibits ALK downstream signaling proteins. Result: Expresses anti-tumor activity against EML-ALK mutant forms shown in NSCLC in patients progressed with crizotinib.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to brigatinib. Caution: Baseline cytopenias. Caution: History of symptomatic bradycardia, bradyarrhythmias, diabetes, hepatic/renal impairment, hypertension, ocular disease, pancreatitis, pulmonary disease. Caution: Concomitant use of strong CYP3A inhibitors, beta blockers, calcium channel blockers (see Interactions).

name: budesonide
brand: Entocort EC, Ortikos, Pulmicort Flexhaler, Pulmicort, Tarpeyo, Uceris
uses: Nasal: (Rx): seasonal or perennial allergic rhinitis6 yrs and older. (OTC): hay fever, other upper respiratory allergies6 yrs and older. Nebulization, oral inhalation: Maintenance or prophylaxis therapy for asthma (dry powder inhaler) or 12 mos to 8 yrs (nebulization). PO: mild to moderate active Crohn’s disease. Maintenance of clinical remission of mild to moderate Crohn’s disease.
action: Inhibits accumulation of inflammatory cells; controls rate of protein synthesis; decreases migration of polymorphonuclear leukocytes (reverses capillary permeability and lysosomal stabilization at cellular level). Result: Relieves symptoms of allergic rhinitis, asthma, Crohn’s disease.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to budesonide (nebulization/inhalation), primary treatment of status asthmaticus, acute episodes of asthma. Not for relief of acute bronchospasms. Nasal: Use in children younger than 6 yrs of age. Caution: Thyroid disease, hepatic impairment, renal impairment, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, glaucoma, cataracts, myasthenia gravis, patients at risk for osteoporosis, seizures, GI disease, post acute MI, elderly.
sideEffects: Nasal: Mild nasopharyngeal irritation, burning, stinging, dryness, headache, cough, inhalation: Flu-like symptoms, pharyngitis.
adverseEffects: Acute hypersensitivity reaction (urticaria, angioedema, severe bronchospasm) occurs rarely.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Question for hypersensitivity to any corticosteroids, components. Auscultate lung sounds. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor for relief of symptoms. Auscultate lung sounds. Observe proper use of medication delivery device to ensure correct technique. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Improvement noted in 24 hrs, but full effect may take 3–7 days. - Report if no improvement in symptoms or if sneezing, nasal irritation occurs.

name: bumetanide
uses: Edema secondary to HF, renal disease, (including nephrotic syndrome), or hepatic disease.
action: Enhances excretion of sodium, chloride, and, to lesser degree, potassium by direct action at ascending limb of loop of Henle and in proximal tubule. Result: Produces diuresis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to bumetanide. Anuria, hepatic coma, severe electrolyte depletion (until condition improves or is corrected). Caution: Severe hypersensitivity to sulfonamides. Caution: hypotension.
sideEffects: Increased urinary frequency and urine volume, muscle cramps, dizziness, hypotension, headache, nausea, impaired hearing, pruritus.
adverseEffects: Vigorous diuresis may lead to profound water and electrolyte depletion, resulting in hypokalemia, hyponatremia, dehydration, coma, circulatory collapse. Ototoxicity manifested as deafness, vertigo, tinnitus may occur, especially in patients with severe renal impairment or those taking other ototoxic drugs. Blood dyscrasias, acute hypotensive episodes have been reported.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain vital signs, especially BP for hypotension, before administration. Assess for edema. Observe skin turgor, mucous membranes for hydration status. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Continue to monitor BP, vital signs, electrolytes, I&O, weight. Note extent of diuresis. Watch for changes from initial assessment (hypokalemia may result in muscle weakness, tremor, muscle cramps, altered mental status, cardiac arrhythmias; hyponatremia may result in confusion, thirst, cold/clammy skin). PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Expect increased urinary frequency/volume. - Report auditory abnormalities (e.g., sense of fullness in ears, tinnitus). -.

name: cabazitaxel
uses: Used in combination with predniSONE for castration-resistant metastatic prostate cancer previously treated with a DOCEtaxel-containing regimen.
action: Binds to tubulin to promote assembly into microtubules and inhibits disassembly, which stabilizes microtubules. Inhibits microtubule depolymerization/cell division. Result: Arrests the cell cycle, inhibiting tumor proliferation.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to cabazitaxel. Severe hepatic impairment (total serum bilirubin > 3 times upper limit of normal [ULN]). Neutrophil count of 1, 500 cells/mm3 or less, history of hypersensitivity to polysorbate 80. Caution: Mild to moderate hepatic impairment (bilirubin equal to or < 3 times ULN), elderly, pregnancy, renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min). Caution: Pts at risk for developing GI complications (e.g., GI ulceration, concomitant use of NSAIDs).
sideEffects: Diarrhea, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, constipation, esthesia, abdominal pain, anorexia.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (anemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia) is an expected response to therapy, but more severe reactions including severe neutropenia, febrile neutropenia may be life threatening. Hypersensitivity reaction may include generalized rash, erythema, hypotension, bronchospasm. 94% of patients develop Grade 1–4 neutropenia and associated complications including anemia, thrombocytopenia, sepsis. GI abnormalities, hypertension, arrhythmias, renal failure may occur.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain ANC, CBC, BMP, LFT, serum testosterone. Assess ANC, CBC prior to each infusion. Question history of hypersensitivity reaction; renal/hepatic impairment; intolerance to corticosteroids. Receive full medication history and screen for interactions. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, ANC on wkly basis during cycle 1 and before each treatment cycle thereafter; do not administer if ANC < 1,500 cells/mm3. Monitor serum ALT, AST, renal function. Monitor for hypersensitivity reaction (rash, erythema, dyspnea). Encourage adequate fluid intake.

name: cabotegravir/rilpivirine
pharmacoClass: Integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI), non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI)
uses: HIV-1 infection in adults and adolescents 12 yrs of age and older and weighing at least 35 kg to replace the current antiretroviral regimen in patients who are virologically suppressed (HIV-1 RNA < 50 copies/mL) on a stable antiretroviral regimen with no history of treatment failure and with no known or suspected resistance to either cabotegravir or rilpivirine.
action: Cabotegravir inhibits HIV integrase by blocking strand transfer of retroviral DNA integration (essential for HIV replication cycle). Rilpivirine blocks noncompetitive HIV-1 reverse transcriptase (does not inhibit DNA polymerases). Result: Interferes with HIV replication, slowing progression of HIV infection.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to cabotegravir or rilpivirine. Concomitant use of carBAMazepine, oxcarbazepine, PHENobarbital, phenytoin, rifabutin, rifAMPin, rifapentine, dexAMETHasone (and others). Caution: Hepatic/renal impairment, psychiatric disorders (e.g., depression, psychosis, suicidal ideation). Caution: Concomitant use of other antiretrovirals is not recommended.
sideEffects: Injection site reactions (pain/discomfort, nodules, induration, swelling, erythema, pruritus, bruising/discoloration, warmth.
adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity reactions, including angioedema, dyspnea, hepatitis. Severe rash that is accompanied by blisters, fatigue, fever, muscle and joint pain, oral lesions may occur. Serious postinjection reactions (abdominal cramping, agitation, bronchospasm, chest or back pain, dizziness, flushing, oral numbness, sweating) reported in < 1% of patients. Hepatotoxicity may occur in patients with or without prior hepatic impairment.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain LFT, CD4+ count, viral load, HIV-1 RNA level; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Pts should be carefully selected for treatment and must agree to comply with the required dosing schedule. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CD4+ count, viral load, HIV-1 RNA level for treatment effectivene. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s that noncompliance may cause drug resistance and viral rebound. Question history of hepatic/renal impairment; psychiatric disorder, suicidal ideation and behavior. nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain WBC. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. Report diarrhea promptly due to potential for serious colitis (even with topical or vaginal administration). Assess skin for rash (dryness, irritation) with topical application. With all routes of administration, be alert for superinfection: fever, vomiting, diarrhea, anal/genital pruritus, oral mucosal changes (ulceration, pain, erythema). PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - It is essential to complete drug therapy despite improvement of symptoms. Early discontinuati.

name: clofarabine
uses: Pediatric patients (1–21 yrs) with relapsed or refractory acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) (after at least 2 prior regimens).
action: Metabolized intracellularly to clofarabine triphosphate. Inhibits ribonucleo-side reductase, which inhibits DNA synthesis. Result: Decreases cell replication, inhibits cell repair.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to clofarabine. Caution: Dehydration, hypotension, concomitant nephrotoxic or hepatotoxic medications, renal/hepatic impairment.
sideEffects: Vomiting, nausea, diarrhea, pruritus, headache, fever, dermatitis, rigors.
adverseEffects: Neutropenia occurred in 57% of patients. Pericardial effusion in 35%. Left ventricular systolic dysfunction in 27%. Hepatomegaly, jaundice in 15%.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain, BMP, LFT; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Question history of hepatic/renal impairment. Offer emotional support. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, renal function test, LFT, serum uric acid. Monitor respiratory status, cardiac function. Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. Assess for GI disturbances. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Do not have immunizations without physician’s approval (drug lowers resista.

name: clonazePAM
uses: Monotherapy or Adjunct for Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (petit mal variant epilepsy). Akinetic, myoclonic seizures. Absence seizures (petit mal) unresponsive to succinimides. Panic disorder.
action: Enhances activity of GABA; depresses nerve impulse transmission in motor cortex. Result: Produces anxiolytic, anticonvulsant effects.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to clonazePAM. Active narrow-angle glaucoma, severe hepatic disease. Caution: Renal/hepatic impairment, impaired gag reflex, chronic respiratory disease, elderly, debilitated patients, depression, patients at risk of suicide or drug dependence, concomitant use of other CNS depressants.
sideEffects: Mild, transient drowsiness, ataxia, behavioral disturbances (aggression, irritability, agitation), especially in children, dizziness.
adverseEffects: Abrupt withdrawal may result in pronounced restlessness, irritability, insomnia, hand tremors, abdominal/muscle cramps, diaphoresis, vomiting, status epilepticus. Overdose results in drowsiness, confusion, diminished reflexes, coma. Antidote: Flumazenil (.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Review history of seizure disorder (frequency, duration, intensity, level of consciousness [LOC]). For panic attack, assess motor responses (agitation, trembling, tension), autonomic responses (cold/clammy hands, diaphoresis). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Observe for excess sedation, respiratory depression, suicidal ideation. Assess children, elderly for paradoxical reaction, particularly during early therapy. Initiate seizure precautions, observe frequently for recurrence of seizure activity. Assist with ambulation if drowsiness, ataxia occur. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s on long-term therapy, CBC, BMP, LFT should be performed periodically. Evaluate for therapeutic response: Decreased i.

name: clopidogrel
uses: Acute coronary syndrome (NSTEMI, STEMI). Recent MI or stroke prevention. Peripheral arterial disease. Stent thrombosis.
action: Irreversibly inhibits the P2Y12 ADP receptor on platelets, preventing ADP-induced platelet aggregation and thrombus formation.
precautions: Caution: increased bleeding risk, surgery (hold 5–7 days before elective surgery), hepatic impairment, CYP2C19 poor metabolizers have reduced efficacy.
sideEffects: Bleeding (most common), bruising, dyspepsia, diarrhea, rash, pruritus.
adverseEffects: Major or fatal bleeding events. TTP (thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura — rare but life-threatening). Neutropenia.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, coagulation studies. Assess bleeding risk, current medications (NSAIDs, anticoagulants). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor for unusual bleeding (gums, urine, stool, prolonged bleeding from cuts). Assess for TTP (fever, neurologic changes, renal dysfunction). Do not switch brands without physician approval. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING Do not stop without telling your doctor — stopping can cause heart attack or stroke. Tell all healthcare providers you take this drug before any procedure. Use electric razor. Avoid NSAIDs unless approved.

name: cobimetinib
uses: Patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a BRAF V600E or V600K mutation, in combination with vemurafenib. As a single agent for the adults with histiocytic neoplasms.
action: Potent and selective inhibitor of mitogen-activated extracellular kinase (MEK) pathway. Reversibly inhibits MEK1 and MEK2, which are upstream regulators of the ERK pathway. Result: Causes apoptosis and reduces tumor growth.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to cobimetinib. Caution: Baseline anemia, lymphopenia, thrombocytopenia. Caution: cardiomyopathy, hepatic/renal impairment, HF, hypertension, ocular disorders. Caution: patients at risk for bleeding (history of gastrointestinal, genitourinary, intracranial, reproductive system bleeding), electrolyte imbalance. Caution: Not recommended in patients taking moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors.
sideEffects: Diarrhea, photosensitivity, sunburn, solar dermatitis, nausea, pyrexia, vomiting, acneiform dermatitis.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (anemia lymphopenia, thrombocytopenia) is an expected response to therapy. New primary malignancies, including squamous cell carcinoma, keratoacanthoma, secondary-primary melanomas, were reported. Serious, sometimes fatal hemorrhagic events, including GI bleeding (4% of patients), intracranial bleeding (1% of patients), hematuria (2% of patients), reproductive system hemorrhage (2% of patients), have occurred. Other hemorrhagic events may include cerebral/conjunctival/intracranial/gingival/hemorrho.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Confirm presence of BRAF V600E or V600K mutation in tumor specimen prior to initiation. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, BMP, LFT, CPK; serum albumin, magnesium, phosphate, ionized calcium; vital signs. Assess skin for ne.

name: codeine
uses: Mild to moderate pain. Cough suppression (antitussive). Often combined with acetaminophen (Tylenol #3, #4).
action: Prodrug — metabolized to morphine by CYP2D6 enzyme. Active morphine binds mu-opioid receptors in CNS, producing analgesia and cough suppression.
precautions: Caution: renal/hepatic impairment, substance use disorder.
sideEffects: Constipation, nausea, dizziness, sedation, dry mouth, pruritus.
adverseEffects: Respiratory depression (dose-related). Physical dependence, tolerance. Severe toxicity in ultra-rapid metabolizers. Antidote: naloxone.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Pain assessment, respiratory status, history of substance use. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor RR (hold if < 12/min), O2 sat, LOC. Bowel function. Constipation management. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING Avoid alcohol. Do not drive. Constipation is expected — use stool softeners. Do not increase dose without provider guidance.

name: colchicine
uses: Prevention, acute gouty arthritis. Used to reduce frequency of recurrence of familial Mediterranean fever (FMF)4 yrs and older.
action: Disrupts cytoskeletal functions by preventing activation, degranulation, and migration of neutrophils associated with gout symptoms. In FMF, may interfere with intracellular assembly of inflamma-some complex present in neutrophils and monocytes. Result: Reduces inflammatory process.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to colchicine. Concomitant use of a P-glycoprotein (e.g., cycloSPORINE) or strong CYP3A4 inhibitor (e.g., clarithromycin) in presence of renal or hepatic impairment. Mitigare: Pts with both renal/hepatic impairment. Caution: Hepatic impairment, elderly, debilitated patients, renal impairment. Caution: Concomitant use of cycloSPORINE, dilTIAZem, verapamil, fibrates, statins may increase risk of myopathy.
sideEffects: Nausea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, anorexia, hypersensitivity reaction, including angioedema.
adverseEffects: Bone marrow depression (aplastic anemia, agranulocytosis, thrombocytopenia) may occur with long-term therapy. Overdose initially causes burning feeling in skin/throat. Severe diarrhea, abdominal pain. Second stage manifests as fever, seizures, delirium, renal impairment (hematuria, oliguria).
nursingConsiderations: INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Discontinue medication immediately if GI symptoms occur. Encourage high fluid intake (3,000 mL/day). Monitor I&O (output should be at least 2,000 mL/day), CBC, hepatic/renal function tests. Monitor serum uric acid. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Drink 8–10 (8-oz) glasses of fluid daily while taking medication. - Rep.

name: copanlisib
uses: Adults with relapsed follicular lymphoma who have received at least two prior systemic therapies.
action: Inhibits phosphatidylinositol-3-kinase (PI3K) expressed on malignant B-cells. Inhibits signaling pathway of B-cell receptors, lymphoma cells lines, and CXCR12-mediated chemotaxis of malignant B-cells. Result: Inhibits tumor cell growth and metastasis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to copanlisib. Caution: Baseline cytopenias. Caution: active infection, conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds). Caution: history of diabetes, hypertension, pulmonary disease. Caution: Concomitant use of moderate CYP3A inhibitors.
sideEffects: Fatigue, asthenia, diarrhea, rash, stomatitis, oropharyngeal erosion, oral pain, vomiting.
adverseEffects: Anemia, leukopenia, lymphopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia are expected responses to therapy. Serious infections including bacterial/fungal/pneumococcal/viral pneumonia, bronchopulmonary aspergillosis, lung infection reported in 21% of patients. Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia reported in < 1% of patients. Hyperglycemia reported 54% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain ANC, CBC, vital signs. Screen for active infection. Obtain pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Question current breastfeeding status. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor ANC, CBC, platelet count periodically. Monitor blood glucose level prior to each treatment; BP before and after each treatment. Be alert for infections, especially lower respiratory tract infectio.

name: crizotinib
uses: Non–small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC): metastatic NSCLC that is anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) positive or is ROS-1 positive. Anaplastic large cell lymphoma (ALCL): ALCL systemic ALK-positive, relapsed or refractory in patients 1–21 yrs of age. Inflammatory myofibro-blastic tumor (IMT): adult and pediatric patients 1 yr of age and older with unresectable, recurrent, or refractory IMT that is ALK-positive.
action: Inhibits receptor tyrosine kinases, including anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK), hepatocyte growth factor receptors (HGFR, c-Met), recepteur d’origine nantais (RON). ALK gene abnormalities due to mutation may result in expression of oncogenic fusion proteins. Result: Inhibits tumor cell proliferation of cells expressing genetic alteration.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to crizotinib. Caution: Baseline hepatic impairment, congenital long QT interval syndrome. Caution: Pregnancy (avoid use). Caution: Concomitant use of CYP3A4 inducers/inhibitors, medications known to cause bradycardia, renal impairment.

name: cyclobenzaprine
uses: Short term (2–3 wks) muscle spasm associated with acute, painful musculoskeletal conditions.
action: Centrally acting skeletal muscle relaxant that reduces tonic somatic muscle activity at level of brainstem. Influences both alpha and gamma motor neurons. Result: Relieves local skeletal muscle spasm.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to cyclobenzaprine. Acute recovery phase of MI, arrhythmias, HF, heart block, conduction disturbances, hyperthyroidism, use within 14 days of MAOIs. Caution: Hepatic impairment, history of urinary hesitancy or retention, angle-closure glaucoma, increased intraocular pressure (IOP), elderly.
sideEffects: Drowsiness, dry mouth, dizziness, fatigue, asthenia, blurred vision, headache, anxiety.
adverseEffects: Overdose may cause visual hallucinations, hyperactive reflexes, muscle rigidity, vomiting, hyperpyrexia.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Record onset, type, location, duration of muscular spasm. Check for immobility, stiffness, swelling. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Assist with ambulation. Assess for therapeutic response: Relief of pain; decreased stiffness, swelling; increased joint mobility; reduced joint tenderness; improved grip strength. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Avoid tasks that require alertness, motor skills until response to drug is established. - Drowsiness usually diminishes with continued therapy. - Avoid alcohol, other depressants while taking medication. - Avoid sudden changes in posture. - Sugarless gum, sips of water may relieve dry mouth.

name: cycloPHOSphamide
uses: Acute lymphocytic, acute nonlymphocytic, chronic myelocytic, chronic lymphocytic leukemias. Ovarian, breast carcinomas. Neuroblastoma. Retinoblastoma. Hodgkin’s, non-Hodgkin’s lymphomas.
action: Inhibits DNA, RNA protein synthesis by cross-linking with DNA, RNA strands. Cell cycle–phase nonspecific. Result: Prevents cell growth.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to cycloPHOSphamide. Urinary outflow obstruction. Caution: Severe leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, tumor infiltration of bone marrow, previous therapy with other antineoplastic agents, radiation, renal/hepatic/cardiac impairment, active UTI.
sideEffects: Marked leukopenia 8–15 days after initiation, nausea, vomiting (beginning about 6 hrs after administration and lasting about 4 hrs), alopecia, diarrhea, darkening of skin/fingernails, stomatitis, headache.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (leukopenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia, hypoprothrom-binemia) is an expected response to therapy. Expect leukopenia to resolve in 17–28 days. Anemia generally occurs after large doses or prolonged therapy. Thrombocytopenia may occur 10– 15 days after drug initiation.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC wkly during therapy or until maintenance dose is established, then at 2-to 3-wk intervals. Question history of urinary outlet flow obstruction, hepatic/renal impairment, active infections. Obtain pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, serum BUN, creatinine, electrolytes, urine output. Monitor WBC counts closely during initial therapy. Monitor for hematologic toxicity (fever, sore throat, signs of local infection, unusual bruising/bleeding from any site), symptoms of anemia (excessive fatigue, weakness). Recovery from marked leukopenia due to myelosuppression can be expected in 17–28 days.

name: cytarabine
uses: Conventional: Remission induction (in combination with other chemotherapeutic agents) in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) in blast phase, prophylaxis and meningeal leukemia.
action: Inhibits DNA polymerase. Cell cycle–specific for S phase of cell division. Result: Inhibits DNA synthesis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to cytarabine. Liposomal: Active meningeal infection. Caution: Renal/hepatic impairment, prior drug-induced bone marrow suppression.
sideEffects: IV: Asthenia, fever, pain, altered taste/smell, nausea, vomiting (risk greater with IV push than with continuous IV infusion). Intrathecal: Headache, asthenia, confusion.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (leukopenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia, megaloblastosis, reticulocytopenia), occurring minimally after single IV dose. Leukopenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia should be expected with daily or continuous IV therapy. Cytarabine syndrome (fever, myalgia, rash, conjunctivitis, malaise, chest pain), hyperuricemia may occur. High-dose therapy may produce severe CNS, GI, pulmonary toxicity.
nursingConsiderations: INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BMP, LFT; serum uric acid. Monitor CBC for myelosuppression. Monitor for blood dyscrasias (fever, sore throat, signs of local infection, unusual bruising/bleeding from any site), symptoms of anemia (excessive fatigue, weakness). Monitor for signs.

name: dabigatran
uses: Nonvalvular atrial fibrillation: Indicated to reduce risk of stroke, systemic embolism in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation. Deep venous thrombosis (DVT and pulmonary embolism [PE]) treatment and PREVENTION: deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) in patients who have been treated with a parenteral anticoagulant for at least 5 days and to reduce risk of recurrence of DVT and PE in previously treated pediatric patients aged 3 mos to 11 yrs (oral pellets), pediatric patients ag.

Prevents thrombin-mediated effects, including cleavage of fibrinogen to fibrin; activation of factors V, VIII, XI, and XIII; and inhibition of thrombin-induced platelet aggregation. Result: Inhibits coagulation.
precautions: Contraindicated: Severe hypersensitivity to dabigatran. Active major bleeding, patients with mechanical prosthetic heart valves. Caution: Renal impairment (CrCl 15–30 mL/min), moderate hepatic impairment, invasive procedures, spinal anesthesia, major surgery, patients with congenital or acquired bleeding disorders, elderly, concurrent use of medications that increase risk of bleeding, valvular heart disease.

adverseEffects: Severe, sometimes fatal, hemorrhagic events, including intracranial hemorrhage, hemorrhagic stroke, Gl bleeding, may occur. Hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, reported in < 1% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC. Question history of mechanical heart valve, recent surgery; hepatic, renal impairment; recent spinal, epidural procedures; recent hemorrhagic events (intracranial hemorrhage, hemorrhagic stroke, GI/GU bleeding). Receive full medication history and screen for interactions. Screen for active bleeding. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Obtain aPTT, platelet count if bleeding occurs. Assess for any signs of bleeding (hematuria, melena, bleeding from gums, petechiae, bruising), hematoma, hypotension, tachycardia, abdominal pain. Question for increase in discharge during menses. Use care when removing adhesives, tape.

name: dabrafenib
uses: Melanoma (Unresectable or Metastatic): unresectable or metastatic melanoma with BRAF V600E mutation (single-agent therapy) or in patients with BRAF V600E or V600K mutations (in combination with trametinib). Melanoma (Adjuvant): Adjuvant melanoma (in combination with trametinib) in patients with a BRAF V600E or BRAF V600K mutation, and lymph node involvement. adverseEffects: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cuSCC) and keratoacanthomas reported in 7% of patients (especially elderly, prior skin cancer, chronic sun exposure). Skin reactions including palmar-plantar eryhrodysesthesia syndrome (PPES), papilloma have occurred. May increase cell proliferation of wild-type BRAF melanoma or new malignant melanomas. Eye conditions including uveitis, iritis reported.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain BMP, blood glucose level; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Confirm BRAF V600 mutation status. Make note of current moles, lesions for future comparison. Conduct ophthalmologic exam, visual acuity. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor serum electrolytes; serum blood glucose periodically (especially in. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s with diabetes). Obtain CBC if hemolytic anemia suspected in.

name: dacomitinib
uses: First-line metastatic non–small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with EGFR exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R substitution mutations.
action: Irreversibly inhibits kinase activity of human EGFR family and certain EGFR mutations. Result: Inhibits tumor cell growth and metastasis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to dacomitinib. Caution: Baseline cytopenias. Caution: dehydration, diabetes, hepatic impairment. Caution: history of pulmonary disease.
sideEffects: Diarrhea, rash, paronychia, stomatitis, decreased appetite, dry skin, xerosis, decreased weight.

Nail reactions including nail infection, nail toxicity, onychoclasis, onycholysis, onychomadesis, paronychia reported in 64% of patients. CTCAE Grade 3 or 4 skin reactions occurred in 21% of patients. Upper respiratory tract infection reported in 12% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain ANC, CBC, LFT; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Question current breastfeeding status. Confirm compliance of effective contraception. Question history of hepatic impairment, pulmonary disease. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, LFT as clinically indicated. Consider ABG, radiologic test if ILD/pneumonitis (excessive cough, dyspnea, hypoxia) is suspected. Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. Antidiarrheal medication may be needed to manage diarrhea.

name: dalfampridine
uses: Indicated to improve ambulation in adults with multiple sclerosis (MS).
action: Improves conduction in demyelinated axons by delaying repolarization and prolonging duration of action potentials. Result: Strengthens skeletal muscle fiber twitch activity; improves peripheral motor neurologic function.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to dalfampridine. History of seizures, moderate to severe renal impairment (CrCl equal to or < 50 mL/min). Caution: Mild renal impairment (CrCl equal to 51–80 mL/min).
sideEffects: Insomnia, dizziness, headache, nausea, asthenia, back pain, paresthesia, nasopharyngitis.
adverseEffects: Seizures may occur at recommended doses and in patients without history of seizures. Severe hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, may occur. Urinary tract infection reported in 12% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain BUN, serum creatinine, creatinine clearance. Question history of seizure disorder, renal impairment. Assess motor function, gait, ability to ambulate. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor creatinine clearance. Monitor for urinary, respiratory infection. Assess for therapeutic response (improvement in walking as demonstrated by increase in walking speed). Monitor for hypersensitivity reactions, seizure-like activity (confusion, muscle twitching/jerking, nystagmus, loss of bladder/bowel control). PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Avoid tasks that require alertness, motor skills until response to drug is established. - Seizures can occur at prescribed doses.

name: dalteparin
uses: Prophylaxis: ischemic complications of unstable angina and non– Q-wave myocardial infarction (MI). Prophylaxis: deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in abdominal surgery, hip replacement surgery, or medical patients with severely restricted mobility during acute illness. Extended symptomatic venous thromboembolism (VTE) to reduce recurrence in adults with cancer (begin with the initial VTE treatment and continue for 6 mos). Symptomatic VTE to reduce recurrence in patients 1 mos and old.
action: Antithrombin in presence of low molecular weight heparin inhibits factor Xa, thrombin. Result: Produces anticoagulation.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to dalteparin, heparin, pork products, active major bleeding, concurrent heparin therapy, unstable angina (and others). Caution: Conditions with increased risk for hemorrhage, bacterial endocarditis, renal/hepatic impairment, uncontrolled hypertension, history of recent GI ulceration/hemorrhage, peptic ulcer d.
sideEffects: Hematoma at injection site, hypersensitivity reaction (chills, fever, pruritus, urticaria, asthma, rhinitis, lacrimation.
adverseEffects: Overdose may lead to bleeding complications ranging from local ecchymoses to major hemorrhage. Thrombocytopenia occurs rarely.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, aPTT, PT/INR; vital signs. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Periodically monitor CBC, stool for occult blood (no need for daily monitoring in. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Usual length of therapy is 5–10 days. - Do not take any OTC medication (especially aspirin) without consulting physician. - Report bleeding, bruising, dizziness, light-headedness, rash, itching, fever, swelling, breathing difficulty. - Rotate injection sites daily.

name: dantrolene
uses: PO: spasticity associated with upper motor neuron disorder (e.g., spinal cord injuries, CVA, cerebral palsy, multiple sclerosis). Parenteral: malignant hyperthermia.
action: Interferes with release of calcium from sarcoplasmic reticulum of skeletal muscle. Prevents/reduces the increase in myoplasmic calcium ion concentration. Result: Dissociates excitation-contraction coupling.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to dantrolene. IV: None. PO: When spasticity used to maintain posture/balance during locomotion or to obtain increased motor function. Active hepatic disease. Caution: Cardiac/pulmonary impairment, history of hepatic disease.
sideEffects: Drowsiness, dizziness, weakness, general malaise, diarrhea (mild). Confusion, diarrhea (severe), headache, insomnia.
adverseEffects: Risk of hepatotoxicity, most notably in females, patients taking other hepatotoxic medications concurrently. Overt hepatitis noted most frequently between 3rd and 12th mo of therapy. Overdose results in vomiting, muscular hypotonia, muscle twitching, respiratory depression, seizures.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain LFT. Record onset, type, location, duration of muscular spasm. Check for immobility, stiffness, swelling. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Assist with ambulation. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Drowsiness usually diminishes with continued therapy. - Avoid tasks that require alertness, motor skills until response to drug is established. - Avoid alcohol/other depressants. - Report continued weakness, fatigue, nausea, diarrhea, skin rash, itching, bloody/tarry stools.

name: dapagliflozin
uses: Adjunct for diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. To reduce risk of hospitalization for HF in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and either established cardiovascular disease or multiple cardiovascular risk factors. To reduce risk of cardiovascular death, hospitalization for HF, and urgent HF visits in adults with HF. To reduce the risk of sustained eGFR decline, end-stage kidney disease, cardiovascular death, and hospitalization for HF.
action: Inhibits SGLT2 in proximal renal tubule, reducing reabsorption of filtered glucose from tubular lumen and lowering renal threshold for glucose. Reduces reabsorption of sodium and increases delivery of sodium to the distal tubule. Result: Increases urinary excretion of glucose; lowers serum glucose levels.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to dapagliflozin; patients who are being treated for glycemic control without established cardiovascular disease or multiple cardiovascular risk factors with severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min); ESRD requiring dialysis. Caution: Concomitant use of loop diuretics, other hypoglycemic agents (e.g., insulin, insulin secretagogues), baseline systolic hypotension, renal impairment, hypovolemia/dehydration, recent genital mycotic infection. Caution: patients at risk for.
sideEffects: Back pain, increased urination, nausea, constipation, extremity pain, discomfort with urination.
adverseEffects: Symptomatic hypotension (orthostatic hypotension, postural dizziness, syncope) may occur, especially in patients who are elderly, use concomitant loop diuretics, or have baseline systolic hypotension. Intravascular volume depletion/contraction may cause acute kidney injury requiring dialysis. Fatal cases of ketoacidosis were reported. Hypoglycemic events were reported in patients using concomitant insulin, insulin secretagogues.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain BUN, serum creatinine, eGFR, CrCl, blood glucose level, Hgb A1c; BP. Assess hydration status. Correct volume depletion prior to initiation. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BUN, serum creatinine, eGFR, CrCl, blood glucose level, Hgb A1c; BP periodically. Monitor for ketoacidosis (e.g., dehydration, confusion, extreme thirst, sweet-smelling breath, Kussmaul respir. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s’s understanding of diabetes management, routine home glucose monitoring. Obtain dietary consult for nutritional education. Question history of renal impairment, type 1 diabetes, ketoacidosis.

name: daratumumab
uses: Multiple myeloma (relapsed/refractory): Monotherapy for the patients with multiple myeloma who have received at least three prior lines of therapy including a proteasome inhibitor and an immunomodulatory agent or who are double-refractory to a proteasome inhibitor and an immunomodulatory agent. action: Binds to cell surface glycoprotein CD38 on CD38-expressing tumor cells (highly expressed on myeloma cells). Inhibits tumor cell proliferation and induces apoptosis. Result: Inhibits tumor cell growth.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to daratumumab. Caution: Obstructive pulmonary disorders (e.g., COPD, emphysema), baseline cytopenias, herpes zoster infection, elderly.

name: daratumumab/hyaluronidase fihj
uses: Adults with multiple myeloma: In combination with bortezomib, melphalan, and prednisone in newly diagnosed patients who are ineligible for autologous stem cell transplant. In combination with lenalidomide and dexamethasone in newly diagnosed patients who are ineligible for autologous stem cell transplant and in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who have received at least one prior therapy. In combination with bortezomib and dexamethasone in patients who have received at least one pr.
action: Daratumumab binds to cell surface glycoprotein CD38 on CD38-expressing tumor cells (highly expressed on myeloma cells). Inhibits tumor cell proliferation and induces apoptosis. Result: Inhibits tumor cell growth and survival.

Caution: Baseline cytopenias, active infection, obstructive pulmonary disorders (e.g., COPD, emphysema), herpes zoster infection, elderly. Caution: conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, immunocompromised patients, renal failure, open wounds). Caution: history of hepatitis B infection.
sideEffects: Note: Frequency and occurrence of side effects may vary based on treatment as monotherapy or in combination with other therapies, diarrhea, fatigue, pyrexia, back pain, injection site reaction, peripheral edema, arthralgia.

Myelosuppression (anemia, leukopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia) has occurred. Grade 3 and 4 neutropenia was reported, especially in patients with lower body weights. Severe systemic reactions including bronchospasm, dyspnea, hypertension, hypoxia, tachycardia wheezing reported in 10% of patients.

Inform blood bank of treatment and possible treatment-related interference with serologic testing. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s with COPD, inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators should be considered during the first 4 treatment doses.

name: darbepoetin alfa
uses: Anemia associated with chronic renal failure (including patients on dialysis and patients not on dialysis), anemia caused by concurrent myelosuppressive chemotherapy in patients planned to receive chemotherapy for minimum of 2 additional months. Anemia of prematurity.
action: Stimulates division and differentiation of committed erythroid progenitor cells; induces release of reticulocytes from bone marrow into bloodstream. Result: Induces erythropoiesis.

name: denosumab

name: desmopressin
