uses: Short-term severe cardiac decompensation (heart failure, cardiogenic shock) to increase cardiac output.
action: Directly stimulates beta-1 adrenergic receptors in the myocardium, increasing contractility and cardiac output with minimal effect on heart rate and blood pressure (unlike dopamine).
precautions: Caution: atrial fibrillation (increases AV conduction — ventricular rate may increase), hypertension, recent MI, hypovolemia.
sideEffects: Increased heart rate, hypertension or hypotension, ventricular ectopy, headache, nausea.
adverseEffects: Ventricular arrhythmias (including VT). Myocardial ischemia. Tolerance with prolonged use (>72 hrs). Hypersensitivity reactions.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Hemodynamic monitoring. Correct hypovolemia. Continuous ECG and BP monitoring required. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Titrate to target cardiac output/BP. Monitor HR, BP, urine output. Continuous ECG for arrhythmias. NOT for resuscitation — does not increase diastolic BP like dopamine. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING ICU medication — administered only in monitored settings.

name: dofetilide
uses: Maintenance of normal sinus rhythm (NSR) in patients with chronic atrial fibrillation/atrial flutter of longer than 1-wk duration who have been converted to NSR. Conversion of atrial fibrillation/flutter to NSR.
action: Prolongs repolarization without affecting conduction velocity by blocking one or more time-dependent potassium currents. No effect on sodium channels, alpha-adrenergic, beta-adrenergic receptors. Result: Terminates reentrant tachyarrhythmias, preventing reinduction.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to dofetilide. Congenital or acquired prolonged QT syndrome (do not use if baseline QT interval or QTc is > 440 msec), severe renal impairment, concurrent use of drugs that may prolong QT interval, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, concurrent use with bictegravir, verapamil, dolutegravir, itraconazole, ketoconazole, prochlorperazine, megestrol, cimetidine, hydroCHLOROthiazide, trimethoprim. Severe renal impairment (CrCl < 20 mL/min).
sideEffects: Headache, chest pain, dizziness, dyspnea, nausea, insomnia, back/abdominal pain, diarrhea.
adverseEffects: Serious ventricular arrhythmias, including torsades de pointes, may occur. Usually within the first 3 days of therapy.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain serum electrolyte levels (especially potassium, magnesium). Prior to initiating treatment, QTc intervals must be determined. Do not use if heart rate < 50 beats/min. Provide continuous ECG monitoring, calculation of creatinine clearance, equipment for resuscitation available for minimum of 3 days. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Assess for conversion of cardiac arrhythmias and absence of new arrhythmias. Constantly monitor ECG. Provide emotional support. Monitor renal function for electrolyte imbalance (prolonged or excessive diarrhea, sweating, vomiting, thirst).

name: dolutegravir
uses: In combination with other antiretroviral agents for the HIV-1 infection in adults (treatment naive or experienced) and pediatric patients (treatment naive or experienced but integrase strand transfer inhibitor [INSTI] naive) at least 4 wks of age and weighing at least 3 kg.
action: Inhibits HIV integrase by blocking strand transfer of retroviral DNA integration (essential for HIV replication cycle). Result: Interferes with HIV replication, slowing progression of HIV infection.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to dolutegravir. Co-administration of dofetilide. Caution: Diabetes, hepatic/renal impairment, history of hepatitis or tuberculosis, prior hypersensitivity reaction to INSTIs.
sideEffects: Insomnia, headache, nausea.
adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity reaction including rash, fever, angioedema, difficulty breathing, skin blistering/peeling, arthralgia, lethargy was reported. Pts co-infected with hepatitis B or C have increased risk for viral reactivation, worsening of hepatic function, and may experience hepatic decompensation and/or failure if therapy is discontinued. May cause redistribution/accumulation of body fat (lipodystrophy). May induce immune recovery syndrome (inflammatory response to dormant opportunistic infectio.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, CMP, CD4+ count, viral load, HIV-1 RNA level; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CD4+ count, viral load, HIV-1 RNA level for treatment effectiveness. Monitor LFT; assess for hepatic injury (bruising, hematuria, jaundice, right upper abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, weight loss). If discontinuation of drug regimen occurs, monitor hepatic function for viral reactivation. Initiate anti-HBV therapy if warranted. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s for hepatitis B or C coinfection. Receive full medication history including herbal products. Offer emotional support.

name: donepezil
uses: Mild, moderate, or severe dementia of Alzheimer’s disease.
action: Reversibly inhibits enzyme acetylcholinesterase, increasing concentration of acetylcholine at cholinergic synapses, enhancing cholinergic function in CNS. Result: Slows progression of Alzheimer’s disease.
precautions: Contraindicated: History of hypersensitivity to donepezil, other piperidine derivatives. Caution: Asthma, COPD, bradycardia, bladder outflow obstruction, history of ulcer disease, those taking concurrent NSAIDs, supraventricular cardiac conduction disturbances (e.g., sick sinus syndrome. Caution: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome), seizure disorder.
sideEffects: Nausea, diarrhea, headache, insomnia, nonspecific pain, dizziness, mild muscle cramps, fatigue.
adverseEffects: Overdose may result in cholinergic crisis (severe nausea, increased salivation, diaphoresis, bradycardia, hypotension, flushed skin, abdominal pain, respiratory depression, seizures, cardiorespiratory collapse). Increasing muscle weakness may occur, resulting in death if muscles of respiration become involved. Antidote: Atropine sulfate 1–2 mg IV with subsequent doses based on therapeutic response.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess cognitive function (e.g., memory, attention, reasoning). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor behavior, mood/cognitive function, activities of daily living. Monitor for cholinergic reaction (GI discomfort/cramping, feeling of facial warmth, excessive salivation/diaphoresis), lacrimation, pallor, urinary urgency, dizziness. Monitor for nausea, diarrhea, headache, insomnia. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Report nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, diaphoresis, increased salivary secretions, severe abdominal pain, dizziness. -.

name: dopamine
uses: Hemodynamic instability: cardiogenic shock, septic shock, refractory heart failure with hypotension. Acute renal failure (low-dose — limited evidence).
action: Dose-dependent receptor actions: Low dose (1–5 mcg/kg/min): D1/D2 dopaminergic — renal/mesenteric vasodilation. Moderate (5–10 mcg/kg/min): beta-1 adrenergic — positive inotropy, increases HR.
precautions: Caution: hypovolemia (correct before use), peripheral vascular disease, extravasation risk.
sideEffects: Tachycardia, headache, nausea, vomiting, dysrhythmias, vasoconstriction at high doses.
adverseEffects: Severe hypertension. Ventricular arrhythmias. Tissue necrosis/gangrene on extravasation (treat with phentolamine). Peripheral ischemia.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Correct hypovolemia before starting. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Continuous ECG, BP (arterial line preferred), HR monitoring. Monitor urine output hourly. Assess IV site frequently for extravasation (pallor, pain, blanching). Titrate per protocol. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING ICU medication — report any burning or pain at IV site immediately.

name: dostarlimab-gxly
uses: Endometrial Cancer (EC): Treatment in combination with carboplatin and paclitaxel, followed by dostarlimab, as a single agent of adults with primary advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer that is mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) OR as a single agent with dMMR recurrent or advanced endometrial cancer that has progressed following prior treatment with a platinum-containing regimen in any setting and who are not candidates for curative surgery or radiation. Mismatch Repair Deficient Recurrent or.
action: Inhibits programmed cell death-1 (PD-1) activity by binding to the PD-1 receptor on T-cells to block PD-1 ligands (PD-L1 and PD-L2) from binding. Blocking the PD-1 pathway inhibits the negative immune regulation caused by PD-1 receptor signaling. Result: Restores immune responses (including T-cell antitumor function), causing decreased tumor growth and proliferation.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to dostarlimab-gxly. Caution: Baseline cytopenias, conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds), diabetes, patients at risk for interstitial lung disease (e.g., COPD, sarcoidosis, connective disease disease). Caution: history of autoimmune disorders (Crohn’s disease, demyelinating polyneuropathy. Caution: Guillain-Barré syndrome. Caution: Hashimoto’s thyroiditis, hyperthyroidism, myasthenia gravis, rheumatoid arthritis.
sideEffects: Fatigue, asthenia, nausea, diarrhea, constipation, vomiting, decreased appetite, cough.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (anemia, leukopenia, lymphopenia) is an expected response to therapy. May cause severe and/or fatal immune-mediated adverse reactions including acute kidney injury, nephritis. Colitis, hepatitis, pancreatitis, pneumonitis. Adrenal insufficiency, hypoparathyroidism, hyperthyroidism, hypophysitis, thyroiditis, Type I diabetes mellitus including ketoacidosis.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BMP, LFT, thyroid panel; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Confirm compliance of effective contraception. Verify presence of dMMR in tumor specimens. Screen for history of autoimmune disorders, diabetes, pituitary/pulmonary/thyroid disease. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor ANC, CBC for myelosuppression; creatinine clearance, LFT, thyroid periodically.

name: doxazosin
uses: Cardura: mild to moderate hypertension. Used alone or in combination with other antihypertensives. Urinary outflow obstruction and/or obstruction and irritation associated with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). Cardura XL: urinary outflow obstruction and/or obstruction and irritation associated with benign prostatic hyperplasia. Dysfunctional voiding, bladder neck obstruction.
action: Hypertension: Selectively blocks alpha1-adrenergic receptors, decreasing peripheral vascular resistance. BPH: Inhibits postsynaptic alpha-adrenergic receptors in prostatic stromal and bladder neck tissues. Result: Hypertension: Causes peripheral vasodilation, lowering BP.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to doxazosin or other quinazolines (prazosin, terazosin). Caution: Constipation, ileus, GI obstruction, hepatic impairment.
sideEffects: Dizziness, asthenia, headache, edema, nausea, pharyngitis, rhinitis, pain in extremities.
adverseEffects: First-dose syncope (hypotension with sudden loss of consciousness) may occur 30–90 min after initial dose of 2 mg or greater, too-rapid increase in dosage, addition of another antihypertensive agent to therapy. First-dose syncope may be preceded by tachycardia (pulse rate 120–160 beats/min).
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Give first dose at bedtime. If initial dose is given during daytime,. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BP, I&O. Monitor pulse diligently (first-dose syncope may be preceded by tachycardia). Assess for edema, headache. Assist with ambulation if dizziness, light-headedness occurs. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Full therapeutic effect may not occur for 3–4 wks. - May cause syncope (fainting); go from lying to standing slowly. - Avoid tasks that require alertness, motor skills until response to drug is established.

name: doxepin
uses: Depression including psychotic and bipolar depression. Silenor (only): insomnia in patients with difficulty staying asleep. Topical: pruritus associated with atopic dermatitis.
action: Increases synaptic concentrations of norepinephrine, serotonin by inhibiting reuptake. Result: Produces antidepressant, anxiolytic effects.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to doxepin. Glaucoma, hypersensitivity to other tricyclic antidepressants, urinary retention, use of MAOIs within 14 days. Caution: Cardiac/hepatic/renal disease, patients at risk for suicidal ideation, respiratory compromise, sleep apnea, history of bowel obstruction, increased IOP, glaucoma, history of seizures, history of urinary retention/obstruction, hyperthyroidism, prostatic hypertrophy, hiatal hernia, elderly.
sideEffects: PO: Orthostatic hypotension, drowsiness, dry mouth, headache, increased appetite, weight gain, nausea, unusual fatigue.
adverseEffects: Abrupt or too-rapid withdrawal may result in headache, malaise, nausea, vomiting, vivid dreams. Overdose may produce confusion, severe drowsiness, agitation, tachycardia, arrhythmias, shortness of breath, vomiting.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess BP, pulse, ECG (those with history of cardiovascular disease). Obtain CBC, serum electrolyte tests before long-term therapy. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BP, pulse, weight. Perform CBC, serum electrolyte tests periodically to assess renal/hepatic function. Monitor mental status, suicidal ideation. Supervise suicidal-risk. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s’s appearance, behavior, level of interest, mood, suicidal ideation, sleep pattern.

name: doxorubicin
uses: Breast cancer, bladder cancer, ovarian cancer, acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, sarcomas.
action: Intercalates into DNA double helix and inhibits topoisomerase II, preventing DNA replication and transcription. Generates free radicals causing DNA strand breaks.
precautions: Caution: cardiotoxicity risk (cumulative lifetime dose limit: 550 mg/m²), vesicant (severe tissue damage on extravasation).
sideEffects: Myelosuppression (nadir day 10–14), alopecia, nausea/vomiting, mucositis, red urine (harmless), fatigue.
adverseEffects: Cardiotoxicity: cardiomyopathy and irreversible heart failure (cumulative dose-related). Extravasation causes severe tissue necrosis — treat with dexrazoxane. Secondary leukemia (rare, long-term). Severe myelosuppression.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, LFT, ECG, LVEF (ECHO/MUGA scan). Calculate cumulative lifetime dose. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC for nadir (days 10–14). Cardiac monitoring (LVEF). IV site vigilance — vesicant: extravasation causes severe necrosis (have dexrazoxane kit available). Monitor for mucositis. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING Urine may appear red for 1–2 days — normal (not blood). Expect hair loss — temporary. Use contraception during and after treatment. Report fever, unusual bleeding, chest pain, shortness of breath.

name: doxycycline
brand: Acticlate, Adoxa, Apo-Doxy , Avidoxy, Doryx, Doxy-100, Oracea, Vibramycin
uses: Susceptible infections due to H. Ducreyi, Pasteurella pestis, P. Tularensis, Bacteroides spp., V. Cholerae, Brucella spp., Rickettsiae, Y. Pestis, Francisella tularensis, M. Pneumoniae, including acne, acute intestinal amebiasis, Clostridium, malaria (prophylaxis), Mycoplasma pneumoniae, respiratory tract infections, rickettsial infections, sexually transmitted infections. (Oracea): inflammatory lesions in adults with rosacea.
action: Inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding to ribosomes. May cause alterations in the cytoplasmic membrane. Result: Bacteriostatic.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to doxycycline, other tetracyclines. Caution: History or predisposition to oral candidiasis (Oracea). Caution: recent Clostridium difficile infection or antibiotic-associated colitis. Caution: history of pancreatitis. Caution: Avoid use during pregnancy, during tooth development in children.
sideEffects: Decreased appetite, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dysphagia, photosensitivity (may be severe). Rash, urticaria.
adverseEffects: Superinfection (especially fungal), benign intracranial hypertension (headache, visual changes) may occur. Hepatotoxicity, fatty degeneration of liver, pancreatitis occur rarely.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Question for history of allergies, especially to tetracyclines, sulfites. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. Assess skin for rash. Be alert for superinfection: fever, vomiting, diarrhea, anal/genital pruritus, oral mucosal changes (ulceration, pain, erythema). PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Avoid unnecessary exposure to sunlight. - Do not take with antacids, iron products. - Complete full course of therapy. - After application of dental gel, avoid brushing teeth, flossing the treated areas for 7 days. - Report severe diarrhea. - May cause nausea, vomiting. If GI upset occurs, may take with small amount food; however, Or.

name: dulaglutide
uses: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults and patients 10 yrs of age and older with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Reduce risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus who have established cardiovascular disease or multiple cardiovascular risk factors.
action: Activates GLP-1 receptors in pancreatic beta cells. Improves glycemic control. Result: Augments glucose-dependent insulin release, slows gastric emptying.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to dulaglutide, other GLP-1 receptor agonists. Personal/family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or multiple endocrine neoplasia syndrome type 2. Caution: Pts with increased serum calcitonin, thyroid nodules, hx pancreatitis, renal/hepatic impairment. Caution: Not recommended in patients with severe GI disease, diabetic ketoacidosis, or type 1 diabetes.
sideEffects: Nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, abdominal pain, decreased appetite, dyspepsia, fatigue, asthenia.
adverseEffects: May increase risk of acute renal failure or worsening of chronic renal impairment (especially with dehydration), severe gastroparesis, pancreatitis, thyroid C-cell tumors. May increase risk of hypoglycemia when used with other hypoglycemic agents or insulin. Dyspnea, pruritus, rash may indicate hypersensitivity reaction. May prolong PR interval by 2–3 msec or may rarely cause first-degree AV block, tachycardia.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain fasting glucose level, Hgb A1c, BMP. Question history of medullary thyroid carcinoma, multiple endocrine neoplasia syndrome type 2, pancreatitis, renal impairment; first-degree AV block, PR interval prolongation. Receive full medication history and screen for use of other hypoglycemic agents or insulin. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor capillary blood glucose levels, Hgb A1c; renal function test in. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s’s understanding of diabetes management, routine home glucose monitoring, medication self-administration. Assess hydration status.

name: duloxetine
uses: Major depressive disorder. Generalized anxiety disorder. Diabetic peripheral neuropathic pain. Fibromyalgia. Chronic musculoskeletal pain.
action: Inhibits reuptake of both serotonin (5-HT) and norepinephrine (NE) at presynaptic terminals, enhancing monoaminergic neurotransmission. Analgesic effect via descending pain inhibitory pathways.
precautions: Caution: suicidal ideation, hepatic impairment, hypertension, seizures, alcohol use (hepatotoxicity risk), abrupt discontinuation (discontinuation syndrome).
sideEffects: Nausea (most common), dry mouth, constipation, dizziness, fatigue, hyperhidrosis, sexual dysfunction, increased BP.
adverseEffects: Suicidal ideation (black box — < 25 yrs). Serotonin syndrome. Hepatotoxicity. Hyponatremia.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess mood, suicide risk, hepatic function, BP. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor mood, suicidal ideation. BP monitoring. LFT in at-risk. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING Do NOT stop abruptly — taper required. Full effect takes 4–6 weeks. Avoid alcohol (hepatotoxicity). Report worsening depression or suicidal thoughts.

name: dupilumab
uses: Atopic Dermatitis: moderate to severe atopic dermatitis in adults and pediatric whose disease is not adequately controlled with topical prescription therapies or when those therapies are not advisable. May be used with or without corticosteroids. Asthma: Add-on maintenance moderate to severe asthma with an eosinophilic pheno-type or corticosteroid-dependent asthma. Chronic Rhinosinusitis With Nasal Polyposis: Add-on.
action: Binds to the IL-4Ra subunit inhibiting inter-leukin-4 (IL-4) and interleukin-13 (IL-13), signaling cytokine-induced responses, including release of proinflammatory cytokines. Mechanism of action in asthma not established. Result: Reduces skin inflammation.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to dupilumab. Caution: History of herpes simplex infection, parasitic (helminth) infection. Caution: Avoid use of live vaccines.
sideEffects: Occasional, injection site reactions, eye inflammation/irritation, rare, eye pruritus, dry eye.
adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity reactions including serum sickness (arthralgia, itching, glomerulonephritis, hypotension, lymphadenopathy, malaise, proteinuria, pyrexia, rash, shock, splenomegaly), urticaria reported in < 1% of patients, which correlated with high antibody titers. Blepharitis, conjunctivitis (allergic, bacterial, giant papillary, viral), keratitis (ulcerative, allergic, atopic kera-toconjunctivitis), herpes simplex infection (genital, otitis externa, herpes virus infection) may occur.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Question history of herpes zoster infection, parasitic infection, hypersensitivity reaction. Question recent administration of live virus vaccine. Pts with preexisting helminth (parasite) infection should be treated prior to first dose. Inhaled or systemic corticosteroids should not be suddenly discontinued upon initiation. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Interrupt or discontinue treatment if hypersensitivity reaction, opportunistic infection (especially parasite i. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s’s willingness to self-inject medication.

name: durvalumab
uses: Non–small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC): unresectable stage III NSCLC that has not progressed following concurrent platinum-based chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Adults with metastatic NSCLC with no sensitizing epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations or anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) genomic tumor aberrations (in combination with tremelimumab-acti and platinum-based chemotherapy). Extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC): First-line adult.
action: Blocks programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1) binding to PD-1 and CD80 (B7.1). PD-L1 blockade increases T-cell activation allowing T- cells to kill tumor cells. Result: Inhibits tumor cell growth and metastasis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to durvalumab. Caution: Active infection, conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, immunocompromised patients, renal failure, open wounds). Caution: corticosteroid intolerance, baseline hematologic cytopenias, elderly patients, hepatic impairment, interstitial lung disease, renal insufficiency. Caution: history of autoimmune disorders (Crohn’s disease, demyelinating polyneuropathy. Caution: Guillain-Barré syndrome.
sideEffects: Fatigue, asthenia, malaise, back/musculoskeletal/neck pain, myalgia, constipation, decreased appetite, nausea.
adverseEffects: Anemia, neutropenia, lymphopenia are expected responses to therapy. May cause severe, sometimes fatal immune-mediated reactions such as adrenal insufficiency (1% of patients), colitis (2% of patients), hepatitis (1% of patients), hypothyroidism (9% of patients), hyperthyroidism (6% of patients), hypophysitis, nephritis (< 1% of patients), pneumonitis (2% of patients), type 1 diabetes (< 1% of patients), rash (15% of patients). Aseptic meningitis, hemolytic anemia, keratitis, myocarditis, myositis, thrombocytopenic purpura, .
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BMP, LFT, thyroid function test; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential; vital signs. Question medical history as listed in Precautions; prior infusion reactions. Question intolerance to corticosteroids. Screen for active infection. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, BMP, LFT, serum ionized calcium, magnesium; thyroid function test periodically. Monitor for infusion reactions including angioedema, back or neck pain, dyspnea, flushing, pruritus, pyrexia, rash, syncope. Consider increasing corticosteroid dose if toxic effects worsen or do.

name: duvelisib
uses: Relapsed or refractory chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) or small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) after at least two prior therapies.
action: Inhibits phosphatidylinositol-3-ki-nase (PI3K) expressed on malignant B-cells. Inhibits signaling pathway of B-cell receptors, lymphoma cells lines, and CXCR12-mediated chemotaxis of malignant B cells. Result: Inhibits tumor cell growth and metastasis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to duvelisib. Caution: Baseline anemia, leukopenia, lymphopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia. Caution: active infection, conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds), dehydration, hepatic impairment, history of pulmonary disease. Caution: Concomitant use of strong CYP3A inducers or CYP3A inhibitors.
sideEffects: Diarrhea, rash, fatigue, pyrexia, cough, nausea, musculoskeletal pain, abdominal pain.
adverseEffects: Anemia, leukopenia, lymphopenia, lympho-cytosis, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia are expected responses to therapy. Serious infections including pneumonia, bronchopul-monary aspergillosis, sepsis, lung infection reported in 31% of patients. Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia reported in < 1% of patients. CMV infection/reactivation or viremia reported in 1% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain ANC, CBC, LFTs; pregnancy test in female. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor ANC, CBC, LFT periodically. If blood dyscrasias occurs, monitor ANC, CBC wkly until i. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s of reproductive potential. Screen for active infection. Recommend prophylaxis therapy for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia during treatment and until absolute CD4+ T cell count is > 200 cells/mm3. To prevent CMV infection, recommend prophylactic antiviral therapy during treatment.

name: elacestrant
uses: Postmenopausal women or adult men with estrogen receptor (ER)–positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)–negative, estrogen receptor 1 gene (ESR1)–mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer with disease progression following at least one line of endocrine therapy.
action: Binds to estrogen receptor (ER)-alpha. In ER-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)–negative breast cancer cells, inhibits 17-beta estradiol–mediated cell proliferation via proteasomal pathway. Result: Inhibits tumor cell growth.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to elacestrant. Caution: Mild to moderate hepatic impairment, dyslipidemia. Caution: Not recommended in patients with severe hepatic impairment. Caution: Avoid concomitant use of strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers.
sideEffects: Musculoskeletal pain, nausea, fatigue, vomiting, decreased appetite, diarrhea, constipation, headache.
adverseEffects: Dyslipidemia reported in 27–30% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, LFT, lipid profile. Educate compliance of effective contraception in males with female partners of reproductive potential. Verify presence of ESR1 mutation in plasma specimen. Question history hepatic impairment, dyslipidemia. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor LFT in. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Take with food to reduce vomit.

name: elbasvir/grazoprevir
uses: Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotype 1 or 4 infection in adults and patients 12 yrs of age and older or weighing at least 30 kg.
action: Elbasvir inhibits hepatitis C virus (HCV) NS5A protein, which is essential for viral RNA replication and virion assembly. Grazoprevir inhibits HCV NS3/4A protease needed for processing HCV-encoded polyproteins, which is essential for viral replication. Result: Inhibits viral replication of hepatitis C virus.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to elbasvir or grazoprevir, decompensated hepatic cirrhosis, moderate or severe hepatic impairment; concomitant use of organic anion transporting polypeptides 1B1/3 (OATP1B1/3) inhibitors, strong CYP3A inducers. Concomitant use of atazanavir, carBAMazepine, cycloSPORINE, darunavir, efavirenz, lopinavir, phenytoin, rifAMPin, saquinavir, St. John’s wort, tipranavir. Any contraindications or hypersensitivity to ribavirin (if used with treatment regimen). Cautions.
sideEffects: Fatigue, headache, diarrhea, nausea, insomnia, dyspnea, rash, pruritus.
adverseEffects: Serum ALT elevation up to 5 times ULN reported in 1% of patients. Serum bilirubin elevation > 2.5 times ULN occurred in 6% of patients. Serum ALT elevation occurred more frequently in the elderly, female patients, and patients of Asian ancestry.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, LFT, HCV-RNA level; pregnancy test in female. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Obtain LFT at wk 8, then as clinically indicated. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s of reproductive potential. Confirm hepatitis C genotype.

name: eletriptan
uses: Acute migraine headache with or without aura.
action: Selective agonist for serotonin in cranial arteries; causes vasoconstriction and reduces inflammation. Result: Relieves migraine headache.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to eletriptan. Arrhythmias associated with conduction disorders, cerebrovascular syndrome including strokes and transient ischemic attacks (TIAs), coronary artery disease, hemiplegic or basilar migraine, ischemic heart disease, peripheral vascular disease including ischemic bowel disease, severe hepatic impairment, uncontrolled hypertension; use within 24 hrs of treatment with another 5-HT1 agonist, an ergotamine-containing or ergot-type medication such as dih.
sideEffects: Dizziness, drowsiness, asthenia, nausea, paresthesia, headache, dry mouth, warm or hot sensation.
adverseEffects: Cardiac reactions (ischemia, coronary artery vasospasm, MI), noncardiac vaso-spasm-related reactions (hemorrhage, CVA) occur rarely, particularly in patients with hypertension, obesity, diabetes, strong family history of coronary artery disease. Males older than 40 yrs. Postmenopausal women. May cause GI ischemia, bowel infarction, non-cardiac-related vasospasms including peripheral vascular ischemia, Raynaud’s syndrome.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Question characteristics of migraine headaches (onset, location, duration, possible precipitating symptoms). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Evaluate for relief of migraine headaches (photophobia, phonophobia, nausea, vomiting, pain, dizziness, fogginess). Monitor for cardiac arrhythmia, coronary events, hypertension, hypersensitivity reaction. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Take a single dose as soon as symptoms of an actual migraine attack appear. - Medication is intended to relieve migraine - headaches, not to prevent or reduce number of attacks. - Avoid tasks that require alertness, mo.

name: elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor
pharmacoClass: Cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulator
uses: Cystic fibrosis (CF) in patients aged 2 yrs and older who have at least one F508del mutation in the CFTR gene.
action: Mutations in the CFTR gene (encodes the CFTR protein) are the cause of cystic fibrosis. The Phe508del mutation (most common CFTR mutation) causes abnormal CFTR trafficking, reducing the quantity of CFTR protein at the cell surface and disrupting channel gating. Result: Improves lung/orga.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to elexacaftor, tezacaftor, ivacaftor. Caution: Moderate hepatic impairment, concomitant use of CYP3A inhibitors. Caution: Avoid use of concomitant strong CYP3A inducers. Caution: Not recommended in severe hepatic impairment.
sideEffects: Headache, abdominal pain, diarrhea, rash, nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, rhinitis, flatulence.
adverseEffects: Elevated transaminases may occur. Worsening of hepatic function was reported in patients with baseline hepatic impairment. Cataracts were reported in pediatric patients taking ivacaftor. Infections including upper respiratory tract infection (16% of patients), influenza (7% of patients), sinusitis (5% of patients), conjunctivitis, pharyngitis, tonsillitis, UTI were reported.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain LFT. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor LFT q3mos for 12 mos, then annually thereafter (or more frequently in. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s’s genotype is unknown, a CF mutation test should be obtained to confirm presence of at least one F508del mutation.

name: elotuzumab
uses: Multiple myeloma (in combination with lenalidomide and dexAMETHasone) in patients who have received one to three prior therapies or (in combination with pomalidomide and dexAMETHasone) in patients who have received at least two prior therapies including lenalidomide and a protea-some inhibitor.
action: Binds to and specifically targets signaling lymphocytic activation molecule family member 7 (SLAMF7), a protein that is expressed on most myeloma and natural killer cells. Directly activates natural killer cells and facilitates cellular death. Result: Inhibits tumor cell growth and metastasis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to elotuzumab. Caution: Diabetes, baseline cytopenias, hypertension. Caution: history of chronic opportunistic infections (especially viral infections, fungal infections), conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, kidney failure, open wounds). Caution: Concomitant use of medications known to cause bradycardia (e.g., antiarrhythmics, beta blockers, calcium channel blockers). Caution: Concomitant use of live vaccines not recommended during treatment and up to 3 mos after discontinu.

name: empagliflozin
uses: Adjunct for diet and exercise to improve glycemic controls with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Reduce risk of cardiovascular death in patients with type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Reduce risk of cardiovascular death and hospitalization for adults with HF. Reduce risk of sustained decline in eGFR, end-stage kidney disease, cardiovascular death, and hospitalization in adults with chronic kidney disease at risk of progression.
action: Inhibits SGLT2 in proximal renal tubule, reducing reabsorption of filtered glucose from tubular lumen and lowering renal threshold for glucose. Reduces reabsorption of sodium and increases delivery of sodium to the distal tubule. Result: Increases urinary excretion of glucose; lowers serum glucose levels.
precautions: Contraindicated: History of hypersensitivity to empagliflozin, other SGLT2 inhibitors, severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min), end-stage renal disease, dialysis. Caution: Concomitant use of loop diuretics, other hypoglycemic agents (e.g., insulin, insulin secretagogues), baseline systolic hypotension, renal impairment, hypovolemia/dehydration, recent genital mycotic infection. Caution: patients at risk for diabetic ketoacidosis (insulin dose reduction, acute febrile illness, reduced calorie int.
sideEffects: Increased urination, dyslipidemia, arthralgia, nausea.
adverseEffects: Symptomatic hypotension (orthostatic hypotension, postural dizziness, syncope) may occur, especially in patients who are elderly, use concomitant loop diuretics, or have baseline systolic hypotension. Intravascular volume depletion/contraction may cause acute kidney injury requiring dialysis. Fatal cases of ketoacidosis were reported. Hypoglycemic events were reported in patients using concomitant insulin, insulin secretagogues.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain BUN, serum creatinine, eGFR, CrCl, blood glucose level, Hgb A1c; BP. Assess hydration status. Correct volume depletion prior to initiation. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BUN, serum creatinine, eGFR, CrCl, blood glucose level, Hgb A1c; BP periodically. Monitor for ketoacidosis (e.g., dehydration, confusion,. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s’s understanding of diabetes management, routine home glucose monitoring. Obtain dietary consult for nutritional education. Question history of renal impairment, type 1 diabetes, ketoacidosis.

name: emtricitabine
uses: Used in combination with at least two other antiretroviral agents for HIV-1 infection.
action: Emtricitabine is phosphorylated intracellularly to emtricitabine 5’-triphosphate, which interferes with HIV viral RNA-dependent DNA polymerase. Result: Impairs HIV replication, slowing progression of HIV infection.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to emtricitabine. Caution: Renal impairment. Caution: history of hepatitis, hepatic impairment.
sideEffects: Headache, rhinitis, rash, diarrhea, nausea, cough, vomiting, abdominal pain.
adverseEffects: Fatal cases of lactic acidosis, severe hepatomegaly with steatosis have occurred. A majority of cases occurred in women. If therapy is discontinued, patients co-infected with hepatitis B virus have an increased risk for viral replication, worsening of hepatic function, and may experience hepatic decompensation and/or failure. May induce immune reconstitution syndrome (inflammatory response to dormant opportunistic infections such as Mycobacterium avium, cytomegalovirus, PCP, tuberculosis, or accelera.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT CD4+ count, viral load, HIV-1 RNA level; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CD4+ count, viral load, HIV-1 RNA level for treatment effectiveness. An increase of serum creatinine > 0.4 mg/dL from. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s for HBV infection. Offer emotional support. Question history of hepatic disease.

name: enalapril
uses: Hypertension alone or in combination with other antihypertensives. Adjunct for symptomatic HF with reduced ejection fraction.
action: Suppresses renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (prevents conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II, a potent vasoconstrictor; may inhibit angiotensin II at local vascular, renal sites). Decreases plasma angiotensin II, increases plasma renin activity, decreases aldosterone secretion. Result: In hypertension, reduces peripheral arterial resistance.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to enalapril. History of angioedema from previous treatment with ACE inhibitors. Idiopathic/hereditary angioedema. Concomitant use of aliskiren in patients with diabetes. Coadministration with or within 36 hrs of switching to or from a neprilysin inhibitor (e.g., sacubitril). Caution: Renal impairment, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with outflow tract obstruction. Caution: severe aortic stenosis. Caution: before, during, or immediately after major surgery. Caution: Concomitant use of potassium.
sideEffects: Headache, dizziness, orthostatic hypotension, fatigue, diarrhea, cough, syncope, angina.
adverseEffects: Excessive hypotension (“first-dose syncope”) may occur in patients with HF, severe salt or volume depletion. Angioedema (facial, lip swelling), hyperkalemia occur rarely. Agranulocytosis, neutropenia may be noted in patients with renal impairment, collagen vascular diseases (scleroderma, systemic lupus erythematosus). Nephrotic syndrome may be noted in those with history of renal disease.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain BUN, serum creatinine, CrCL. Receive full medication history, especially potassium-sparing diuretics. Obtain BP immediately before each dose (be alert to fluctuations). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Assist with ambulation if dizziness occurs. Monitor BP. Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - To reduce hypotensive effect, go from lying to standing slowly. - Several wks may be needed for full therapeutic effect of B.

name: enasidenib
uses: Adults with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with an isocitrate dehydrogenase-2 (IDH2) mutation.
action: Inhibits isocitrate dehydrogenase-2 (IDH2) enzymes on mutant IDH2 variants, decreasing 2-hydroxyglu-tarate (2-HG) levels and restoring myeloid differentiation. Inhibits tumor growth and proliferation. Result: Reduces blast counts; increases percentage of myeloid cells.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to enasidenib. Caution: Hepatic/renal impairment, dehydration. Caution: patients at high risk for tumor lysis syndrome (high tumor burden), conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds).
sideEffects: Nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, decreased appetite, dysgeusia.
adverseEffects: Life-threatening differentiation syndrome (bone pain, dyspnea, fever, lymphadenopathy, peripheral edema, plural/pericar-dial etfusion, pulmonary infiltrates, rapid weight gain, respiratory distress. Hepatic/renal/multiorgan dysfunction) reported in 14% of patients. May occur 10 days to 5 mos after initiation. Noninfectious leukocytosis reported in 12% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain WBC; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Verify presence of IDH2 mutations in the blood or bone marrow. Screen for active infection. Confirm compliance of effective contraception. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor WBC for leukocytosis; BMP, serum calcium, phosphate, uric acid for tumor lysis syndrome (acute renal failure, electrolyte imbalance, cardiac arrhythmias, seizures) q2wks for the first 3 mos. Monitor LFT for transa-minitis, hepatotoxicity periodically. If differentiation syndrome is suspected, con.

name: encorafenib
uses: Patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a BRAF V600E or V600K mutation (in combination with binimetinib). Metastatic colorectal cancer (CRC) in adults with a BRAF V600E mutation (in combination with cetuximab) after prior therapy. Adults with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with a BRAF V600E mutation (in combination with binimetinib).
action: An ATP-competitive inhibitor of protein kinase BRAF, which suppresses the MAPK pathway. Result: Inhibits tumor cell growth.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to encorafenib. Caution: Baseline cytopenias. Caution: active infection. Caution: conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds), diabetes, hepatic/renal impairment. Caution: patients at risk for QTc interval prolongation (congenital long QT syndrome, HF, mediations that prolong QTc interval, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia).
sideEffects: Fatigue, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, arthralgia, hyperkeratosis, myopathy, rash.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (anemia, leukopenia, lymphopenia, neutropenia) is an expected response to therapy. In patients receiving combination therapy, new primary cutaneous malignancies including cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (including keratoacan-Stoma) (3% of patients), basal cell carcinoma (2% of patients) have occurred. In patients receiving single-agent therapy, new primary cutaneous malignancies including cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (including keratoacan-thoma) (8% of patients), basal cell carcinoma (1% of patients), .
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BMP, LFT; pregnancy test in female. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s of reproductive potential. Confirm compliance of effective nonhormonal contraception. Correct hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia prior to and during treatment. Confirm presence of BRAF V600E or V600K mutation in tumor specimen.

name: enfortumab vedotin-ejfv
uses: As a single agent for adults with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma who have previously received a programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) or programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) inhibitor and a platinum-containing chemotherapy or are ineligible for cisplatin-containing chemotherapy and have previously received one or more prior lines of therapy. In combination with pembrolizumab for the adults with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer who are not.
action: Binds to and internalizes Nectin-4 antibody conjugated to a microtubule-dis-rupting agent, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE). MMAE binds to and disrupts cellular microtubule network, causing cell cycle arrest and apoptosis (cellular death). Result: Inhibits tumor cell growth.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to enfortumab vedotin-ejfv. Caution: Baseline cytopenias, diabetes, patients at risk for hyperglycemia (e.g., diabetes, chronic use of corticosteroids). Caution: conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds). Caution: dermatologic disease. Caution: history of herpes zoster infection.
sideEffects: Fatigue, asthenia, decreased appetite, nausea, dysgeusia, diarrhea, dry eye, eye irritation.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (anemia, leukopenia, lymphopenia, neutropenia) is an expected response to therapy. Fatal cases of hyperglycemia, diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) were reported in patients regardless of history of diabetes. Grade 3 or 4 hyperglycemia was reported in 8% of patients, and more prevalent in patients with higher body mass index and in patients with elevated hemoglobin A1c. Peripheral neuropathy including hypoesthesia, gait disturbance, muscular weakness, paresthesia, peripheral motor/sensorimotor neuropathy.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain weight in kilograms. Obtain CBC, LFT, blood glucose level, pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Verify compliance of effective contraception in females and males with female partners of reproductive potential. Obtain visual acuity. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, LFT, blood glucose levels periodically. Monitor for hyperglycemia (blurred vision, confusion, excessive thirst, Kussmaul respirations, polyuria); new onset or worsening peripheral ne.

name: enoxaparin
uses: Prophylaxis: deep vein thrombosis (DVT): DVT prophylaxis following hip or knee replacement surgery, abdominal surgery, or patients with severely restricted mobility during acute illness. Unstable angina and non–Q-wave myocardial infarction: Prophylaxis: ischemic complications of unstable angina and non–Q-wave MI when administered with aspirin.
action: Enhances the inhibition rate of clotting proteases by antithrombin III. Impairs normal hemostasis and inhibition of factor Xa. Result: Produces anticoagulation.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to enoxaparin. Active major bleeding, concurrent heparin therapy, hypersensitivity to heparin, pork products. History of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) in past 100 days or in the presence of circulating antibodies. Caution: Conditions with increased risk of hemorrhage, platelet defects, renal impairment (renal failure), elderly, uncontrolled arterial hypertension, history of recent GI ulceration or hemorrhage. Caution: When neur-axial anesthesia (epidural or s.
sideEffects: Injection site hematoma, nausea, peripheral edema.
adverseEffects: May lead to bleeding complications ranging from local ecchymoses to major hemorrhage. May cause heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT). Antidote: IV injection of protamine sulfate (1% solution) equal to dose of enoxaparin injected. 1 mg protamine sulfate neutralizes 1 mg enoxaparin. One additional dose of 0.5 mg protamine sulfate per 1 mg enoxaparin may be given if aPTT tested 2–4 hrs after first injection remains prolonged.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC. Note platelet count. Question medical history as listed in Precautions. Ensure that. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Periodically monitor CBC, stool for occult blood (no need for daily monitoring in. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s has not received spinal anesthesia, spinal procedures. Assess for active bleeding.

name: entrectinib
uses: Non–small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC): adults with metastatic non–small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors are ROS1 positive. Solid tumors: adult and pediatric patients (1 mo and older) with solid tumors that have a neurotrophic receptor tyrosine kinase (NTRK) gene fusion without a known acquired resistance mutation. Are metastatic or where surgical resection is likely to result in severe morbidity. Or have no satisfactory alternative treatment or that have progressed follow.
action: Inhibits activation of tropomyosin receptor kinase (TRK) proteins encoded by NTRK gene fusions. Inhibits proto-oncogenic tyro-sine-protein kinase ROS1 and anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK). Result: Inhibits tumor cell proliferation.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to entrectinib. Caution: Baseline cytopenias, hepatic impairment, cardiac disease (cardiomyopathy, HF), conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, immunocompromised patients, renal failure, open wounds), patients at risk for bone fractures (e.g., fall risk, osteoporosis, chronic use of corticosteroids), patients at risk for QTc interval prolongation, cardiac arrhythmias (congenital long QT syndrome, HF, concomitant use of QT interval-prolonging medications, hypok.
sideEffects: Fatigue, asthenia, constipation, dysgeusia, edema (facial, generalized, localized, peripheral).
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (anemia, lymphopenia, neutropenia) is an expected response to therapy. HF reported in 3% of patients. Median onset of HF was approx. 2 mos. Myocarditis in the absence of HF reported in < 1% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, LFT, uric acid level; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Verify use of effective contraception in females of reproductive potential. Confirm presence of NTRK gene fusion or ROS1 rearrangements in tumor specimen. Assess risk of QT interval prolongation, fractures, falls. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, uric acid level periodically. Monitor LFT for hepa.

name: enzalutamide
uses: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC). Metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC). Nonmetastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (nmCSPC) with biochemical recurrence (BCR) at high risk for metastasis.
action: Inhibits androgen binding to androgen receptors in target tissue, and inhibits interaction with DNA. Result: Decreases proliferation, induces cell death of prostate cancer cells.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to enzalutamide. Women who are pregnant or may become pregnant (not indicated in female population). Caution: History of seizure disorder, underlying brain injury with loss of consciousness, transient ischemic attack within past 12 mos, CVA, brain metastases, brain arteriove-nous abnormality, ischemic heart disease. Caution: patients at risk for fractures (e.g., osteoporosis, osteopenia), falls. Caution: conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocom.
sideEffects: Asthenia, back pain, diarrhea, arthralgia, hot flashes, peripheral edema, musculoskeletal pain, headache.
adverseEffects: Upper respiratory tract infection occurs in 11% of patients. Lower respiratory tract and lung infection (includes pneumonia, bronchitis) occur in slightly less (9% of patients). Spinal cord compression and cauda equina syndrome occur in 7% of patients. Life-threatening ischemic heart disease reported in 3% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain LFT. Assess risk for falls/fractures. Screen for active infection. Question history of seizures, ischemic heart disease, cerebrovascular disease. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor LFT periodically. Monitor BP for hypertension. Obtain echocardiogram if ischemic heart disease (dyspnea, edema, exercise intolerance, palpitations) is suspected. Monitor for hypersensitivity reactions, seizure activity.

name: epcoritamab-bysp
uses: Adults with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), not otherwise specified, including DLBCL arising from indolent lymphoma, and high-grade B-cell lymphoma after two or more lines of systemic therapy.
action: Binds to CD3 receptor expressed on surface of T cells and CD20 expressed on surface of lymphoma cells. Result: Activates T cells causing release of proinflammatory cytokines and induces lysis of B cells.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to epcoritamab-bysp. Caution: Baseline cytopenias, dehydration, conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds). Caution: Avoid administration of live vaccines.
sideEffects: Fatigue, asthenia, lethargy, musculoskeletal pain, injection site reactions (erythema, inflammation, pain, pruritus.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (anemia, leukopenia, lymphopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia) is an expected response to therapy, but more severe reactions including bone marrow depression, febrile neutropenia may occur. Life-threatening CRS reported in 51% of patients. Symptoms of CRS may include fatigue, headache, hypotension, hypoxia, nausea, pyrexia, tachycardia. Serious events may include acute respiratory distress syndrome, atrial fibrillation, capillary leak syndrome, disseminated intravascular coagulatio.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BMP, LFT, pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Confirm compliance with effective contraception. Administer in an environment equipped to manage symptoms of CRS, neurological toxicities. Pts should be hospitalized for at least 24 hrs following the first 48 mg dose. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC for myelosuppression (bleeding, bruisin. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s per administration guidelines. Recommend prophylaxis therapy for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, herpes virus prior to initiation.

name: epinephrine
pharmacoClass: Endogenous catecholamine; alpha and beta adrenergic agonist
clinicalClass: Vasopressor, bronchodilator, cardiac stimulant, anaphylaxis antidote
uses: Anaphylaxis (first-line — IM injection). Cardiac arrest (asystole, VF, PEA — ACLS). Bronchospasm (severe asthma). Adjunct to local anesthetics (vasoconstriction to prolong effect).
action: Stimulates alpha-1 (vasoconstriction), beta-1 (increased HR and contractility), and beta-2 (bronchodilation) adrenergic receptors. Reverses bronchoconstriction, restores vascular tone, and increases cardiac output.
precautions: Caution: cardiovascular disease, hypertension, hyperthyroidism, diabetes, pregnancy. Caution: For anaphylaxis — no absolute contraindications (life-threatening emergency). Caution: For elective use: narrow-angle glaucoma, pheochromocytoma.
sideEffects: Palpitations, tachycardia, tremor, anxiety, headache, pallor, hypertension.
adverseEffects: Severe hypertension, ventricular arrhythmias, pulmonary edema, cerebrovascular hemorrhage. Tissue necrosis on extravasation.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT For anaphylaxis: immediate IM injection in outer mid-thigh (EpiPen). Obtain vitals, O2 sat. Call 911/emergency response. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BP, HR, cardiac rhythm, RR continuously. IV infusion: use dedicated line, titrate carefully. Monitor for recurrent anaphylaxis (observe for 4–8 hrs). PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING (EpiPen users): Carry 2 EpiPens at all times. Inject into outer thigh (through clothing if necessary). Go to ER immediately after use. Wear medical alert bracelet.

name: eplerenone
uses: Hypertension alone or in combination with other antihypertensive agents. Improve survival of patients with symptomatic heart failure (HF) with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) after an acute myocardial infarction (AMI).
action: Binds to mineralocorticoid receptors in kidney, heart, blood vessels, brain, blocking binding of aldosterone. Prevents myocardial and vascular fibrosis. Result: Reduces BP.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to eplerenone. Concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole), CrCl < 30 mL/min, serum potassium level > 5.5 mEq/L at initiation. Use in patients with Addison’s disease. Hypertension (additional): Type 2 diabetes with microalbuminuria, CrCl < 50 mL/min, serum creatinine > 2 mg/dL in men, > 1.8 mg/dL in women (and others).
sideEffects: Dizziness, diarrhea, cough, fatigue, flu-like symptoms, abdominal pain.
adverseEffects: Hyperkalemia may occur, particularly in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and microalbuminuria.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain serum potassium level. Obtain BP, apical pulse immediately before each dose, in addition to regular monitoring (be alert to fluctuations). If excessive reduction in BP occurs, place. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor serum potassium. Assist with ambulation if dizziness occurs. Assess BP for hypertension/hypotension. Assess for evidence of flu-like symptoms. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Avoid tasks that require alertness, motor skills until response to drug is established (possible dizziness effect). - Hypertension requires lifelong control. - Avoid exercising during hot weather (risk of dehydration, hypoten.

name: epoetin alfa
uses: Anemia due to chronic kidney disease (CKD): anemia due to CKD, including patients on dialysis and not on dialysis, to decrease the need for red blood cell (RBC) transfusion. Anemia due to zidovudine in patients with HIV infection: Administered at ≤ 4, 200 mg/wk in patients with HIV infection with endogenous serum erythropoietin levels of ≤ 500 units/mL. Anemia due to chemotherapy in patients with cancer: Pts with nonmyeloid malignancies where anemia is due to the.
action: Stimulates division, differentiation of erythroid progenitor cells in bone marrow. Result: Induces erythropoiesis, releases reticulocytes from bone marrow into blood, where they mature into erythrocytes.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to epoetin. Pure red cell aplasia that begins after treatment, uncontrolled hypertension. Caution: History of seizures or controlled hypertension. Caution: Cancer patients: Tumor growth, shortened survival may occur when Hgb levels of 11 g/dL or greater are achieved with epoetin alfa. Caution: Chronic renal failure patients: Increased risk for serious cardiovascular reactions (e.g., stroke, MI) when Hgb levels > 11 g/dL are achieved with epoetin alfa.
sideEffects: ### Pts Receiving Chemotherapy Fever, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, edema, asthenia, shortness of breath, paresthesia.
adverseEffects: Hypertensive encephalopathy, thrombosis, cerebrovascular accident, MI, seizures occur rarely. Hyperkalemia occurs occasionally in patients with chronic renal failure, usually in those who do not comply with medication regimen, dietary guidelines, frequency of dialysis regimen.
