name: erdafitinib
uses: Adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma that has susceptible FGFR3 or FGFR2 genetic mutation alterations and progressed during or following at least one line of prior platinum-containing chemotherapy including within 12 mos of neoadjuvant or adjuvant platinum-containing chemotherapy.
action: Binds to and inhibits fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) enzyme activity. Decreases FGFR-related signaling and cell viability. Result: Inhibits tumor cell growth and metastasis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to erdafitinib. Caution: Baseline hemoglobinemia, neutropenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia. Caution: conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds), hepatic/renal impairment, optic disorders, patients at risk for hyperphosphatemia (hypoparathyroidism, concomitant use of phosphorus-containing medications, chronic kidney disease), CYP2C9 poor metabolizers (patients with CYP2C9*3/*3 genotype). Caution: concomitant use of CYP3A inhi.
sideEffects: Stomatitis, fatigue, asthenia, lethargy, malaise, diarrhea, dry mouth, onycholysis.
adverseEffects: Hemoglobinemia, leukopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia are expected responses to therapy. Ocular toxicities including serious retinopathy/retinal pigment epithelial detachment reported in 25% of patients. Ocular disorders including keratitis, foreign body sensation, corneal erosion reported in 28% of patients. Grade 3 serious retinopathy/retinal pigment epithelial detachment reported in 3% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BMP, LFT, pregnancy test in female. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, BMP, LFT, serum ionized calcium periodically. Obtain serum phosphate level 14–21 days after initiation. Restrict phosphorus intake to 600–800 mg daily. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s of reproductive potential. Confirm presence of susceptible FGFR genetic alterations in tumor specimens. Verify compliance of effective contraception in female.

name: erlotinib
pharmacoClass: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) inhibitor; tyrosine kinase inhibitor
uses: Locally advanced or metastatic non–small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after failure of at least one prior chemotherapy regimen (as monotherapy). First-line locally advanced, unresectable, or metastatic pancreatic cancer (in combination with gemcitabine).
action: Reversibly inhibits overall epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)–tyrosine kinase activity. Inhibits intracellular phosphorylation. Result: Produces tumor cell death.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to erlotinib. Caution: Severe hepatic/renal impairment, cardiovascular disease. Caution: Concurrent use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers or CYP1A2 inhibitors, patients at risk for GI perforation (e.g., peptic ulcer disease, diverticular disease), conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds).
sideEffects: Rash, diarrhea, decreased appetite, fatigue, cough, dyspnea, pyrexia, nausea.
adverseEffects: Severe, life-threatening pneumonitis, ILD, respiratory failure reported in 9% of patients. Life-threatening hepatorenal syndrome reported in < 1% of patients. Fatal cases of GI perforation. Blistering, and exfoliative skin reactions, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BMP, LFT; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Confirm compliance of effective contraception. Question history of CVA, optic disorders, pulmonary disease, hepatic/renal impairment, GI perforation. Screen for active infection. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, LFT, renal function periodically. An increase of serum creatinine > 0.4 mg/dL from.

name: ertapenem
uses: S. Aureus (methicillin-susceptible only), S. Agalactiae, S. Pneumoniae (penicillin-susceptible only), S. Pyogenes, E. Coli, H. Influenzae (beta-lactamase negative strains only), K. Pneumoniae, M. Catarrhalis, Bacteroides spp., C. Clostridioforme, Peptostreptococcus spp., including moderate to severe intra-abdominal, skin/skin structure infections. Community-acquired pneumonia. Complicated UTI. Acute pelvic infection. Adult diabetic foot infections without osteomyelitis.
action: Penetrates bacterial cell wall of microorganisms, binds to penicillin-binding proteins, inhibiting cell wall synthesis. Result: Produces bacterial cell death.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ertapenem. History of anaphylactic hypersensitivity to beta-lactams (e.g., imipenem, meropenem), hypersensitivity to amide-type local anesthetics (e.g., lidocaine) (IM use only). Caution: Hypersensitivity to penicillins, cephalosporins, renal impairment, CNS disorders (brain lesions or history of seizure disorder), elderly.
sideEffects: Diarrhea, nausea, headache, altered mental status, insomnia, rash, abdominal pain, constipation.
adverseEffects: Antibiotic-associated colitis, other superinfections (abdominal cramps, severe watery diarrhea, fever) may result from altered bacterial balance in GI tract. Anaphylactic reactions have been reported. Seizures may occur in patients with CNS disorders (brain lesions, history of seizures), bacterial meningitis, severe renal impairment.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Question for history of allergies, particularly to beta-lactams, penicillins, cephalosporins. Inquire about history of seizures. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor WBC count. Monitor renal/hepatic function. Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. Monitor for nausea, vomiting. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Report tremors, seizures, rash, prolonged diarrhea, chest pain, other new symptoms.

name: erythromycin
brand: Akne-Mycin, EES, Erybid , Eryc, EryDerm, EryPed, Ery-Tab, Erythrocin
uses: Susceptible infections due to S. Pyogenes, S. Pneumoniae, S. Aureus, M. Pneumoniae, Legionella, Chlamydia, other susceptable bacterial infections including infections of upper and lower respiratory tract, non-gonococcal urethritis, Lyme disease, diphtheria, pertussis, gastroenteritis, syphillis. Surgical prophylaxis. Topical: acne vulgaris. Ophthalmic: gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum, superficial ocular infections.
action: Penetrates bacterial cell membranes, reversibly binds to bacterial ribosomes, inhibiting RNA-dependent protein synthesis. Result: Bacteriostatic.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to erythromycin. Concomitant administration with ergot derivatives, lovastatin, pimozide, simvastatin. Caution: Elderly, myasthenia gravis, strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, hepatic impairment, patients with prolonged QT intervals, uncorrected hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia, concurrent use of class IA or III antiarrhythmics.
sideEffects: IV: Abdominal cramping/discomfort, phlebitis/thrombophlebitis, topical: Dry skin, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, rash, urticaria.
adverseEffects: Antibiotic-associated colitis, other superinfections (abdominal cramps, severe watery diarrhea, fever), reversible cholestatic hepatitis may occur. High dosage in patients with renal impairment may lead to reversible hearing loss. Anaphylaxis occurs rarely. Ventricular arrhythmias, prolonged QT interval occur rarely with IV form.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Question for history of allergies (particularly erythromycins), hepatitis. Receive full medication history and screen for interactions. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. Assess skin for rash. Assess for hepatotoxicity (malaise, fever, abdominal pain, GI disturbances). Be alert for superinfection: fever, vomiting, diarrhea, anal/genital pruritus, oral mucosal changes (ulceration, pain, erythema). PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Continue therapy for full length of treatment. - Doses should be evenly spaced. - Take medicati.

name: escitalopram
uses: Major depressive disorder12–17 yrs of age. Generalized anxiety disorder (GAD). G., autism), vasomotor symptoms associated with menopause.
action: Blocks uptake of neurotransmitter serotonin at neuronal presynaptic membranes, increasing its availability at postsynaptic receptor sites. Result: Antidepressant effect.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to escitalopram. Use of MAOI intended to treat psychiatric disorders (concurrent or within 14 days of discontinuing either escitalopram or MAOI). Initiation in patients receiving linezolid or IV methylene blue. Concurrent use with pimozide. Caution: Hepatic/renal impairment, history of seizure disorder, concurrent use of CNS depressants, patients at high risk of suicide, concomitant aspirin, NSAIDs, warfarin (may potentiate bleeding risk), elderly, metabolic disease.
sideEffects: Nausea, dry mouth, drowsiness, insomnia, diaphoresis, tremor, diarrhea, abnormal ejaculation.
adverseEffects: May increase risk of suicidal thoughts and behavior in adolescents and young adults. Life-threatening serotonin syndrome may include mental status changes (agitation, hallucinations, delirium, coma), autonomic instability (tachycardia, labile blood pressure, dizziness, sweating, flushing, hyperthermia), neuromuscular symptoms (tremor, rigidity, myoclonus hyperactive reflexes, incoordination). May cause hyponatremia as a result of syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone (SIADH).
nursingConsiderations: INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Supervise suicidal-risk. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Do not stop taking medication or increa.

name: esmolol
uses: Rapid, short-term ventricular rate in supraventricular tachycardia (SVT), atrial fibrillation or flutter. Tachycardia and/or hypertension (especially intraop or postop). Noncompensatory sinus tachycardia.
action: Selectively blocks beta1-adrenergic receptors. Result: Slows sinus heart rate, decreases cardiac output, reducing BP.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to esmolol. Cardiogenic shock, uncompen-sated cardiac failure, second-or third-degree heart block (except in patients with pacemaker), severe sinus bradycardia, sick sinus syndrome, IV administration of calcium blockers in close proximity to esmolol, pulmonary hypertension. Caution: Compensated HF. Caution: concurrent use of digoxin, verapamil, dilTIAZem. Caution: Diabetes, myasthenia gravis, renal impairment, history of anaphylaxis to allergens. Caution: Hypovolemia, hypertension, bronchos.
sideEffects: Generally well tolerated, with transient, mild side effects, hypotension (systolic BP < 90 mm Hg) manifested as dizziness, nausea, diaphoresis, headache, cold extremities.
adverseEffects: Overdose may produce profound hypotension, bradycardia, dizziness, syncope, drowsiness, breathing difficulty, bluish fingernails or palms of hands, seizures. May potentiate insulin-induced hypoglycemia in diabetic patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess BP, apical pulse immediately before drug is administered (if pulse is 60 or less/min or systolic BP is 90 mm Hg or less, withhold medication, contact physician). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BP for hypotension, ECG, heart rate, respiratory rate, development of diaphoresis, dizziness (usually first sign of impending hypotension). Assess pulse for quality, irregular rate, bradycardia, extremities for coldness. Assist with ambulation if dizziness occurs. Assess for nausea, diaphoresis, headache, fatigue.

name: esomeprazole
uses: PO: gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD): Short-term treatment (4–8 wks) of erosive esophagitis. Maintenance healing of erosive esophagitis. Symptomatic gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). Pathological hypersecretory conditions: pathologic hypersecretory conditions, including Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. H. Pylori eradication: Used in triple therapy with amoxicillin and clarithromycin for H. Pylori infection in patients with duodenal ulcer.
action: Inhibits H+/K+-ATPase on surface of gastric parietal cells. Result: Reduces gastric acid secretion.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to esomeprazole, other proton pump inhibitors. Concomitant use with rilpivirine. Caution: May increase risk of hip, wrist, spine fractures. Caution: hepatic impairment. Caution: Asian populations. Caution: Concurrent use of CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifAMPin).
sideEffects: Headache, diarrhea, abdominal pain, nausea, dizziness, asthenia, vomiting, constipation.
adverseEffects: Pancreatitis, hepatotoxicity, interstitial nephritis occur rarely.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess epigastric/abdominal pain. Question history of hepatic impairment, pathologic bone fractures. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Evaluate for therapeutic response (relief of GI symptoms). Question if GI discomfort, nausea, diarrhea occur. Monitor for occult blood, observe for hemorrhage in. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Report headache. - Take at least 1 hr before eating. - If swallowing capsules is difficult, open capsule and mix pellets with 1 tbsp applesauce. Swallow immediately without chewing.

name: estradiol
brand: Alora, Climara, Delestrogen, Depo-Estradiol, Divigel, Dotti, Elestrin, Estrogel, Evamist, Femring, M
uses: Moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms associated with menopause, vulvar and vaginal atrophy associated with menopause, hypoestrogenism (due to castration, hypogonadism, primary ovarian failure), metastatic breast cancer (palliation) in men and postmenopausal women, advanced prostate cancer (palliation), osteoporosis in postmenopausal women.
action: Modulates pituitary secretion of gonado-tropins; follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), luteinizing hormone (LH). Reduces elevated levels of FSH, LH. Result: Promotes normal growth/development of female sex organs.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to estradiol, angioedema, hepatic dysfunction or disease, undiagnosed abnormal vaginal bleeding, active or history of arterial thrombosis, estrogen-dependent cancer (known, suspected, or history of), known or suspected breast cancer (except for patients being treated for metastatic disease), pregnancy, thrombophlebitis or thromboembolic disorders (current or history of), known protein C, protein S, antithrombin deficiency or other known thrombophilic disorder. Caut.
sideEffects: Anorexia, nausea, swelling of breasts, peripheral edema marked by swollen ankles and feet, transdermal: Skin irritation, redness, vomiting (especially with high doses), headache (may be severe).
adverseEffects: Prolonged administration increases risk of gallbladder disease, thromboembolic disease, breast/cervical/vaginal/endometrial/hepatic carcinoma. Cholestatic jaundice occurs rarely.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess frequency/severity of vasomotor symptoms. Question medical history as listed in Precautions. Question for possibility of pregnancy (contraindicated). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BP, weight, serum calcium, glucose, LFT. Monitor for loss of vision, sudden onset of proptosis, diplopia, migraine, thromboembolic disorders. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Limit alcohol, caffeine. - Avoid grapefruit products. - Immediately report sudden headache, vomiting, disturbance of vision/speech, numbness/weakness of extremities, chest pain, calf pain, shortness of breath, severe abdominal pain, mental depression, unusual bleeding. - Avoid smoking. - Report abnormal va.

name: etanercept
uses: Moderate to severely active rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Moderately to severely active polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) in patients 2 yrs or older, ankylosing spondylitis (AS), psoriatic arthritis. Active juvenile psoriatic arthritis (JPsA) in pediatric patients 2 yrs of age and older. Chronic, moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in patients 4 yrs or older.
action: Binds to tumor necrosis factor (TNF), blocking its interaction with cell surface receptors. Elevated levels of TNF, involved in inflammatory processes and the resulting joint pathology of rheumatoid arthritis, JIA, AS, and plaque psoriasis. Result: Relieves symptoms of arthritis, psoriasis, spondylitis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to etanercept. Serious active infection or sepsis. Caution: History of recurrent infections, conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds). Caution: History of HF, decreased left ventricular function, significant hematologic abnormalities. Caution: moderate to severe alcoholic hepatitis, elderly, preexisting or recent-onset CNS demyelinating disorder.
sideEffects: Injection site erythema, pruritus, pain, swelling, abdominal pain, vomiting (more common in children than adults). Headache, rhinitis, dizziness.
adverseEffects: Infection (pyelonephritis, cellulitis, osteomyelitis, wound infection, leg ulcer, septic arthritis, diarrhea, bronchitis, pneumonia) occurs in 29%–38% of patients. Rare adverse effects include heart failure, hypertension, hypotension, pancreatitis, GI hemorrhage.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess onset, type, location, duration of pain, inflammation. If significant exposure to varicella virus has occurred during treatment, therapy should be temporarily discontinued and treatment with varicella-zoster immune globulin should be considered. Screen for active infection. Question history as listed in Precautions. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Assess for improvement of joint swelling, pain, tenderness. Monitor erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein level, CBC with differential, platelet count. Observe for signs of infection. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - A healthcare provider will show y.

name: ethambutol
uses: Active TB — part of the standard 4-drug regimen (HRZE) for the initial 2-month phase. Tuberculosis caused by drug-resistant strains.
action: Inhibits arabinosyl transferase enzymes involved in mycobacterial cell wall arabinogalactan synthesis, disrupting cell wall structure. Bacteriostatic at standard doses.
precautions: Caution: renal impairment (dose adjustment), gout (raises uric acid).
sideEffects: Visual disturbances (most important — optic neuritis: decreased visual acuity, red-green color blindness). Arthralgia, hyperuricemia, nausea, headache.
adverseEffects: Optic neuritis (most serious — can lead to irreversible blindness if not caught early. Dose- and duration-related). Peripheral neuropathy. Anaphylaxis (rare).
nursingConsiderations: INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monthly visual acuity and color vision testing. Report any visual changes immediately — STOP drug. Monitor renal function. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING Report any changes in vision immediately (blurring, difficulty distinguishing red from green). Monthly eye exams are essential while on this drug. Take with food to reduce GI upset. Complete full TB treatment course.

name: everolimus
uses: Afinitor: advanced renal cell carcinoma after failure of treatment with SUNItinib or SORAfenib. Subependymal giant cell astrocytoma (SEGA) associated with tuberous sclerosis. Progressive neuroendocrine tumors of pancreatic origin and progressive, well-differentiated, nonfunctional neuroendocrine tumors of GI or lung origin. Advanced hormone receptor–positive, HER2-negative breast cancer in postmenopausal women. Tuberous sclerosis c.
action: Binds to the FK binding protein to form a complex that inhibits activation of mTOR. Inhibits vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF). Result: Reduces cell proliferation, produces cell death.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to everolimus, sirolimus, other rapamycin derivatives. Caution: Conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds). Caution: Hereditary galactose intolerance. Caution: renal/hepatic impairment. Caution: hyperlipidemia.
sideEffects: Stomatitis, asthenia, diarrhea, cough, rash, nausea, peripheral edema, anorexia.
adverseEffects: Noninfectious pneumonitis characterized as hypoxia, pleural effusion, cough, or dyspnea was reported in 14% of patients. Grade 3 noninfectious pneumonitis reported in 4%. Localized and systemic infections, including pneumonia, other bacterial infections, and invasive fungal infections, have occurred due to everolimus immunosuppressive properties. Renal failure occurs in 3% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess medical history, especially renal function, use of other immunosuppressants. Obtain CBC, BMP, LFT before treatment begins and routinely thereafter. Screen for active infection. Offer emotional support. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Offer antiemetics to control nausea, vomiting. Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. Assess skin for evidence of rash, edema. Monitor CBC, particularly Hgb, platelet, neutrophil count; BUN, creatinine, LFT. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Treatment may depress your immune system and reduce your ability to fight infect.

name: exemestane
uses: Advanced breast cancer in postmenopausal women whose disease has progressed following tamoxifen therapy. Adjuvant postmenopausal women with estrogen receptor-positive early breast cancer after 2–3 yrs of tamoxifen therapy for completion of 5 consecutive yrs of adjuvant hormonal therapy.
action: Irreversibly inactivates aromatase, the principal enzyme that converts androgens to estrogens in both premenopausal and postmenopausal women, lowering circulating estrogen level. Result: Inhibits growth of breast cancers stimulated by estrogens.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to exemestane. Caution: Not indicated for use in premenopausal women. Caution: Concomitant use of estrogen-containing agents, strong CYP3A4 inducers.
sideEffects: Fatigue, nausea, depression, hot flashes, pain, insomnia, anxiety, dyspnea.
adverseEffects: MI has been reported.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Question history of cardiac disease. Receive full medication history and screen for interactions. Offer emotional support. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor for onset of depression. Assess sleep pattern. Monitor for and assist with ambulation if dizziness occurs. Assess for headache. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Report if nausea, hot flashes become unmanageable. - Avoid tasks that require alertness, motor skills until response to drug is established. - Best taken after meals and at same time each day.

name: ezetimibe
uses: Adjunct to diet for primary hypercholesterolemia (monotherapy or in combination with HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors [statins]), homozygous sitos-terolemia, homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (combined with atorvastatin or simvastatin). Mixed hyperlipidemia (in combination with fenofibrate).
action: Inhibits cholesterol absorption in brush border of small intestine, leading to decrease in delivery of intestinal cholesterol to liver. Reduces hepatic cholesterol stores and increases clearance of cholesterol from the blood. Result: Reduces total serum cholesterol, LDL, triglycerides; increases HDL.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ezetimibe. Concurrent use of an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (atorvastatin, fluvastatin, lovastatin, pravastatin, simvastatin) in patients with active hepatic disease or unexplained persistent elevations in serum transaminase; pregnancy and breastfeeding (when used with a statin). Caution: Severe renal or mild hepatic impairment. Caution: Not recommended in those with moderate or severe hepatic impairment.
sideEffects: Back pain, diarrhea, arthralgia, sinusitis, abdominal pain, cough, pharyngitis, fatigue.
adverseEffects: Hepatitis, hypersensitivity reaction, myopathy, rhabdomyolysis occur rarely.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain diet history, especially fat consumption. Obtain serum cholesterol, triglycerides, hepatic function tests, blood counts during initial therapy and periodically during treatment. Treatment should be discontinued if hepatic enzyme levels persist more than 3 times normal limit. Receive full medication history and screen for interactions. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Periodic laboratory tests are essen.

name: famciclovir
uses: Acute herpes zoster (shingles) in immunocompetent patients, treatment and suppression of recurrent genital herpes in immunocompetent patients, recurrent mucocutaneous herpes simplex in HIV-infected patients. Recurrent herpes labialis (cold sores) in immunocompetent patients.
action: Inhibits HSV-2 polymerase, inhibiting herpes viral DNA synthesis and replication. Shortens healing time of herpes zoster lesions. Result: Suppresses replication of herpes simplex virus, varicella-zoster virus.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to famciclovir, penciclovir. Caution: Renal impairment. Caution: Avoid use in galactose intolerance, severe lactose deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption syndromes.
sideEffects: Headache, nausea, dizziness, drowsiness, paresthesia (especially feet), diarrhea, vomiting, constipation.
adverseEffects: Urticaria, severe skin rash, hallucinations, confusion (delirium, disorientation occur predominantly in elderly) has been reported.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Question history of galactose intolerance, severe lactose deficiency, glucose-galactose malabsorption, renal impairment. Assess herpetic lesions. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor herpetic lesions. Be alert to neurologic effects: headache, dizziness. Provide analgesics, comfort measures. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Do not touch lesions with fingers to avoid spreading infection to new site. - Genital herpes: Continue therapy for full length of treatment. - Avoid contact with lesions during duration of outbreak to prevent cross-contamination. - Use condoms during sexual activity. - Report if lesions recur or do not improve. - Avoid tasks that require alertness, m.

name: famotidine
uses: Short-term active duodenal ulcer. Prevention, maintenance of duodenal ulcer recurrence. Short-term active benign gastric ulcer. Short-term gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) (symptoms of GERD, erosive esophagitis). Pathological hypersecretory conditions (e.g., Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, multiple endocrine adenomas).
action: Inhibits histamine action of H2 receptors of parietal cells. Result: Inhibits gastric acid secretion (fasting, nocturnal, or stimulated by food, caffeine, insulin).
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to famotidine, other H2 antagonists. OTC: Avoid use in patients with dysphagia, odynophagia, hematemesis, melena, hematochezia. Renal impairment. Caution: Renal/hepatic impairment, elderly, thrombocytopenia.
sideEffects: Headache, confusion, constipation, diarrhea, dizziness.
adverseEffects: Agranulocytosis, pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia occur rarely.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess epigastric/abdominal pain. Verify platelet count in critically ill. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. Monitor for headache. Assess for confusion in elderly. Consider interrupting treatment in. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Report headache. - Avoid excessive amounts of coffee, aspirin. - Report persistent symptoms of heartburn, acid indigestion, sour stomach. Fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki fam tras-tu-zoo-mab de-rux-the-can (Enhertu) BLACK BOX ALERT Serious and fatal cases of interstitial lung disease (ILD), pneumonitis were reported. Monitor for symptoms of ILD,.

name: febuxostat
uses: Hyperuricemia in adults with gout having an inadequate response to maximum dose of allopurinol, intolerant to allopurinol, or when allopurinol is not advisable.
action: Decreases uric acid production by selectively inhibiting the enzyme xanthine oxidase. Result: Reduces uric acid concentrations in serum and urine.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to febuxostat. Concomitant use with azaTHIOprine, mercaptopurine. Caution: Severe renal/hepatic impairment, history of cardiac disease or stroke. Caution: Hypersensitivity to allopurinol. Caution: Pts at risk for urate formation.
sideEffects: Nausea, arthralgia, rash, dizziness.
adverseEffects: Hepatic function abnormalities occur in 6% of patients. May increase risk of thromboembolic events including CVA, MI.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess renal function, LFT; concomitant use with azaTHIOprine, mercaptopurine, theophylline (contraindicated). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Discontinue medication immediately if rash appears. Encourage high fluid intake (3,000 mL/day). Monitor I&O (output should be at least 2,000 mL/day). Monitor CBC, serum uric acid, renal function, LFT. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Encourage drinking 8–10 (8-oz) glasses of fluid daily while taking medication. - Report rash, chest pain, shortness of.

name: ferumoxytol
uses: Ferric carboxymaltose: iron deficiency in adults and patients 1 yr of age and older who have either intolerance or an unsatisfactory response to oral iron. Adults with non-dialysis-dependent chronic kidney disease. Iron deficiency in adults with HF class II/III. Ferumoxytol: iron deficiency in adults. Ferrous fumarate, gluconate, sulfate: Prevention, iron-deficiency anemia.
action: Essential component in formation of Hgb, myoglobin, enzymes. Promotes effective erythropoiesis and transport, utilization of oxygen. Result: Prevents iron deficiency.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to iron salts. Hemochromatosis, hemolytic anemias. Caution: Peptic ulcer, regional enteritis, ulcerative colitis, patients receiving frequent blood transfusions.
sideEffects: Mild, transient nausea, heartburn, anorexia, constipation, diarrhea.
adverseEffects: Large doses may aggravate existing GI tract disease (peptic ulcer, regional enteritis, ulcerative colitis). Severe iron poisoning occurs most often in children, manifested as vomiting, severe abdominal pain, diarrhea, dehydration, followed by hyperventilation, pallor, cyanosis, cardiovascular collapse.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess nutritional status, dietary history. Question history of hemochromatosis, hemolytic anemia, ulcerative colitis. Question use of antacids, calcium supplements. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor serum iron, total iron-binding capacity, reticulocyte count, Hgb, ferritin. Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. Assess for clinical improvement, record relief of iron-deficiency symptoms (fatigue, irritability, pallor, paresthesia of extremities, headache). PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Expect stool color to darken. - Oral liquid may stain teeth. - To prevent mucous membrane and teeth staining with liquid preparation, use dropper or straw and.

name: fesoterodine
uses: Adults with overactive bladder with symptoms including urinary incontinence, urgency, frequency. Neurogenic detrusor overactivity (NDO) in patients 6 yrs of age and older and weighing more than 25 kg.
action: Exhibits antimuscarinic activity by interceding via cholinergic muscarinic receptors, thereby mediating urinary bladder contraction. Result: Decreases urinary frequency, urgency.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to fesoterodine. Gastric retention, uncontrolled narrow-angle glaucoma, urinary retention. Caution: Severe renal impairment, severe hepatic impairment, clinically significant bladder outflow obstruction (risk of urinary retention), GI obstructive disorders (e.g., pyloric stenosis [risk of gastric retention]), treated narrow-angle glaucoma, myasthenia gravis, concurrent therapy with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, elderly, use in hot weather.
sideEffects: Dry mouth, constipation, urinary tract infection, dry eyes, nausea, dysuria, back pain, rash.
adverseEffects: Severe anticholinergic effects including abdominal cramps, facial warmth, excessive salivation/lacrimation, diaphoresis, pallor, urinary urgency, blurred vision.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess urinary pattern (e.g., urinary frequency, urgency). Question history as listed in Precautions. Receive full medication history. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Assist with ambulation if dizziness occurs. Question for visual changes. Monitor incontinence, postvoid residuals. Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - May produce constipation and urinary retention. - Blurred vision may occur; use caution until drug effects have been determined. - Heat prostration (due to decreased sweating) can occur if used in a hot environment. - Do not ingest grapefruit products.

name: fexofenadine
uses: Symptoms associated with hayfever or other upper respiratory allergies (e.g., runny nose, sneezing, itching of nose/throat).
action: Competes with histamine-1 receptor site on effector cells in GI tract, blood vessels, and respiratory tract. Result: Relieves hayfever/upper respiratory symptoms.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to fexofenadine. Caution: Renal impairment, hypertension (if drug combined with pseudoephedrine). Caution: Orally disintegrating tablet not recommended in children younger than 6 yrs.
sideEffects: Drowsiness, headache, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, abdominal distress, dysmenorrhea.
adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity reaction occurs rarely.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess severity of congestion, rhinitis, urticaria, watery eyes. Monitor rate, depth, rhythm, type of respiration; quality, rate of pulse. Assess lung sounds for rhonchi, wheezing, rales. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Assess for therapeutic response; relief from allergy: itching, red, watery eyes, rhinorrhea, sneezing. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Avoid tasks that require alertness, motor skills until response to drug is established. - Avoid alcohol during antihistamine therapy. - Coffee, tea may help reduce drowsiness. - Do not take with any fruit juices.

name: fidaxomicin
uses: Cbstridioides difficile–associated diarrhea6 mos and older.
action: Binds to ribosomal sites of susceptible organisms, inhibiting RNA-dependent protein synthesis by RNA polymerase. Result: Bactericidal against C.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to fidaxomicin. Caution: History of anemia, neutropenia, macrolide allergy.
sideEffects: Pyrexia, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, abdominal distension, abdominal tenderness, dyspepsia, dysphagia.
adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity reactions including angioedema, dyspnea, pruritus, rash were reported. May increase risk of development of drug-resistant bacteria or superinfection when used in the absence of proven or strongly suspected C. Difficile infection. GI hemorrhage reported in 4% of patients. Other reactions include drug eruption, metabolic acidosis.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Verify positive C. Difficile toxin test before initiating treatment. Initiate contact precautions. Assess bowel sounds, stool characteristics (color, frequency, consistency). Assess hydration status. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor for volume loss, dehydration, hypotension, abdominal pain, pyrexia. Encourage nutrition/fluid intake. Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. Routinely assess bowel sounds.

name: filgrastim
uses: Granix: Decreases duration of severe neutropenia1 mo and older with nonmyeloid malignancies receiving chemotherapy associated with severe neutropenia, fever. Neupogen, Zarxio: Reduces neutropenia duration, sequelae in patients with nonmyeloid malignancies having myeloablative therapy followed by bone marrow transplant (BMT). Mobilization of hematopoietic progenitor cells into peripheral blood for collection by apheresis. Reduces incidence and duration of severe neutropenia (e.
action: Stimulates production, maturation, activation of neutrophils. Result: Increases migration and cytotoxicity of neutrophils.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to filgrastim. Neupogen, Zarxio (additional): History of serious allergic reaction to human granulocyte colony-stimulating factors. Caution: Malignancy with myeloid characteristics (due to G-CSF’s potential to act as growth factor), gout, psoriasis, neutrophil count > 50, 000 cells/mm3, sickle cell disease, concomitant use of other drugs that may result in thrombocytopenia. Caution: Do not use 24 hrs before or after cytotoxic chemotherapy.
sideEffects: Nausea/vomiting, mild to severe bone pain (more frequent with high-dose IV form, less frequent with low-dose SQ form), alopecia, diarrhea, fever, fatigue, anorexia.
adverseEffects: Long-term administration occasionally produces chronic neutropenia, splenomegaly. Acute respiratory distress syndrome, alveolar hemorrhage and hemoptysis (patients undergoing peripheral blood progenitor cell collection mobilization), capillary leak syndrome, cutaneous vasculitis, glomerulonephritis, leukocytosis, MI, thrombocytopenia, sickle cell crisis, splenic rupture may occur.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC prior to initiation and twice wkly thereafter. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Report fever, chills, severe bone pain, chest pain, palpitations, difficulty breathing; left upper abdominal pain/tightness; flank pain.

name: finasteride
uses: Proscar: Treatment (monotherapy) of symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) to improve symptoms, reduce risk of acute urinary retention, or reduce the need for surgery, including transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) and prostatectomy. Used in combination with an alpha-blocker (e.g., doxazosin) to reduce risk of symptomatic progression of BPH. Propecia: male pattern hair loss.
action: Inhibits 5-alpha reductase, an intracellular enzyme that converts testosterone into dihydrotestosterone (DHT) in prostate gland, resulting in decreased serum DHT. Result: Reduces size of prostate gland.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to finasteride, pregnancy or women of childbearing potential. Caution: Hepatic impairment, urinary outflow obstruction, urinary retention. Caution: Women who are attempting to conceive should avoid exposure to crushed or broken tablets.
sideEffects: Gynecomastia, sexual dysfunction (impotence, decreased libido, decreased volume of ejaculate).
adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity reaction, circumoral swelling, testicular pain occur rarely.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Digital rectal exam, serum prostate-specific antigen (PSA) determination should be performed in. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Diligently monitor urinary output, especially in. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Treatment may cause impoten.

name: finerenone
uses: To reduce the risk of sustained estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline, end-stage kidney disease, cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction (MI), and hospitalization for HF in adults with chronic kidney disease (CKD) associated with type 2 diabetes.
action: Selectively blocks MR-mediated sodium reabsorption and MR overactivation in both epithelial (kidney) and nonepithelial (heart, blood vessels) tissues. Result: Reduces inflammation and fibrosis in epithelial and nonepithelial tissues.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to finerenone. Concomitant use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, ketoconazole, ritonavir). Adrenal insufficiency. Caution: Mild to moderate hepatic impairment. Caution: Avoid use in patients with severe hepatic impairment. Caution: Avoid concomitant use of mild to moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors or strong or moderate CYP3A inducers.
sideEffects: Moderate: Hyperkalemia, hypotension, hyponatremia.
adverseEffects: May cause hyperkalemia. Overdose may further increase risk of hyperkalemia.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain serum potassium, eGFR; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Do not initiate treatment if serum potassium is >5.0 mEq/L. Question history of hepatic impairment. Obtain full medication history and screen for interactions. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Obtain serum potassium level 4 wks after initiation and with any dose adjustment. Consider more frequent monitoring if serum potassium level is 4.8–5 mEq/L upon initiation or in. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Treatment may c.

name: fingolimod
uses: Relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS), including clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, and active secondary progressive disease, in patients 10 yrs of age and older.
action: Blocks capacity of lymphocytes to move out from lymph nodes, reducing number of lymphocytes available to the CNS. Result: May involve reduction of lymphocyte migration into central nervous system, which reduces central inflammation.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to fingolimod. Sick sinus syndrome, second-degree or higher conduction block (unless patients has functioning pacemaker). Baseline QT interval 500 msec or greater. Concurrent use of class Ia or III antiarrhythmic. Recent (within 6 mos) MI, unstable angina, stroke, TIA, decompensated requiring hospitalization or NYHA class III/IV HF. Caution: Concomitant use of antiarrhythmics, beta blockers, calcium channel blockers, immunosuppressants, immune modulators, antineopl.
sideEffects: Headache, diarrhea, back pain, cough, dyspnea, clinical depression, dizziness, hypertension.

name: fluconazole

name: fondaparinux

name: fosphenytoin

name: frovatriptan

Question regarding onset, location, duration of migraine, possible precipitating factors. name: furosemide

name: glatiramer

name: glipizide
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus as an adjunct to diet and exercise.

Never skip meals. Carry glucose tablets. Report signs of low blood sugar immediately.

name: glyburide
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus as adjunct to diet and exercise. Gestational diabetes (alternative to insulin in some guidelines).

Prolonged hypoglycemia may require hospitalization. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING Take with first meal of the day. Never skip meals. Carry glucose tablets/fast-acting carbohydrates. name: golimumab
uses: Simponi: adults with active ankylosing spondylitis. Adults with active psoriatic arthritis (alone or in combination with methotrexate). action: Binds specifically to tumor necrosis factor (TNF) alpha, blocking its interaction with cell surface TNF receptors. Result: Alters biologic activity of TNF alpha, reduces inflammation, may alter pathophysiology of rheumatoid arthritis.

Caution: Residence or travel from areas of endemic mycosis. Caution: tuberculosis, underlying hematologic disorders, preexisting or recent-onset demyelinating disorders (e.g., multiple sclerosis, polyneuropathy), patients with HF or decreased left ventricular function. Caution: Avoid concomitant use with live vaccines, abatacept, or anakinra (increased incidence o.
sideEffects: Laryngitis, nasopharyngitis, pharyngitis, rhinitis, upper respiratory tract infection, bronchitis, hypertension, rash.
adverseEffects: Neutropenia, lymphopenia may increase risk of infection. New-onset psoriasis, exacerbation of preexisting psoriasis have been reported. Serious infections including sepsis, pneumonia, cellulitis, TB, invasive fungal infections reported. May increase risk of lymphoma, melanoma, new malignancies.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, LFT; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Do not initiate therapy if active infection suspected. Evaluate for active TB and test for latent infection prior to and during treatment. Induration of 5 mm or greater with tuberculin skin test should be considered a positive result when assessing for latent TB. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, LFT every 4–8.

name: goserelin
uses: Breast cancer: Palliative advanced breast cancer in pre-and peri-menopausal women. Endometrial thinning: Endometrial thinning before ablation for dysfunctional uterine bleeding. Endometriosis: endometriosis, including pain relief and lesions. Prostate cancer: Palliative advanced carcinoma of the prostate. Locally confined prostate cancer (in combination with an antiandrogen).
action: Initially, stimulates release of luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) from anterior pituitary. Chronic administration causes a sustained suppression of pituitary gonadotropins. Result: In females, reduces ovarian, uterine, mammary gland size; regresses hormone-responsive tumors.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to goserelin, GnRH, GnRH agonist analogues. Pregnancy (except when used for palliative treatment of advanced breast cancer). Caution: Women of childbearing potential until pregnancy has been excluded. Caution: Pts at risk for decreased bone density.
sideEffects: Headache, hot flashes, depression, diaphoresis, sexual dysfunction, impotence, lower urinary tract symptoms, pain.
adverseEffects: Arrhythmias, HF, hypertension occur rarely. Ureteral obstruction, spinal cord compression have been observed (immediate orchiectomy may be necessary). Hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, may occur. Hyperglycemia, new-onset diabetes occurred in men taking GnRH antagonists.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Question history of diabetes, cardiovascular disease, recent MI, prior hypersensitivity reaction. Receive full medication history; screen for QT interval–prolonging medications, anticoagulant medications. Screen for conditions predisposing to QT interval prolongation. In males, question history of urethral obstruction, urinary retention, spinal cord compression, spinal stenosis. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Use nonhormonal methods of contraception during therapy. - Report.

name: granisetron
uses: Nausea/vomiting associated with emetogenic cancer therapy and cancer radiation therapy.
action: Selectively blocks serotonin stimulation at receptor sites centrally in chemo-receptor trigger zone, peripherally on vagal nerve terminals. Result: Prevents nausea/vomiting.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to granisetron. Hypersensitivity to other 5-HT3 receptor antagonists. Caution: Congenital QT prolongation, concomitant administration of medications that prolong QT interval, electrolyte abnormalities, cumulative high-dose anthracycline therapy. Caution: Following abdominal surgery or in chemotherapy-induced nausea, vomiting (may mask progressive ileus or gastric distention), hepatic disease.
sideEffects: Headache, constipation, asthenia, diarrhea, abdominal pain, altered taste, fever.
adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity reaction, hypertension, hypotension, arrhythmias (sinus bradycardia, atrial fibrillation, AV block, ventricular ectopy), ECG abnormalities occur rarely. Increased risk of serotonin syndrome reported in patients taking concomitant serotonergic drugs (e.g., SSRIs, SNRIs). May prolong QTc interval.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess hydration status. Ensure that granisetron is given within 30 min of starting chemotherapy. Receive full medication history and screen for interactions. Screen for QT interval–prolonging conditions. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor for therapeutic effect. Assess for headache. Monitor for dehydration due to recurrent vomiting. Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Granisetron is effective shortly following administration; prevents nausea/vomiting. - Transitory taste disorder may occur.

name: guselkumab
uses: Moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adult patients who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy. Active psoriatic arthritis in adults.
action: Selectively binds to interleukin-23 receptor reducing levels of IL-17A, IL-17F, IL-22. IL-23 is a cytokine that is involved in inflammatory and immune responses. Result: Inhibits release of proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to guselkumab. Caution: Hepatic impairment, active infection until resolved, history of chronic or recurrent infections, conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, immunocompromised patients, open wounds), prior tuberculosis exposure (do not give to patients with active TB infection). Caution: Concomitant use of live vaccines not recommended.
sideEffects: Headache, tension headache, arthralgia, diarrhea.
adverseEffects: May increase risk of tuberculosis infection. Other infections including upper respiratory tract infection, nasopharyngitis, pharyngitis, viral upper respiratory tract infection (14% of patients), gastroenteritis, viral gastroenteritis (1% of patients), tinea infections (1% of patients), herpes simplex virus (1% of patients) may occur. Mild to moderate elevated serum ALT, AST reported in 3% of patients. Immunogenicity (auto-gusel-kumab antibodies) occurred in 6% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain LFT in. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor LFT periodically. Monitor for symptoms of tub. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s with hepatic impairment. Question history of hepatic impairment, herpes zoster infection, parasitic infection. Screen for active infection. Pts should be evaluated for active tuberculosis and tested for latent infection prior to initiating treatment and periodically during therapy.

name: haloperidol
uses: Schizophrenia, Tourette’s disorder (controls tics and vocal utterances), severe behavioral problems in children with combative explosive hyperexcitability without immediate provocation. Psychotic disorder, short-term hyperactive children.
action: Nonselectively blocks postsynaptic DOPamine receptors in brain. Strong extrapyramidal, antiemetic effects; weak anticholinergic, sedative effects. Result: Produces tranquilizing effect.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to haloperidol, CNS depression, coma, Parkinson’s disease. Caution: Renal/hepatic impairment, cardiovascular disease, history of seizures, prolonged QT syndrome, medications that prolong QT interval, hypothyroidism, thyrotoxicosis, electrolyte imbalance (e.g., hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia), EEG abnormalities, narrow–angle glaucoma, elderly, patients at risk for pneumonia, decreased GI motility, urinary retention, BPH, visual disturbances, myelosuppression.
sideEffects: Blurred vision, constipation, orthostatic hypotension, dry mouth, swelling or soreness of female breasts, peripheral edema, allergic reaction, difficulty urinating.
adverseEffects: Extrapyramidal symptoms (EPS) appear to be dose related and typically occur in first few days of therapy. Marked drowsiness/lethargy, excessive salivation, fixed stare may be mild to severe in intensity. Less frequently noted are severe akathisia (motor restlessness), acute dystonias: torticollis (neck muscle spasm), opisthotonos (rigidity of back muscles), oculogyric crisis (rolling back of eyes). Tardive dyskinesia (tongue protrusion, puffing of cheeks, chewing/puckering of the mouth) may occu.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess behavior, appearance, emotional status, response to environment, speech pattern, thought content. Assess mental status. Screen for comorbidities as listed in Precautions (especially seizure disorder, long QT syndrome). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BP, heart rate/rhythm. Monitor ECG, QT interval. Supervise suicidal-risk. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s closely during early therapy (as depression lessens, energy level improves, increasing suicide potential). Monitor for rigidity, tremor, mask-like facial expression, fine tongue movement. Assess for therapeutic response (interest in surroundings, improvement in self-care, increased ability to concentrate, relaxed facial expression).

name: heparin
uses: Prophylaxis and thromboembolic disorders (e.g., venous thromboembolism, pulmonary embolism) and thromboembolic complications associated with atrial fibrillation. Anticoagulant for extracorporeal and dialysis procedures. Maintain patency of IV devices. Prevents clotting in arterial and cardiac surgery.
action: Potentiates action of antithrombin III. Interferes with blood coagulation by blocking conversion of prothrombin to thrombin and fibrinogen to fibrin. Result: Prevents further extension of existing thrombi or new clot formation.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to heparin. Severe thrombocytopenia, uncontrolled active bleeding (unless secondary to disseminated intravascular coagulation [DIC]), history of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT), heparin-induced thrombocytopenia with thrombosis (HITT), or patients who test positive for HIT antibody. Caution: Allergy to pork. Caution: Pts at risk for bleeding (e.g., congenital/acquired bleeding disorders, active GI ulcerative disease, hemophilia, concomitant platelet inhibitors, sever.
sideEffects: Pruritus, burning (particularly on soles of feet) caused by vasospastic reaction, pain, cyanosis of extremity 6–10 days after initial therapy lasting 4–6 hrs, hypersensitivity reaction (chills, fever, urticaria, asthma.
adverseEffects: Bleeding complications ranging from local ecchymoses to major hemorrhage (cutaneous/GI/genitourinary/intracranial/nasal/oral/pharyngeal /urethral/vaginal bleeding) occur more frequently in high-dose therapy, intermittent IV infusion, women 60 yrs and older. HIT can cause life-threatening thromboembolism such as CVA, MI, DVT, pulmonary embolism, renal artery thrombosis, mesenteric thrombosis. Antidote: Protamine sulfate 1–1.5 mg IV for every 100 units heparin SQ within 30 min of overdose, 0.5–0.7.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, PT/INR, aPTT. Cross-check dose with coworker. Assess for bleeding risk. Question history of recent trauma, head injuries, GI/GU bleeding. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, PT/INR daily. Obtain aPTT (or anti-Xa assay) 6 hrs after initiation or any change in dosage (or per clinical standards) until maintenance dose is established, then check aPTT (or anti-Xa assay) q24hrs (or per clinical standards). In long-term therapy, monitor 1–2 times/mo. Diligently assess for bleeding. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s has not received spinal anesthesia, spinal procedures.

name: hydrochlorothiazide
uses: Hypertension. Edema associated with heart failure, renal disease, or cirrhosis. Nephrolithiasis prevention (calcium stones).
action: Inhibits sodium-chloride reabsorption in the distal convoluted tubule of the kidney, increasing urinary excretion of sodium, chloride, and water.
precautions: Caution: diabetes (may increase glucose), gout (increases uric acid), hypokalemia risk, SLE, renal/hepatic impairment.
sideEffects: Hypokalemia, dizziness, orthostatic hypotension, polyuria, nausea, photosensitivity.
adverseEffects: Severe hypokalemia, hyponatremia, hypomagnesemia, hyperglycemia, hyperuricemia, pancreatitis (rare), hypersensitivity reactions.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Monitor BP, electrolytes (K+, Na+), BMP, glucose, uric acid. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor daily weight. Watch for hypokalemia (muscle cramps, weakness, arrhythmias). Assess for orthostatic hypotension. Give in the morning to avoid nocturia. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING Take in the morning. Eat potassium-rich foods (bananas, oranges). Avoid prolonged sun exposure. Change positions slowly.

name: hydrocortisone
brand: Anusol HC, Cortaid, Cortef, SOLU-Cortef, Cortenema, Preparation H, Proctocort
uses: Systemic: allergic states. Endocrine, hematologic, ophthalmic, rheumatic disorders. Dermatologic, neoplastic, respiratory diseases. Topical: Inflammatory dermatoses, adjunctive ulcerative colitis, atopic dermatitis, inflamed hemorrhoids.
action: Inhibits accumulation of inflammatory cells at inflammation sites, phagocytosis, lysosomal enzyme release, synthesis and/or release of mediators of inflammation. Reverses increased capillary permeability. Result: Prevents/suppresses cell-mediated immune reactions.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to hydrocortisone. Systemic fungal infections. Use in premature infants. Administration of live or attenuated virus vaccines. IM administration in idiopathic thrombocytopenia purpura. Intrathecal administration. Caution: Thyroid dysfunction, cirrhosis, hypertension, osteoporosis, thromboembolic tendencies or thrombophlebitis, HF, seizure disorders, diabetes, respiratory tuberculosis, untreated systemic infections, renal/hepatic impairment, acute MI, myastheni.
sideEffects: Insomnia, heartburn, anxiety, abdominal distention, diaphoresis, acne, mood swings, increased appetite.
adverseEffects: Long-term therapy: Hypocalcemia, hypokalemia, muscle wasting (especially arms, legs), osteoporosis, spontaneous fractures, amenorrhea, cataracts, glaucoma, peptic ulcer, HF. Abrupt withdrawal after long-term therapy: Nausea, fever, headache, sudden severe joint pain, rebound inflammation, fatigue, weakness, lethargy, dizziness, orthostatic hypotension.
nursingConsiderations: INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Assess for edema. Be alert to infection (reduced immune response): sore throat, fever, vague symptoms. Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. Monitor electrolytes, BP, weight, serum glucose.

name: hydrOXYzine
uses: Symptomatic anxiety. Pruritus due to allergic conditions and histamine-mediated pruritus. Urticaria.
action: Competes with histamine for receptor sites in GI tract, blood vessels, respiratory tract. Result: Produces anxiolytic, anticholinergic, antihistaminic, analgesic effects; relaxes skeletal muscle; controls nausea, vomiting.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to hydrOXYzine, cetirizine, or levocetirizine. Early pregnancy; SQ, IV administration; patients with prolonged QT interval. Caution: Narrow-angle glaucoma, prostatic hypertrophy, bladder neck obstruction, asthma, COPD, elderly.
sideEffects: Side effects are generally mild, transient, drowsiness, dry mouth, marked discomfort with IM injection, dizziness, ataxia, asthenia.
adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity reaction (wheezing, dyspnea, chest tightness) may occur. QT interval prolongation, torsades de pointes have been reported. Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis (AGEP) may occur.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Anxiety: Offer emotional support. Assess motor responses (agitation, trembling, tension), autonomic responses (cold/clammy hands, diaphoresis). Antiemetic: Assess for dehydration (poor skin turgor, dry mucous membranes, longitudinal furrows in tongue). PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s on long-term therapy, CBC, BMP, LFT should be performed periodically. Monitor lung sounds for signs of hypersensitivity reaction. Monitor serum electrolytes in.

name: ibandronate
uses: Treatment/osteoporosis in postmenopausal women. Prostate cancer, metastatic, bone pain.
action: Inhibits bone resorption via activity on osteoclasts or osteoclast precursors. Result: Reduces rate of bone resorption, resulting in indirect increased bone mineral density.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ibandronate, other bisphosphonates; oral tablets in patients unable to stand or sit upright for at least 60 min; patients with abnormalities of the esophagus that would delay emptying (e.g., stricture, achalasia), hypocalcemia. Caution: GI diseases (duodenitis, dysphagia, esophagitis, gastritis, ulcers [drug may exacerbate these conditions]), renal impairment with CrCl < 30 mL/min.
sideEffects: Back pain, dyspepsia, peripheral discomfort, diarrhea, headache, myalgia, IV: Abdominal pain, constipation.
adverseEffects: Upper respiratory infection occurs occasionally. Overdose results in hypocalcemia, hypophosphatemia, significant GI disturbances.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain serum calcium, vitamin D level. Hypocalcemia, vitamin D deficiency must be corrected before beginning therapy. Obtain results of bone density study. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor serum calcium, phosphate. Monitor renal function tests. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Expected benefits occur only when medication is taken with full glass (6–8 oz) of plain water, first thing in the morning and at least 60 min before first food, beverage, medication of the day. Any other beverage (mineral water, orange juice, coffee) significantly reduces absorption of medication. - Do not chew, crush, dissolve, or divide tablets; swallow whole. - Do not lie down for at least.

name: ibrutinib
uses: Adults with chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL) (as monotherapy or in combination with riTUXimab or obinutuzumab or in combination with bendamustine and riTUXimab), Waldenstrom’s macroglobulinemia (WM) (as monotherapy or in combination with riTUXimab). Adults and children 1 yr and older with chronic graft-versus-host disease (CGVHD) after failure of at least one line of systemic therapy.
action: Inhibits enzymatic activity of Bruton’s tyrosine kinase (BTK), a signaling molecule that promotes malignant B-cell proliferation and survival. Result: Decreases malignant B-cell proliferation and survival.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ibrutinib. Caution: Hepatic/renal impairment, hypertension, elderly, pregnancy, history of GI disease (e.g., bleeding, ulcers). Caution: patients at high risk for tumor lysis syndrome (high tumor burden).
sideEffects: Diarrhea, fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, peripheral edema, nausea, bruising, dyspnea, constipation.
adverseEffects: Anemia, lymphopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia are expected responses to therapy. Severe myelosuppression (Grade 3–4 CTCAE) reported in 41% of patients: Neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, anemia. Infections including upper respiratory tract infection, UTI, pneumonia, skin infection, sinusitis were reported. Hemorrhagic events including epistaxis, GI bleeding, hematuria, intracranial hemorrhage, subdural hematoma reported in 5% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain vital signs, CBC, serum chemistries, LFT, PT/INR if on anticoagulants. Question history of arrhythmias, HF, GI bleed, hepatic/renal impairment, peripheral edema, pulmonary disease. Obtain negative pregnancy test before initiating treatment. Assess hydration status. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC monthly; LFT, serum chemistries, renal function routinely. Monitor stool frequency, consistency, characteristics. Immediately report hemorrhagic events:.

name: ibuprofen
clinicalClass: Antirheumatic, analgesic, antipyretic, antidysmenorrheal, vascular headache suppressant
uses: Oral: fever, inflammatory disease, and rheumatoid disorders, osteoarthritis, mild to moderate pain, primary dysmenorrhea. OTC: Reduce fever. Manage pain due to headache, physical or athletic overexertion (e.g., sprains/strains), dental pain, minor muscle/bone/joint pain, backache. Caldolor: Mild to moderate pain. Severe pain in combination with an opioid analgesic6 mos and older.
action: Reversibly inhibits COX-1 and COX-2 enzymes, resulting in decreased formation of prostaglandin precursors. Result: Produces analgesic, antiinflammatory effects; decreases fever.
precautions: Contraindicated: History of hypersensitivity to ibuprofen, aspirin, other NSAIDs. Treatment of perioperative pain in coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery. Aspirin triad (bronchial asthma, aspirin intolerance, rhinitis). NeoProfen: Preterm neonates with proven or suspected untreated infection, elevated total bilirubin, congenital heart disease in whom patency of the patent ductus arteriosus is necessary for satisfactory pulmonary or systemic blood flow (e.g., pulmonary atresia), bleeding.
sideEffects: Nausea, vomiting, dyspepsia, dizziness, rash, diarrhea or constipation, flatulence, abdominal cramps or pain.
adverseEffects: Overdose may result in metabolic acidosis. Rare reactions with long-term use include peptic ulcer, GI bleeding, gastritis, severe hepatic reaction (cholestasis, jaundice), nephrotoxicity (dysuria, hematuria, proteinuria, nephrotic syndrome), severe hypersensitivity reaction (particularly in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus or other collagen diseases). NeoProfen: Hypoglycemia, hypocalcemia, respiratory failure, UTI, edema, atelectasis may occur. Caldolor: Abdominal pain, anemia, cough, dizzi.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess onset, type, location, duration of pain, inflammation. Inspect appearance of affected joints for immobility, deformities, skin condition. Assess temperature. Question medical history as listed in Precautions. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor for evidence of nausea, dyspepsia. Assess skin for rash. Observe for bleeding, bruising, occult blood loss. Evaluate for therapeutic response: Relief of pain, stiffness, swelling; increased joint mobility; reduced joint tenderness; improved grip strength. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Avoid aspirin, alcohol during therapy (increases risk of GI bleeding). - If GI upset occurs, take with food, milk, a.

name: ifosfamide
uses: Germ cell testicular carcinoma (used in combination with other chemotherapy agents and with concurrent mesna for Prophylaxis: hemorrhagic cystitis).
action: Inhibits DNA, protein synthesis by cross-linking with DNA strands, preventing cell growth. Result: Produces cellular death (apoptosis).
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ifosfamide. Urinary outflow obstruction. Caution: Renal/hepatic impairment, compromised bone marrow reserve, active urinary tract infection, preexisting cardiac disease, prior radiation therapy, conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds). Caution: Avoid use in patients with WBC < 2, 000 cells/mm3 and platelets < 50, 000 cells/mm3.
sideEffects: Alopecia, nausea, vomiting, confusion, drowsiness, hallucinations, infection, dizziness.
adverseEffects: Hemorrhagic cystitis with hematuria, dysuria occurs frequently if protective agent (mesna) is not used. Myelosuppression (leukopenia, thrombocytopenia) occurs frequently. Pulmonary toxicity, hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, cardiotoxicity, CNS toxicity (confusion, hallucinations, drowsiness, coma) may require discontinuation of therapy. Secondary malignancies including lymphoma, thyroid cancer, sarcoma were reported.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain urinalysis before each dose. If hematuria occurs (> 10 RBCs per field), therapy should be withheld until resolution occurs. Obtain WBC, platelet count, Hgb before each dose. Question history of hepatic/renal impairment, cardiac disease. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, urinalysis, renal function, LFT. Assess for fever, sore throat, signs of local infection, unusual bruising/bleeding from any site, symptoms of anemia (excessive fatigue, weakness). Monitor for toxicities. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Treatment may depress your immune system response and reduce your ability to fight infec.

name: iloperidone
uses: Acute schizophrenia in adults.
action: Mixed combination of DOPamine type 2 (D2) and serotonin type 2 (5-HT2) antagonisms (thought to improve negative symptoms of psychosis). Result: Diminishes symptoms of schizophrenia and reduces incidence of extrapyramidal side effects.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to iloperidone. Caution: Cardiovascular disease (HF, history of MI, ischemia, cardiac conduction abnormalities), cerebrovascular disease (increases risk of CVA in patients with dementia, seizure disorders). Caution: Pts at risk for orthostatic hypotension. Caution: Pts with bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia may be at greater risk for torsades de pointes. Caution: History of seizures, conditions lowering seizure threshold, high risk of suicide, risk of aspiration pneumonia, congenital.
sideEffects: Dizziness, drowsiness, tachycardia, nausea, dry mouth, nasal congestion, weight increase, diarrhea.
adverseEffects: Extrapyramidal disorders, including tardive dyskinesia (protrusion of tongue, puffing of cheeks, chewing/puckering of the mouth), occur in 4% of patients. Upper respiratory infection occurs in 3% of patients. QT interval prolongation may produce torsades de pointes, a form of ventricular tachycardia. Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (e.g., hyperpyrexia, muscle rigidity, altered mental status, irregular pulse or BP) has been noted.
nursingConsiderations: INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor for orthostatic hypotension; assist with ambulation. Monitor for fine tongue movement (may be first sign of tardive dyskinesia, possibly irreversible). Monitor serum potassium, magnesium in. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s’s behavior, appearance, emotional status, response to environment, speech pattern, thought content. ECG should be obtained to assess for QT prolongation before instituting medication. Question medical history as listed in Precautions.

name: imatinib
uses: Newly diagnosed chronic-phase Philadelphia chromosome positive chronic myeloid leukemia (Ph+ CML) in children and adults. Pts in blast crisis, accelerated phase, or chronic phase Ph+ CML who have already failed interferon therapy. Adults with relapsed or refractory Ph+ acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Treatment in children with newly diagnosed Philadelphia chromosome–positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph+ ALL), in combination with chemotherapy. Adults with myelodysplastic/myeloproliferati.
action: Inhibits Bcr-Abl tyrosine kinase, an enzyme created by Philadelphia chromosome abnormality found in patients with chronic myeloid leukemia. Result: Blocks tumor cell proliferation and induces cellular death (apoptosis).
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to imatinib. Caution: Hepatic/renal impairment, thyroidectomy patients, hypothyroidism, gastric surgery patients. History of effusions or edema (pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, generalized edema). Caution: conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds), patients at risk for GI perforation (e.g. Caution: Crohn’s disease, diverticulitis, GI tract or abdominal malignancies, GI ulcers), patients at high risk for tumor lysis syndrome (.
sideEffects: Nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, headache, fluid retention, rash, musculoskeletal pain, muscle cramps.
adverseEffects: Severe fluid retention (pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, pulmonary edema, ascites), hepatotoxicity occur rarely. Neutropenia, thrombocytopenia are expected responses to the therapy. Respiratory toxicity is manifested as dyspnea, pneumonia. Heart damage (left ventricular dysfunction, HF) may occur.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BMP, LFT; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Question history of hepatic impairment/renal impairment, hypothyroidism, HF, edema. Due to increased risk of tumor lysis syndrome, assess hydration status prior to each treatment. Assess risk of GI perforation. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC for myelosuppression wkly for 4 wks, then biweekly for 4 wks, then periodically thereafter. Obtain LFT if hepatotoxicity (bruising, jaundice, right upper abdominal pain, na.

name: indomethacin
uses: Indocin: moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis (including acute flares of chronic disease), osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, acute gouty arthritis. Relieves acute bursitis, tendinitis. Tivorbex: mild to moderate acute pain in adults. IV: For closure of hemodynamically significant patent ductus arteriosus of premature infants weighing between 500 and 1, 750 g when 48-hr usual medical management is ineffective.
action: Reversibly inhibits COX-1 and COX-2 enzymes. Produces antipyretic, analgesic, antiinflammatory effects by inhibiting prostaglandin synthesis. Result: Reduces inflammatory response, fever, intensity of pain.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to aspirin, indomethacin, other NSAIDs. Perioperative pain in setting of CABG surgery. History of asthma, urticaria, allergic reactions after taking aspirin, other NSAIDs. Suppositories: History of proctitis, recent rectal bleeding. Injection: In preterm infants with untreated/systemic infection or congenital heart disease where patency of PDA necessary for pulmonary or systemic blood flow; bleeding, thrombocytopenia, coagulation defects, necrotizing enterocol.
sideEffects: Headache, nausea, vomiting, dyspepsia, dizziness, depression, tinnitus, diaphoresis.

May aggravate depression or other psychiatric disturbances, epilepsy, parkinsonism. Nephrotoxicity (dysuria, hematuria, proteinuria, nephrotic syndrome) occurs rarely.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess onset, type, location, duration of pain, fever, inflammation. Inspect appearance of affected joints for immobility, deformities, skin condition. Question medical history as listed in Precautions. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor serum BUN, creatinine, potassium, LFT. Monitor for evidence of nausea, dyspepsia. Assist with ambulation if dizziness occurs. Evaluate for therapeutic response: relief of pain, stiffness, swelling; increased joint mobility; reduced joint tenderness; improved grip strength.

name: inotuzumab ozogamicin
uses: Adults with relapsed or refractory B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL).
action: Binds to and internalizes ADC-CD22 complex in CD22-expressing tumor cells, promoting cellular release of N-acetyl-gamma-calicheamicin dimethyl hydrazide (a cytotoxic agent). Activation of N-acetyl-gamma-calicheamicin dimethyl hydrazide induces breakage of double-strand DNA, resulting in cell cycle arrest and apoptosis. Result: Inhibits tumor cell growth and metastasis in ALL.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to inotuzumab. Caution: Conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, immunocompromised patients, renal failure, open wounds), elderly. Caution: Pts at risk for QT interval prolongation or torsades de pointes (congenital long QT syndrome, medications that prolong QT interval, hy.
