Hemorrhagic events including contusion, ecchymosis, epistaxis, gingival bleeding, hematemesis, hematochezia, hematotympanum, hematuria, metrorrhagia, subdural hematoma, postprocedural hematoma, hemorrhagic shock, hemorrhage (conjunctival, gastric, GI, hemorrhoidal, intra-abdominal, intracranial, l.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain ANC, CBC, LFT; ECG before each dose. Calculate body surface area. Obtain pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Screen for active infection. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor ANC, CBC for myelosuppression. Monitor ECG for QT interval prolongation. LFTs should be obtained before each dose and correlated with symptoms of hepatic veno-occlusive disease (ascites, serum bilirubin elevati.

name: insulin
uses: Type 1 diabetes (insulin-dependent) and type 2 diabetes (non–insulin-dependent) to improve glycemic control. Insulin NPH: Gestational diabetes.
action: Acts via specific receptor to regulate metabolism of carbohydrates, protein, and fats. Acts on liver, skeletal muscle, and adipose tissue. Result: Controls serum glucose levels.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to insulin, use during episodes of hypoglycemia. Afrezza only: Chronic lung disease. Caution: Pts at risk for hypokalemia. Caution: renal/hepatic impairment, elderly. Caution: Afrezza only: Must be used with a long-acting insulin in type 1 diabetes. Caution: Not recommended for use in diabetic ketoacidosis or in smokers.
sideEffects: Localized redness, swelling, itching (due to improper insulin injection technique), allergy to insulin cleansing solution, infrequent: Somogyi effect (rebound hyperglycemia) with chronically excessive insulin dosages, systemic allergic reaction (rash, angioedema, anaphylaxis).
adverseEffects: Severe hypoglycemia (due to hyperinsulinism) may occur with insulin overdose, decrease/delay of food intake, excessive exercise, patients with brittle diabetes. Diabetic ketoacidosis may result from stress, illness, omission of insulin dose, long-term poor insulin control.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain serum glucose level, Hgb A1c. Discuss lifestyle to determine extent of learning, emotional needs. If given IV, obtain serum chemistries (especially serum potassium). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Assess for hypoglycemia (refer to pharmacokinetics table for peak times and duration): cool, wet skin, tremors, dizziness, headache, anxiety, tachycardia, numbness in mouth, hunger, diplopia. Assess sleeping. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s for restlessness, diaphoresis. Check for hyperglycemia: polyuria (excessive urine output), polyphagia (excessive food intake), polydipsia (excessive thirst), nausea/vomiting, dim vision, fatigue, deep and rapid breathing (Kussmaul respirations). Be alert to conditions.

name: ipilimumab
uses: Melanoma: unresectable or metastatic melanoma in adults and pediatric. Adults with unresectable or metastatic melanoma, in combination with nivolumab. Adjuvant patients with cutaneous melanoma with pathologic involvement of regional lymph nodes of more than 1 mm who have undergone complete resection, including total lymphadenectomy. Renal cell carcinoma (RCC): patients with intermediate-or poor-risk advanced renal cell carcinoma, as.
action: Augments T-cell activation and proliferation. Binds to cytotoxic T-lymphocyte–associated antigen 4 (CTLA-4) and blocks interaction of CTLA-4 with its ligands, allowing for enhanced T-cell activation and proliferation. Result: May indirectly mediate T-cell immune responses against tumors.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ipilimumab. Caution: Hepatic impairment, chronic peripheral neuropathy, thyroid/adrenal/pituitary dysfunction, autoimmune disorders (ulcerative colitis. Caution: Crohn’s disease, lupus, sarcoidosis).
sideEffects: Fatigue, diarrhea, pruritus, rash, colitis.
adverseEffects: Severe and fatal immune-mediated adverse reactions have occurred. Enterocolitis (7% of patients) may present with fever, ileus, abdominal pain, GI bleeding, intestinal perforation, severe dehydrating diarrhea. Endocrinopathies (4% of patients), including hypopituitarism, adrenal insufficiency, hypogonadism, hypothyroidism, may present with fatigue, headache, mental status change, unusual bowel habits, hypotension and may require emergent hormone replacement therapy. Dermatitis including toxic epidermal ne.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BMP, LFT; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Screen for history of hepatic impairment, chronic neuropathy, thyroid/adrenal/pituitary dysfunction, autoimmune disorders. Screen for active infection. Receive full medication history including herbal products. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor vital signs, LFT, thyroid panel before each dose. Continue focused assessment and screen for life-threatening immune-mediated adverse reactions. If adverse reactions occur, immediately notify physician and initiate proper treatment. Report suspected pregnancy.

name: ipratropium
uses: Inhalation, nebulization: Maintenance bronchospasm associated with COPD, including bronchitis, emphysema. Not indicated for immediate bronchospasm relief. Nasal spray: Symptomatic rhinorrhea associated with allergic and nonallergic perennial rhinitis (6 yrs and older) and associated with seasonal allergic rhinitis (5 yrs and older). Symptomatic rhinorrhea associated with common cold (5 yrs and o.
action: Blocks action of acetylcholine at parasym-pathetic sites in bronchial smooth muscle. Application to nasal mucosa inhibits serous/seromucous gland secretions. Result: Causes broncho-dilation, inhibits nasal secretions.
precautions: Contraindicated: History of hypersensitivity to ipratropium, atropine. Caution: Narrow-angle glaucoma, prostatic hypertrophy, bladder neck obstruction, myasthenia gravis.
sideEffects: Inhalation: Cough, dry mouth, headache, nausea, nasal: Dry nose/mouth, nasal irritation, inhalation: Dizziness, transient increased bronchospasm.
adverseEffects: Worsening of angle-closure glaucoma, acute eye pain, hypotension occur rarely.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Auscultate lung sounds. Question history of glaucoma, urinary retention, myasthenia gravis. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor rate, depth, rhythm, type of respiration; quality, rate of pulse. Assess lung sounds for rhonchi, wheezing, rales. Monitor ABGs. Observe for retractions (clavicular, sternal, intercostal), hand tremor. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Increase fluid intake (decreases lung secretion viscosity). - Do not take more than 2 inhalations at any one time (excessive use may produce paradoxical bron-ch.

name: irbesartan
uses: Hypertension alone or in combination with other antihypertensives. Diabetic nephropathy in patients with an elevated serum creatinine and proteinuria (> 300 mg/day) in patients with type 2 diabetes and hypertension. OFF- LABEL: Acute coronary syndrome (STEMI, non-STEMI), proterinuric chronic kidney disease (non-diabetic).
action: Blocks vasoconstriction, aldosterone-secreting effects of angiotensin II, inhibiting binding of angiotensin II to AT1 receptors. Result: Produces vasodilation, decreases peripheral resistance, decreases BP.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to irbesartan. Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with diabetes. Caution: Renal impairment, unstented unilateral or bilateral renal artery stenosis, dehydration, HF, idiopathic or hereditary angioedema or angioedema associated with ACE inhibitor therapy.
sideEffects: Upper respiratory tract infection, fatigue, diarrhea, cough, heartburn, dizziness, headache, nausea.
adverseEffects: Overdose may manifest as hypotension, syncope, tachycardia. Bradycardia occurs less often.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain BP, pulse immediately before each dose in addition to regular monitoring (be alert to fluctuations). Question possibility of pregnancy. Assess medication history (especially diuretic therapy). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Maintain hydration (offer fluids frequently). Assess for evidence of upper respiratory infection. Assist with ambulation if dizziness occurs. Monitor BP, pulse. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - May cause fetal or neonatal morbidity or mortality. - Report any sign of infection (sore throat, fever). - Avoid exercising during hot weather (risk of dehydration, hypotension).

name: irinotecan
uses: Camptosar: First-line therapy in combination with 5-fluorouracil and leucovorin in patients with metastatic carcinoma of the colon or rectum. Pts with metastatic carcinoma of the colon or rectum whose disease has recurred or progressed following initial fluorouracil- based therapy. Onivyde: metastatic adenocarcinoma of the pancreas (in combination with 5-fluorouracil and leucovorin) after disease progression following gemcitabine-based therapy.
action: Binds reversibly with topoisomerase I, an enzyme that relieves torsional strain in DNA by inducing reversible single-strand breaks. Prevents religation of these single-stranded breaks, resulting in damage to double-strand DNA, cell death. Result: Produces cytotoxic effect on cancer cells.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to irinotecan. Caution: Pt previously receiving pelvic, abdominal irradiation (increased risk of myelosuppression), patients older than 65 yrs, hepatic dysfunction, hyperbilirubinemia, renal impairment, preexisting pulmonary disease, conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds).
sideEffects: Nausea, alopecia, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, fatigue, fever, asthenia.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression is an expected response to therapy, but more severe reactions including febrile neutropenia may be life threatening. Pts who are homozygous for the UGT1A1*28 allele are at increased risk for neutropenia. Hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis may occur. Fatal pulmonary toxicities, interstitial pulmonary disease were reported.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC (prior to each dose), LFT; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Due to risk of severe dehydration related to diarrhea, ensure adequate hydration prior to each dose. Question history pulmonary disease, hepatic/renal impairment. Screen for active infection. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC as indicated. Monitor pulmonary status, pulse oximeter readings. Consider ABG, radiologic test if ILD/pneumonitis (excessive cough, dyspnea, fever, hypoxia) is suspect.

name: isatuximab-irfc
uses: Multiple myeloma (in combination with pomalidomide and dexamethasone) in adults who have received at least two prior therapies including lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor. Relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (in combination with carfilzomib and dexAMETHasone) in adults who have received 1–3 prior lines of therapy.
action: Binds to and inhibits cell surface glyco-protein CD38 on CD38-expressing tumor cells (highly expressed on myeloma cells). Promotes antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis and cell-mediated cytotoxicity. Result: Inhibits tumor cell growth.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to isatuximab. Caution: Baseline cytopenias, conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds).
sideEffects: Diarrhea, dyspnea, nausea, vomiting.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (anemia, lymphopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia) is an expected response to therapy, but more severe reactions including severe neutropenia, febrile neutropenia may be life threatening. Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia reported in 85% of patients. Infusion-related reactions including chills, cough, dyspnea, nausea reported in 39% of patients. Grade 3 or 4 infusion reactions including dyspnea, hypertension, bronchospasm reported in 1% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, blood type and screen; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Confirm compliance of effective contraception. Inform blood bank of treatment and possible treatment-related interference with serologic testing. Administer in an environment equipped to monitor for and manage infusion-related reactions. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC periodically for myelosuppression. Monitor vital sign during infusion. If infusion-related reaction occurs, interrupt infusion and manage symptoms.

name: isavuconazonium
uses: Invasive aspergillosis and invasive mucormycosis. (injection): adults and patients 1 yr of age and older. (capsules): adults and patients 6 yrs of age and older weighing 16 kg or greater.
action: Isavuconazonium is the prodrug of isavuconazole. Interferes with fungal cyto-chrome activity, decreasing ergosterol synthesis, inhibiting fungal cell membrane formation. Result: Damages fungal cell wall membrane.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to isavuconazonium or isavuconazole, concomitant use of strong CYP3A inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, high-dose ritonavir), strong CYP3A inducers (e.g., carBAMazepine, rifAMPin, St. John’s wort), history of short QT syndrome. Caution: Renal/hepatic impairment, hypersensitivity to other azoles. Caution: Pts at risk for acute pancreatitis. Caution: concomitant use of nephrotoxic medications. Caution: patients at risk for hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia.
sideEffects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, headache, dyspnea, peripheral edema, constipation.
adverseEffects: Severe hepatic injury including cholestasis, hepatitis, hepatic failure reported in patients with underlying medical conditions (e.g., hematologic malignancies). Infusion-related reactions including chills, dizziness, dyspnea, hypoesthesia, hypotension, paresthesia may occur. Acute respiratory failure, renal failure, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, serious hypersensitivity reaction (including anaphylaxis) were reported.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain LFT, pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential Specimens for fungal culture, histopathology should be obtained prior to initiating therapy. Receive full medication history and screen for interactions/contraindications. Question history of hypersensitivity reaction, hepatic impairment. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor LFT periodically. Monitor for infusion-related reactions, hypersensitivity reactions, anaphylaxis. Monitor I&O. Report worsening of hepatic/renal function. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Swallow capsule whole; do not chew, crush, cut, or open capsules. - Use effective contraception to avoid pregnancy. - Do not take herbal products su.

name: isoniazid
uses: Susceptible active tuberculosis due to Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Latent tuberculosis caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
action: Inhibits mycolic acid synthesis. Causes disruption of bacterial cell wall, loss of acid-fast properties in susceptible mycobacteria. Result: Bactericidal against actively growing intracellular, extracellular susceptible mycobacteria.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to isoniazid (including drug-induced hepatitis), acute hepatic disease, hepatic injury or severe adverse reactions with previous isoniazid therapy. Caution: Chronic hepatic disease, alcoholism, severe renal impairment. Caution: Pregnancy, patients at risk for peripheral neuropathy, HIV infection, history of hypersensitivity reactions to latent TB infection medications.
sideEffects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, pain at injection site, hypersensitivity reaction.
adverseEffects: Neurotoxicity (ataxia, paresthesia), optic neuritis, hepatotoxicity occur rarely.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain LFT. Question for history of hypersensitivity reactions, hepatic injury or disease, sensitivity to nicotinic acid or chemically related medications. Ensure collection of specimens for culture, sensitivity. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor LFT, assess for hepatotoxicity: anorexia, nausea, vomiting, weakness, fatigue, dark urine, jaundice (withhold concurrent INH therapy and inform physician promptly). Assess for paresthesia of extremities (. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING sespecially at risk for neuropathy may be given pyridoxine prophylactically: malnourished, elderly, diabetics,.

name: isosorbide mononitrate
uses: Dinitrate: angina pectoris due to coronary artery disease. Mononitrate: Treatment (immediate-release only) and angina pectoris due to coronary artery disease.
action: Forms free radical nitric oxide which activates intracellular cyclic guanosine monophosphate, leading to smooth muscle relaxation. Decreases preload, afterload, cardiac oxygen demand. Result: Relaxes vascular smooth muscle of arterial, venous vasculature.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to nitrates, concurrent use of sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil, or riociguat. Caution: Inferior wall MI, head trauma, increased intracranial pressure (ICP), orthostatic hypotension, blood volume depletion from diuretic therapy, systolic BP < 90 mm Hg, hy-pertrophic cardiomyopathy, alcohol consumption.
sideEffects: Headache (may be severe) occurs mostly in early therapy, diminishes rapidly in intensity, usually disappears during continued treatment, sublingual: Burning, tingling at oral point of dissolution, transient flushing of face/neck, dizziness, weakness.
adverseEffects: Discontinue if blurred vision occurs. Severe orthostatic hypotension manifested by syncope, pulselessness, cold/clammy skin, diaphoresis has been reported. Tolerance may occur with repeated, prolonged therapy, but may not occur with extended-release form. Minor tolerance with intermittent use of sublingual tablets.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Record onset, type (sharp, dull, squeezing), radiation, location, intensity, duration of anginal pain; precipitating factors (exertion, emotional stress). If headache occurs during management therapy, administer medication with meals. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Assist with ambulation if light-headedness, dizziness occurs. Assess for facial/neck flushing. Monitor number of anginal episodes, orthostatic BP. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Do not chew, crush, dissolve, or divide sublingual, extended-release, sustained-release forms. - Take sublingual tablets while sitting down. - Go from lying to standing slowly (prevents dizziness effect). - Take oral form on empty s.

name: itraconazole
uses: Oral capsules: aspergillosis, blastomycosis, histoplasmosis, onychomycosis. Oral solution: oral and esophageal candidiasis. Oral tablet: onychomycosis of toenail.
action: Inhibits synthesis of ergosterol (vital component of fungal cell formation). Result: Damages fungal cell membrane, altering its function.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to itraconazole, other azoles. Treatment of onychomycosis in patients with evidence of ventricular dysfunction (e.g., HF or history of HF), concurrent use of dofetilide, dronedarone, eplerenone, ergot derivatives, felodipine, irinotecan, lovastatin, lurasidone, methadone, midazolam (oral), pimozide, ranolazine, simvastatin, ticagrelor, triazolam, quiNIDine, concurrent use with colchicine, fesoterodine, solifenacin in patients with renal/hepatic impairment (and others).
sideEffects: Nausea, rash, vomiting, headache, diarrhea, hypertension, peripheral edema, fatigue.
adverseEffects: Hepatotoxicity (anorexia, abdominal pain, unusual fatigue/weakness, jaundiced skin/sclera, dark urine) occurs rarely.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain LFT. Assess allergies. Receive full medication history (numerous contraindications/cautions). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor for hepatotoxicity (abdominal pain, jaundice, nausea, vomiting). Monitor LFT in. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Take capsules with food, liquids if GI distress occurs. - Therapy will continue for at least 3 mos, until lab tests, clinical presentation indicate infection is controlled. - Report liver problems (abdominal pain, bruising, clay-colored stool, amber-or dark-colored urine, yellowing of the skin or eyes). - Avoid grapefruit products.

name: ivabradine
uses: To reduce the risk of hospitalization for worsening HF in patients with stable, symptomatic chronic HF with left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 35%, who are in sinus rhythm with a resting heart rate ≥ 70 bpm, and either are on maximally tolerated dose of beta blockers or have a contraindication to beta blocker use.
action: Reduces spontaneous pacemaker activity of the cardiac sinus node by blocking HCN channels that are responsible for cardiac current, which regulates heart rate. Does not affect ventricular repolarization or myocardial contractility. Result: Reduces heart rate.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ivabradine. Acute decompensated HF, BP < 90/50 mm Hg, sick sinus syndrome; sinoatrial block or third-degree AV block (unless a functional pacemaker is present), resting heart rate < 60 bpm prior to initiation, severe hepatic impairment, pacemaker dependence (heart rate maintained exclusively by a pacemaker), concomitant use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Caution: History of atrial fibrillation, hypertension. Caution: Avoid concomitant use of dilTIAZe.
sideEffects: Bradycardia, hypertension, phosphenes (visual disturbances, luminous phenomena), visual brightness.
adverseEffects: May increase risk of atrial fibrillation (8.3% of patients). Bradycardia, sinus arrest, or heart block may occur. Bradycardia occurred in 10% of patients. Risk factors for bradycardia may include sinus node dysfunction, conduction defects (e.g., first-or second-degree AV block, bundle branch block), ventricular dyssynchrony, or use of negative chronotropic drugs.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain heart rate, BP. Confirm negative pregnancy test before initiating therapy. Receive full medication history and screen for interactions. Screen for contraindications as listed in Precautions. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor heart rate, BP. Diligently monitor for atrial fibrillation, bradycardia, syncope. If symptomatic bradycardia occurs, temporary cardiac pacing or infusion of beta-stimulating agents may be warranted. Monitor for hypersensitivity reaction. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Take medication with meals. - Avoid grapefruit.

name: ivosidenib
uses: Treatment as monotherapy or in combination with azacitidine of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with a susceptible IDH1 mutation in adults with newly diagnosed AML who are 75 yrs or older or who have comorbidities that preclude use of intensive induction chemotherapy. Adults with relapsed or refractory myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) or acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with a susceptible IDH1 mutation. Adults with locally advanced or metastatic IDH1-mutated cholangiocarcinoma w.
action: Inhibits IDH1 enzymes on mutant IDH1 variants, decreasing 2-hydroxyglutarate (2-HG) levels and restoring myeloid differentiation. Inhibits tumor growth and proliferation. Result: Reduces blast counts; increases percentage of myeloid cells.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ivosidenib. Caution: Baseline leukopenia, hypotension. Caution: active infection, cardiac disease, hepatic/renal impairment, electrolyte imbalance. Caution: conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds). Caution: patients at risk for QTc interval prolongation, cardiac arrhythmias (congenital long QT syndrome, HF, QT interval–prolonging medications, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia).
sideEffects: Fatigue, asthenia, arthralgia, diarrhea, dyspnea, edema, nausea, abdominal pain.
adverseEffects: Anemia, leukopenia are expected responses to therapy. Life-threatening and/or fatal differentiation syndrome, a condition with rapid proliferation and differentiation of myeloid cells, reported in 19%–25% of patients. QT interval prolongation with QTc interval > 500 msec (9% of patients) and QTc interval > 60 msec from baseline (14% of patients) have occurred. Guillain-Barré syndrome occurred in < 1% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BMP, LFT; ECG; pregnancy test in female. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, BMP, LFT at least wkly f. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s of reproductive potential. Replete electrolytes if applicable. Confirm presence of IDH1 mutations in the blood or bone marrow. Assess adequate hydration prior to initiation due to increased risk of tumor lysis syndrome, diarrhea, vomiting.

name: ixabepilone
uses: Combination therapy with capecitabine for metastatic or locally advanced breast cancer in patients after failure of anthracycline, taxane therapy, or is taxane-resistant and further anthracycline therapy is contraindicated. As monotherapy, metastatic or locally advanced breast cancer in patients after failure of anthracycline, taxane, and capecitabine therapy.
action: Binds directly on microtubules during active stage of G2 and M phases of cell cycle, preventing formation of microtubules, an essential part of the process of separation of chromosomes. Result: Blocks cells in mitotic phase of cell division, leading to cell death.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ixabepilone. Severe hypersensitivity reaction (Grade 3 or 4) to Cremophor, baseline neutrophil count < 1, 500 cells/mm3 or platelet count < 100, 000 cells/mm3. Combination capecitabine therapy: Serum ALT or AST > 2.5 times the upper limit of normal, bilirubin > 1 times the upper limit of normal. Caution: Diabetes, existing moderate to severe neuropathy, history of cardiovascular disease. Caution: Monotherapy: Serum ALT or AST gre.
sideEffects: Peripheral sensory neuropathy, fatigue, asthenia, myalgia, arthralgia, alopecia, nausea, vomiting.
adverseEffects: Neuropathy occurs early during treatment. 75% of new-onset or worsening neuropathy occurred during first 3 cycles. Diabetics may be at increased risk for severe neuropathy manifested as Grade 4 neutropenia. Neutropenia, leukopenia occur commonly.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BMP, LFT; pregnancy in females of reproductive potential. Question history of hepatic impairment, cardiac disease. Offer emotional support. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor for symptoms of neuropathy (burning sensation, hyperesthesia, hypoesthesia, paresthesia, discomfort, neuropathic pain). Assess skin for erythema. Monitor CBC for evidence of neutropenia, thrombocytopenia; LFT for hepatotoxicity. Assess mouth for stomatitis, mucositis. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Treatment may depress your immune system response and reduce your ability to fight infection. Report symptoms.

name: ixazomib
uses: Multiple myeloma (in combination with lenalidomide and dexamethasone) in patients who have received at least 1 prior therapy.
action: Reversibly inhibits activity of beta 5 subunit of the 20S proteasome, leading to cell cycle arrest and tumor cell death (apoptosis). Result: Inhibits tumor cells growth and metastasis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Severe hypersensitivity to ixazomib. Caution: Baseline neutropenia, thrombocytopenia. Caution: hepatic/renal impairment, chronic peripheral edema, predisposing factors to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, open wounds). Caution: Concomitant use of strong CYP3A inducers not recommended.
sideEffects: Diarrhea, constipation, nausea, vomiting, back pain, blurry vision, dry eye.
adverseEffects: Neutropenia, thrombocytopenia are expected responses to therapy. Thrombocytopenia reported in 78% of patients. Neutropenia in 67% of patients. Severe diarrhea may lead to discontinuation of treatment.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain ANC, CBC (especially platelet count), renal function test (in. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor ANC, platelet count at least monthly, more frequently during first 3 cycles; LFT in. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s with renal impairment), LFT; pregnancy test in female.

name: ixekizumab
uses: Moderate to severe plaque psoriasis6 yrs and older who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy. Active psoriatic arthritis in adults. Active ankylosing spondylitis in adults. Active nonradiographic axial spondyloarthritis with objective signs of inflammation in adults.
action: Selectively binds to and inhibits interaction of interleukin-17A receptor, a naturally occurring cytokine that is involved in inflammatory and immune response. Result: Alters biologic immune response; inhibits release of proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ixekizumab. Caution: Baseline neutropenia, thrombocytopenia. Caution: inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn’s disease, ulcerative colitis), HIV infection, concomitant immunosuppressant therapy, conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, open wounds), patients who have been exposed to tuberculosis. Caution: Concomitant use of live vaccines not recommended.
sideEffects: Injection site reactions (pain, erythema). Nausea.
adverseEffects: May increase risk of infection including tuberculosis. Infections including upper respiratory tract infection (14% of patients), nasopharyngitis (14% of patients), tinea infections (2% of patients) have occurred. Cytopenias including neutropenia (11% of patients), thrombocytopenia (3% of patients) were reported. May cause exacerbation of Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC in. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s with known history of neutropenia, thrombocytopenia. Screen for active infection. Pts should be evaluated for active tuberculosis and tested for latent infection prior to initiating treatment and periodically during therapy. Induration of 5 mm or greater with tuberculin skin testing should be considered a positive test result when assessing if treatment for latent tuberculosis is necessary.

name: ketorolac
brand: Acular, Acular LS, Acuvail, Apo-Ketorolac , Sprix, Toradol
uses: PO, Injection, Nasal: Short-term (5 days or less) mild to moderate pain. Ophthalmic: ocular itching due to seasonal allergic conjunctivitis. Treatment postop for inflammation following cataract extraction, pain following incisional refractive surgery. Migraine, severe, acute treatment (Injection).
action: Inhibits COX-1 and COX-2 enzymes, resulting in decreased prostaglandin synthesis; reduces prostaglandin levels in aqueous humor. Result: Produces analgesic, antipyretic, antiinflammatory effect; reduces intraocular inflammation.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ketorolac, aspirin, or other NSAIDs. Intracranial bleeding, hemorrhagic diathesis, incomplete hemostasis, high risk of bleeding; concomitant use of aspirin, NSAIDs, probenecid, or pentoxifylline; labor and delivery, advanced renal impairment or risk of renal failure, active or history of peptic ulcer disease, chronic inflammation of GI tract, recent or history of GI bleeding/ulceration. Perioperative pain in setting of CABG surgery. Prophylaxis before major.
sideEffects: Headache, nausea, abdominal cramps/pain, dyspepsia, diarrhea, nasal: Nasal discomfort, rhinalgia, increased lacrimation.
adverseEffects: Peptic ulcer, GI bleeding, gastritis, severe hepatic reaction (cholestasis, jaundice) occur rarely. Nephrotoxicity (glomerular nephritis, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome) may occur in patients with preexisting renal impairment. Acute hypersensitivity reaction (fever, chills, joint pain) occurs rarely.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess onset, type, location, duration of pain. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor renal function, LFT, urinary output. Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. Observe for occult blood loss. Assess for therapeutic response: relief of pain, stiffness, swelling; increased joint mobility; reduced joint tenderness; improved grip strength. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Avoid aspirin, alcohol. - Report abdominal pain, bloody stools, or vomiting blood. - If GI upset occurs, take with food, milk. - Ophthalmic: Transient.

name: labetalol
uses: Hypertension. IV for severe hypertension.
action: Blocks alpha-1, beta-1, beta-2 (large doses) adrenergic receptor sites. Result: Decreases peripheral vascular resistance, BP.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to labetalol. Bronchial asthma, history of obstructive airway disease, cardiogenic shock, uncompensated HF, second-or third-degree heart block (except in patients with functioning pacemaker), severe bradycardia, conditions associated with severe, prolonged hypotension. Caution: Compensated HF, severe anaphylaxis to allergens, myasthenia gravis, psychiatric disease, hepatic impairment, pheochromocytoma, diabetes. Caution: concurrent use with digoxin, verapamil, or dilTIAZem.
sideEffects: Drowsiness, dizziness, excessive fatigue, dyspnea, peripheral edema, depression, anxiety, constipation.
adverseEffects: May cause, aggravate HF due to decreased myocardial stimulation. Abrupt withdrawal may cause myocardial ischemia, producing chest pain, diaphoresis, palpitations, headache, tremor. May mask signs of acute hypoglycemia (tachycardia, BP changes) in diabetic patients. Rapid reduction of blood pressure may cause CVA, optic nerve infarction, ischemic changes on ECG.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess BP, heart rate immediately before drug administration (if pulse is 60/min or less or systolic BP is lower than 90 mm Hg, withhold medication, contact physician). Question history of bradycardia, HF, second-or third-degree heart block, myasthenia gravis. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BP for hypotension; heart rate. Assist with ambulation if dizziness occurs. Assess for evidence of HF: Dyspnea (particularly on exertion or lying down), night cough, peripheral edema, distended neck veins. Monitor I&O (increase in weight, decrease in urine output may indicate HF). PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Do not prematurely stop treatment (may cause or worsen HF). -.

name: lacosamide
uses: Monotherapy or Adjunct for focal (partial) onset seizures1 mo and older. Adjunct for primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures4 years of age and older.
action: Selectively enhances slow inactivation of sodium channels, stabilizing hyper-excitable neuronal membranes and inhibits neuronal firing. Result: Reduces seizure frequency.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to lacosamide. Caution: Renal/hepatic impairment, cardiac conduction problems (e.g., marked first-degree AV block, second-degree or higher AV block, sick sinus syndrome without pacemaker), myocardial ischemia, HF, patients at risk of suicide.
sideEffects: Dizziness, headache, nausea, double vision, vomiting, fatigue, blurred vision, ataxia.
adverseEffects: May increase risk of suicidal ideation, behavior. PR interval prolongation, AV block, ventricular tachyarrhythmias may occur. Sudden discontinuation may increase risk of seizures. Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS), also known as multiorgan hypersensitivity, has been reported.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain LFT, renal function test. Review history of seizure disorder (intensity, frequency, duration, level of consciousness). Initiate seizure precautions. Question history of cardiac conduction disorders, depression, suicidal ideation and behavior. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor LFT, renal function periodically. Observe for recurrence of seizure activity. Assess for clinical improvement (decrease in intensity/frequency of seizures). Assist with ambulation if dizziness occurs.

name: lamiVUDine

name: lapatinib
uses: Combination treatment with capecitabine for the human epidermal growth receptor type 2 (HER2)-overexpressing advanced or metastatic breast cancer in patients who have received prior therapy including an anthracycline, a taxane, and trastuzumab. precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to lapatinib. Caution: Baseline cytopenias, conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds), hepatic impairment, cardiac disease, HF. Caution: patients at risk for QT interval prolongation (congenital long QT syndrome, HF, medications that prolong QT interval, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia). Caution: History of treatment with anthracyclines, chest wall irradiation. Caution: Avoid concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers.

name: larotrectinib

name: lecanemab-irmb

Pts with apolipoprotein E e4 homozygotes have a higher incidence of ARIA compared to heterozygotes and noncarriers when treated with amyloid beta-directed antibodies. Symptoms of ARIA include confusion, dizziness, focal deficits, headache, nausea, visual changes, and gait difficulty.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain weight in kg. Test for ApoE e4 homozygotes and confirm presence of amyloid beta pathology prior to initiation. Obtain MRI of brain at. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor for symptoms of ARIA (aphasia, confusion, dizziness, headache, nausea, weakness, or seizure, vision changes), intracranial hemorrhage (altered mental status, aphasia, blindness, hemiparesis, unequal pupils, seizures). name: ledipasvir/sofosbuvir

name: leflunomide

name: lenvatinib

name: leucovorin

name: levalbuterol
uses: Treatment, bronchospasm due to reversible obstructive airway disease (e.g., asthma, bronchitis, emphysema).
action: Stimulates beta2-adrenergic receptors in lungs, resulting in relaxation of bronchial smooth muscle. Result: Relieves bronchospasm, reduces airway resistance.
precautions: Contraindicated: History of hypersensitivity to albuterol or levalbuterol. Caution: Cardiovascular disorders (cardiac arrhythmias, HF), seizures, hypertension, hyperthyroidism, diabetes, glaucoma, hypokalemia.

adverseEffects: Excessive sympathomimetic stimulation may cause palpitations, premature heart contraction, tachycardia, chest pain, slight increase in BP followed by substantial decrease, chills, diaphoresis, blanching of skin. Too-frequent or excessive use may decrease bronchodilating effectiveness, lead to severe, paradoxical bronchoconstriction.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess lung sounds, pulse, BP, oxygen saturation. Note color, amount of sputum. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor rate, depth, rhythm, type of respiration; quality/rate of pulse, ECG, serum potassium. Assess lung sounds for wheezing (bronchoconstriction). Observe for paradoxical bronchospasm. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Increase fluid intake (decreases lung secretion viscosity). - Rinsing mouth with water immediately after inhalation may prevent mouth/throat dryness. - Avoid excessive use of caffeine derivatives (chocolate, coffee, tea, cola, cocoa). name: levetiracetam

Observe for behavioral changes — irritability, aggression, mood changes. Monitor renal function (dose adjustment in impairment). Implement seizure precautions. Treat with adrenocortical steroids before thyroid therapy in coexisting hypothyroidism and hypoadrenalism. Children: (Undertreatment): May decrease intellectual development, linear growth. (Overtreatment): Adversely affects brain maturation, accélérâtes bone age. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Do not discontinue therapy; replacement for h.

name: lidocaine

uses: Ventricular arrhythmias (IV: VT, VF during cardiac arrest). Local/regional anesthesia. Topical analgesia (patch: postherpetic neuralgia).

name: linagliptin
uses: Adjunct for diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes alone or in combination with other antidiabetic agents.

Screen for glucose-altering conditions: fever, increased activity or stress, surgical procedures. Dietary consult for nutritional education. name: linezolid
uses: Susceptible infections due to aerobic and facultative, gram-positive microorganisms, including E. Faecium (van-comycin-resistant strains only), S. Aureus (including methicillin-resistant strains), S. Agalactiae, S. Pneumoniae (including multidrug-resistant strains), S. Pyogenes. Pneumonia (community-acquired and hospital-acquired), skin, soft tissue infections (including diabetic foot infections), bacteremia caused by susceptible vancomycin-resistant (VRE) organisms.
action: Inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding to bacterial ribosomal RNA sites, preventing formation of a functional initiation complex that is essential for bacterial translation. Result: Bacteriostatic against enterococci, staphylococci; bactericidal against streptococci.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to linezolid. Concurrent use or within 2 wks of MAOIs. Caution: History of seizures, preexisting myelosuppression, medications that may cause bone marrow depression, uncontrolled hypertension, pheochromocytoma, carcinoid syndrome, untreated hyperthyroidism, diabetes, chronic infection. nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain appropriate culture specimens for sensitivity testing prior to therapy. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. Mild GI effects may be tolerable, but increasing severity may indicate onset of antibiotic-associated colitis. Be alert for superinfection: fever, vomiting, diarrhea, anal/genital pruritus, oral mucosal changes (ulceration, pain, erythema). Monitor CBC, platelets, Hgb, chemistries. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Continue therapy for full length of treatment. - Dos.

sideEffects: Headache, injection site reaction (pain, erythema, swelling, itching, burning sensation), back pain, fatigue.
adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity reactions including angioedema, bronchospasm, hypotension, urticaria, rash were reported. Hypersensitivity reactions typically occurred hrs to days after administration. Infections including herpes zoster, influenza, UTI may occur. Unknown if treatment will influence the immunological response to helminth (parasite) infection.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain pulse rate, oxygen saturation. Auscultate lung fields. Question history of herpes zoster infection, parasitic infection, hypersensitivity reaction. Pts with preexisting helminth (parasite) infection should be treated prior to initiation. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor rate, depth, rhythm of respirations. Assess lungs for wheezing, rales. Monitor oxygen sat.

name: meropenem
uses: Bacterial meningitis: intra-abdominal infections (e.g., complicated appendicitis, peritonitis). Complicated skin/skin structure infections caused by susceptible microorgansims including S. Aureus, S. Pyogenes, S. Agalactiae, S. Pneumoniae, H. Influenzae, N. Men-ingitidis, M. Catarrhalis, E. Coli, Klebsiella, Enterobacter, Serratia, P. Aeruginosa, B. Fragilis. Cystic fibrosis (acute pulmonary exacerbat.
action: Binds to penicillin-binding proteins. Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis. Result: Bactericidal.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to meropenem, anaphylactic reactions to penicillins, cephalosporins, other beta-lactams. Caution: Renal impairment, CNS disorders (particularly with history of seizures, concurrent use with valproic acid).
sideEffects: Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, headache, inflammation at injection site, oral candidiasis, rash, pruritus.
adverseEffects: Antibiotic-associated colitis, other superinfections (abdominal cramps, severe watery diarrhea, fever) may result from altered bacterial balance in GI tract. Anaphylactic reactions have been reported. Seizures may occur in patients with CNS disorders (e.g., brain lesions, history of seizures), bacterial meningitis, renal impairment. Severe cutaneous toxicities including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, erythema multiforme, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, drug reaction.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain specimen culture. Question history of seizures; hypersensitivity, allergic reaction to penicillins, cephalosporins. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. Monitor for nausea, vomiting. Evaluate for inflammation at IV injection site. Monitor skin for cutaneous toxicities. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Report persistent diarrhea, abdominal cramps, fever.

name: mesalamine
brand: Apriso, Asacol HD, Canasa, Delzicol, Lialda, Pentasa, Rowasa, Salofalk , sfRowasa
uses: PO: Treatment, maintenance of remission of mild to moderate active ulcerative colitis. Rectal: active mild to moderate distal ulcerative colitis, proctosigmoiditis, or proctitis.
action: Exact mechanism unknown. May modulate local mediators of inflammation, may inhibit tumor necrosis factor. Result: Decreases inflammation in colon.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to mesalamine, salicylates. Caution: Active peptic ulcer, pyloric stenosis, pericarditis, myocarditis, renal/hepatic impairment, elderly.
sideEffects: Mesalamine is generally well tolerated, with only mild, transient effects, PO: Abdominal cramps/pain, diarrhea, dizziness, headache, nausea.
adverseEffects: Sulfite sensitivity may occur in susceptible patients, manifested as cramping, headache, diarrhea, fever, rash, urticaria, pruritus, wheezing. Discontinue drug immediately Hepatitis, pancreatitis, pericarditis occur rarely with oral forms.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain BUN, serum creatinine, LFT. Assess for abdominal pain, discomfort. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Encourage adequate fluid intake. Assess bowel sounds for peristalsis. Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency; record time of evacuation. Assess skin for rash, urticaria. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Report rash, fever, abdominal pain, significant diarrhea. - Avoid tasks that require alertness, motor skills until response to drug is established. - May discolor urine yellow-brown. - Suppositories stain fabrics. MetFORMIN met-for-min (Glumetza, Glycon , Riomet) BLACK BOX ALE.

name: metformin
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus: first-line pharmacologic therapy. Prevention of type 2 diabetes in high-risk individuals.
action: Decreases hepatic glucose production (gluconeogenesis). Increases insulin sensitivity in peripheral tissues.
precautions: Caution: renal impairment, alcohol use, heart failure, elderly.
sideEffects: GI disturbances (nausea, diarrhea, abdominal discomfort) — most common, especially on initiation, metallic taste.
adverseEffects: Lactic acidosis (rare but life-threatening — risk increased with renal/hepatic impairment, alcohol, iodinated contrast). Vitamin B12 deficiency with long-term use.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain fasting glucose, HbA1c, BMP (creatinine/eGFR), LFT. Hold before iodinated contrast procedures. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor blood glucose, HbA1c, renal function periodically. Watch for lactic acidosis (muscle pain, respiratory distress, unusual drowsiness). PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING Take with food to reduce GI effects. Do not drink excessive alcohol. Report unusual muscle pain or difficulty breathing immediately. Monitor blood glucose regularly.

name: methadone
uses: Oral: Moderate to severe pain when a continuous around-the-clock analgesic is needed. Detoxification/maintenance opioid addiction in conjunction with social/medical services. Injection: pain severe enough to require an opioid analgesic when alternate options are inadequate.
action: Binds with opioid receptors within CNS, causing inhibition of ascending pain pathways. Alters processes affecting analgesia, emotional response to pain; reduces withdrawal symptoms from other opioid drugs. Result: Produces generalized CNS depression.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to methadone. Severe respiratory depression, acute or severe bronchial asthma (in absence of resuscitative equipment or unmonitored setting), hypercarbia, GI obstruction including paralytic ileus (known or suspected). Caution: Renal/hepatic impairment, elderly/debilitated patients, patients at risk for QTc interval prolongation (congenital long QT syndrome, HF, medications that prolong QTc interval, hypokalemia. Caution: Hypomagnesemia), cardiovascular disease, patients at high risk.
sideEffects: Sedation, orthostatic hypotension, diaphoresis, facial flushing, constipation, dizziness, nausea, vomiting.
adverseEffects: Overdose results in respiratory depression, skeletal muscle flaccidity, cold/clammy skin, cyanosis, extreme Drowsiness progressing to seizures, stupor, coma. Early sign of toxicity presents as increased sedation after being on a stable dose. Cardiac toxicity manifested as QT prolongation, torsades de pointes. Tolerance to analgesic effect, physical dependence may occur with repeated use.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain ECG. Assess type, location, intensity of pain. Detoxification: Assess. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor vital signs 15–30 min after SQ/IM dose, 5–10 min following IV dose. Oral medication is 50% as potent as parenteral. Assess for adequate voiding. Monitor daily pattern of bowel acti. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s for opioid withdrawal. Pt should be in recumbent position before drug administration by parenteral route. Obtain vital signs before giving medication. If respirations are 12/min or less (20/min or less in children), withhold medication, contact physician.

name: methimazole
uses: Hyperthyroidism (Graves' disease, toxic nodular goiter). Thyrotoxicosis — pre-surgical or pre-radioiodine preparation. Thyroid storm (adjunct).
action: Inhibits thyroid peroxidase, blocking iodination of tyrosine residues and coupling of iodothyronines to form T3 and T4. Does NOT block release of existing stored hormone (delayed onset of effect).
precautions: Caution: hepatic disease, bone marrow suppression.
sideEffects: Rash, urticaria, pruritus, nausea, GI upset, arthralgia, headache.
adverseEffects: Agranulocytosis (most dangerous — rare, can be fatal. Typically within first 3 months). Hepatotoxicity. Hypothyroidism (over-treatment). Aplastic anemia, ANCA-positive vasculitis.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, LFT, TFTs. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor TFTs (TSH, free T4). CBC monthly for first 3 months (agranulocytosis). PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING Report sore throat, fever, mouth ulcers immediately (agranulocytosis signs). Do NOT stop without provider guidance. Monitoring labs are essential.

name: methotrexate
uses: Oncology-related: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia, breast cancer, cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, gestational trophoblastic neoplasia, head and neck cancer, meningeal leukemia, non-Hodgkin’s lymphomas, osteosarcoma. Non-oncology uses: Polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis, psoriasis, rheumatoid arthritis. Non-oncology: Atopic dermatitis, Crohn’s disease, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), termination of intrauterine.
action: Irreversibly binds to and inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, inhibiting formation of reduced folates and thymidylate synthetase, which inhibits purine/thy-midylic acid synthesis. Result: Interferes with DNA synthesis, repair, and cellular replication.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to methotrexate. Breastfeeding. For patients with psoriasis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, or rheumatoid arthritis: Pregnancy, hepatic disease, alcoholism, immunodeficiency syndrome, preexisting blood dyscrasias. Caution: Peptic ulcer, ulcerative colitis, preexisting myelosuppression, history of chronic hepatic disease, alcohol consumption, obesity, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, use with other hepatotoxic medications, concomitant use of proton pump inhibitors.
sideEffects: Nausea, vomiting, stomatitis, burning/erythema at psoriatic site (in patients with psoriasis). Occasional (3%-Diarrhea, rash, dermatitis, pruritus, alopecia.
adverseEffects: High potential for various severe toxicities. GI toxicity may produce gingivitis, glossitis, pharyngitis, stomatitis, enteritis, hematemesis. Hepatotoxicity more likely to occur with frequent small doses than with large intermittent doses. Pulmonary toxicity characterized by interstitial pneumonitis.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Rheumatoid arthritis: Assess pain, range of motion. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, BMP, LFT, urinalysis, chest X-rays, serum uric acid. Monitor for hematologic toxicity (fever, sore throat, signs of local infection, unusual bruising/bleeding from any site), symptoms of anemia (excessive fatigue, weakness). Assess skin for evidence of dermatologic toxicity. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s well hydrated, urine alkaline. Avoid recta.

name: methylergonovine
uses: Uterine atony, hemorrhage and subinvolution of uterus following delivery of placenta. Control uterine hemorrhage following delivery of anterior shoulder in second stage of labor.
action: Increases tone, rate, amplitude of contraction of uterine smooth muscle. Result: Produces sustained contractions, which shortens third stage of labor, reduces blood loss.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to methylergonovine. Hypertension, pregnancy, toxemia. Caution: Renal/hepatic impairment, coronary artery disease, patients at risk for coronary artery disease (diabetes, obesity, smoking, hypercholesterolemia), concurrent use with CYP3A4 inhibitors, occlusive peripheral vascular disease, sepsis, second stage of labor.
sideEffects: Nausea, uterine cramping, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, dizziness, diaphoresis, tinnitus.
adverseEffects: Severe hypertensive episodes may result in CVA, serious arrhythmias, seizures. Hypertensive effects are more frequent with patients susceptibility, rapid IV administration, concurrent use of regional anesthesia, vasoconstrictors. Peripheral ischemia may lead to gangrene.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain serum calcium level, BP, pulse. Assess for any evidence of bleeding before administration. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor uterine tone, bleeding, BP, pulse q15min until stable (about 1–2 hrs). Assess extremities for color, warmth, movement, pain. Report chest pain promptly. Provide support with ambulation if dizziness occurs. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Avoid smoking: Causes increased vasoconstriction. - Report increased cramping, bleeding, foul-smelling lo-chia. - Report pale, cold hands/feet (possibility of diminished circulation).

name: methylnaltrexone
uses: Injection: opioid-induced constipation in patients with advanced illness or pain caused by active cancer who require opioid dosage escalation for palliative care. Injection/tablets: opioid-induced constipation in patients with chronic pain unrelated to cancer including patients with chronic pain related to prior cancer or its treatment not requiring frequent opioid dosage escalation.
action: Blocks binding of opioids to peripheral opioid receptors within GI tract. Inhibits opioid-induced decreased GI motility and delay in GI transit time. Result: Decreases constipating effect of opioids.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to methylnaltrexone. Known or suspected GI obstruction. Pts at increased risk of recurrent GI obstruction. Caution: Renal impairment, history of GI tract lesions (e.g., peptic ulcer disease, GI tract malignancies).
sideEffects: Abdominal pain, flatulence, nausea, diarrhea, dizziness.
adverseEffects: None known.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Question characteristics of constipation, frequency of bowel movements. Assess bowel sounds. Question history of GI obstruction, perforation,. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Laxative effect usually occurs w.

name: methylphenidate
brand: Adhansia XR, Aptensio XR, Concerta, Cotempla XR-ODT, Daytrana, Jornay PM, Methylin, Quillichew ER, Q
uses: Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Narcolepsy.
action: Blocks reuptake of norepinephrine, dopamine into presynaptic neurons. Stimulates cerebral cortex and subcortical structures. Result: Decreases motor restlessness, fatigue.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to methylphenidate. Use during or within 14 days following MAOI therapy; marked anxiety, tension, agitation, motor tics; family history or diagnosis of Tourette’s syndrome, glaucoma. Metadate: Severe hypertension, HF, arrhythmia, hyperthyroidism, recent MI or angina. Caution: Hypertension, seizures, acute stress reaction, emotional instability, HF, recent MI, hyperthyroidism or thyrotoxicosis, known structural cardiac abnormality, bipolar disorder, cardiomyop.
sideEffects: Anxiety, insomnia, anorexia, dizziness, drowsiness, headache, nausea, abdominal pain.
adverseEffects: Prolonged administration to children with ADHD may delay normal weight gain pattern. Overdose may produce tachycardia, palpitations, arrhythmias, chest pain, psychotic episode, seizures, coma. Hypersensitivity reactions, blood dyscrasias occur rarely.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT ADHD: Assess attention span, impulsivity, interaction with others, distractibility. Narcolepsy: Observe/assess frequency of episodes. Question history of seizures. Assess for potential of abuse/misuse (e.g., drug seeking behavior, mental health conditions, history of substance abuse). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BP, pulse, changes in ADHD symptoms. CBC with differential should be performed routinely during therapy. If paradoxical return of attention-deficit occurs, dosage should be reduced or discontinued. Monitor growth. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Avoid tasks that require alertness, motor skills.

name: methylprednisolone
uses: Severe inflammatory conditions (asthma exacerbation, COPD, anaphylaxis adjunct). Autoimmune diseases (SLE, IBD). Organ transplant rejection. Spinal cord injury (controversial). Multiple sclerosis exacerbations.
action: Binds glucocorticoid receptors and modulates gene transcription. Potent anti-inflammatory effect: inhibits cytokine synthesis, arachidonic acid pathway, and immune cell activation.
precautions: Caution: diabetes, hypertension, peptic ulcer, infections (masks fever), psychosis, osteoporosis, prolonged use requires taper.
sideEffects: Hyperglycemia, increased appetite, mood changes, insomnia, GI upset, weight gain, fluid retention.
adverseEffects: Same as other corticosteroids with long-term use: Cushing's syndrome, adrenal suppression, osteoporosis, AVN, immunosuppression, peptic ulcer.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Blood glucose, BP, weight. Screen for active infections, TB. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor glucose closely (insulin adjustments may be needed). BP, weight. Watch for signs of infection (fever masked). Report mood/behavioral changes. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING Do NOT stop abruptly. Take with food. Report unusual weight gain, mood changes, unusual infections. Blood glucose monitoring if diabetic.

name: methylPREDNISolone sodium succinate
uses: Anti-inflammatory or immunosuppressant in the hematologic, allergic, neoplastic, dermatologic, endocrine, GI, nervous system, ophthalmic, renal, or rheumatic disorders.
action: Anti-inflammatory: Suppresses migration of polymorphonuclear leukocytes, reverses increased capillary permeability. Exerts effects on modulating carbohydrate, protein, lipid metabolism. Result: Decreases inflammation.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to methylPREDNISolone. Administration of live or attenuated virus vaccines, systemic fungal infection. IM: Idiopathic thrombocytopenia purpura. Intrathecal administration. Caution: Respiratory tuberculosis, untreated systemic infections, hypertension, HF, diabetes, GI disease (e.g., peptic ulcer), myasthenia gravis, renal/hepatic impairment, seizures, cataracts, glaucoma, following acute MI, thyroid disorder, thromboembolic tendencies, cardiovascular disease, .
sideEffects: Insomnia, heartburn, anxiety, abdominal distention, diaphoresis, acne, mood swings, increased appetite.
adverseEffects: Long-term therapy: Hypocalcemia, hypokalemia, muscle wasting (especially in arms, legs), osteoporosis, spontaneous fractures, amenorrhea, cataracts, glaucoma, peptic ulcer, HF. Abrupt withdrawal after long-term therapy: Anorexia, nausea, fever, headache, severe arthralgia, rebound inflammation, fatigue, weakness, lethargy, dizziness, orthostatic hypotension.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Question for hypersensitivity to corticosteroids, components. Obtain height, weight, BP, serum glucose, electrolytes. Check results of initial tests (tuberculosis [TB] skin test, X-rays, ECG). Question history as listed in Precautions. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor I&O, daily weight; assess for edema. Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. Check vital signs at least twice daily. Be alert for infection (sore throat, fever, vague symptoms).

name: metoclopramide
uses: GERD and gastroparesis (diabetic and post-surgical). Nausea/vomiting (chemotherapy, surgery, post-partum). Hiccups (refractory). Migraine nausea adjunct.
action: Blocks dopamine D2 receptors in the CTZ (antiemetic) and GI tract (prokinetic). Increases lower esophageal sphincter tone and gastric motility, accelerating gastric emptying.
precautions: Caution: tardive dyskinesia risk (cumulative dose/duration — black box), renal impairment, depression. Caution: Parkinson's (worsens motor symptoms).
sideEffects: Drowsiness, restlessness, dizziness, diarrhea, extrapyramidal symptoms (EPS: akathisia, dystonia).
adverseEffects: Tardive dyskinesia (irreversible involuntary movements — cumulative risk, especially >12 weeks). EPS reactions. Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (rare). Hyperprolactinemia (galactorrhea, amenorrhea).
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess nausea severity, GI motility. EPS history, depression, renal function. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Administer 30 min before meals and at bedtime. Monitor for EPS (restlessness, facial grimacing). Limit use to < 12 weeks. Monitor renal function. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING Take 30 min before meals. Report involuntary movements (arms, face, tongue). Avoid alcohol and CNS depressants. Do not use for more than 3 months.

name: metOLazone
uses: Edema due to HF, nephrotic syndrome, or impaired renal function.
action: Blocks reabsorption of sodium, potassium, chloride at distal convoluted tubule, increasing excretion of sodium, potassium, water. Result: Reduces BP, promotes diuresis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to metolazone. Anuria, hepatic coma/precoma. Caution: Hypersensitivity to sulfonamides, thiazide diuretics. Caution: Severe renal disease, severe hepatic impairment, gout, prediabetes or diabetes, elevated serum cholesterol, triglycerides.
sideEffects: Dizziness, light-headedness, headache, muscle cramps/spasm, drowsiness, fatigue, lethargy, asthenia.
adverseEffects: Vigorous diuresis may lead to profound water loss and electrolyte depletion, resulting in hypokalemia, hyponatremia, dehydration. Acute hypotensive episodes may occur. Hyperglycemia may occur during prolonged therapy. Pancreatitis, paresthesia, blood dyscrasias, pulmonary edema, allergic pneumonitis, dermatologic reactions occur rarely.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess vital signs, especially BP for hypotension. Obtain serum electrolytes. Assess skin turgor, mucous membranes for hydration status. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BP, vital signs, serum electrolytes, I&O, weight. Note extent of diuresis. Monitor for electrolyte disturbances (hypokalemia may result in weakness, tremors, muscle cramps, nausea, vomiting, altered mental status, tachycardia; hyponatremia may result in confusion, thirst, cold/clammy skin). PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Expect increased urinary frequency/volume. - Slowly go from lying to standing to reduce hypotensive effect. - Avoid.

name: metoprolol
uses: Hemodynamically stable acute myocardial infarction (AMI) to reduce CV mortality. Long-term angina pectoris. Hypertension. Stable symptomatic HF of ischemic, hypertensive, or cardio-myopathic origin to reduce rate of hospitalization in patients receiving ACE inhibitors, diuretics, and/or digoxin.
action: Selectively blocks beta1-adrenergic receptors. Decreases myocardial ischemia severity. Result: Slows heart rate, decreases cardiac output, reduces BP.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to metoprolol. Second-or third-degree heart block. Immediate-release: MI: Severe sinus bradycardia (HR < 45 beats/min), systolic BP < 100 mm Hg, moderate to severe HF, significant first-degree heart block. Immediate-release: HTN/angina: Sinus bradycardia, cardiogenic shock, overt HF, sick sinus syndrome (except with pacemaker), severe peripheral arterial disease. Extended-release: Severe bradycardia, cardiogenic shock, decompensated HF, sick s.
sideEffects: Diminished sexual function, drowsiness, insomnia, unusual fatigue/weakness, anxiety, diarrhea, constipation, nausea.
adverseEffects: Overdose may produce profound bradycardia, hypotension, bronchospasm. Abrupt withdrawal may result in diaphoresis, palpitations, headache, tremulousness, exacerbation of angina, MI, ventricular arrhythmias. May precipitate HF, MI in patients with heart disease, thyroid storm in those with thyrotoxicosis, peripheral ischemia in those with existing peripheral vascular disease. Hypoglycemia may occur in patients with previously controlled diabetes (may mask signs of hypoglycemia).
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess BP, heart rate immediately before drug administration (if pulse is 60/min or less or systolic BP is < 90 mm Hg, withhold medication, contact physician). Antianginal: Record onset, type (sharp, dull, squeezing), radiation, location, intensity, duration of anginal pain, precipitating factors (exertion, emotional stress). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Measure BP near end of dosing interval (determines whether BP is controlled throughout day). Monitor BP for hypotension, respiration for shortness of breath. Assess pulse for quality, rate, rhythm. Assess for evidence of HF: Dyspnea (especially on exertion, lying down), night cough, peripheral edema, distended.

name: metronidazole
uses: Bacterial vaginosis. Trichomoniasis. C. Difficile colitis. Intra-abdominal infections. H. Pylori eradication (combo therapy).
action: Enters microbial cells and undergoes reduction to toxic intermediates that damage DNA. Bactericidal against anaerobic bacteria and antiprotozoal.
precautions: Caution: hepatic impairment, CNS disease, blood dyscrasias.
sideEffects: Nausea, metallic taste, dry mouth, headache, dizziness, dark/reddish-brown urine.
adverseEffects: Peripheral neuropathy (prolonged use). Seizures and encephalopathy (high doses). Disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol. Pseudomembranous colitis.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, LFT. Ask about alcohol use and pregnancy. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor for CNS symptoms (seizures, dizziness, peripheral numbness). Check stool pattern. Monitor LFT in prolonged therapy. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING Avoid alcohol during and 48 hrs after treatment. Take with food to reduce GI upset. Urine may turn dark — this is normal. Complete the full course.

name: micafungin
uses: Esophageal candidiasis, candidemia, candida peritonitis, abscesses, acute disseminated candidiasis, Prophylaxis: Candida infection in patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplant. G., osteomyelitis), neutropenic fever (empiric therapy).
action: Inhibits synthesis of glucan (vital component of fungal cell formation), damaging fungal cell membrane. Result: Decreased glucan content leads to cellular lysis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to micafungin. Caution: Hepatic/renal impairment, concomitant hepatotoxic medications.
sideEffects: Nausea, headache, diarrhea, vomiting, fever, rare Dizziness, drowsiness, pruritus.
adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity reaction characterized by rash, pruritus, facial edema occurs rarely. Anaphylaxis, hemoglo-binuria, hemolytic anemia have been reported.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain renal function, LFT. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BUN, serum creatinine, CrCl, LFT. Monitor for hepatotoxicity. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Report liver problems such as bruising, confusion; dark amber or orange-colored urine; right upper abdominal pain; yellowing of the skin or eyes. - Report decreased urine output; dark, amber urine; swelling of the hands or feet. - Do not take OTC medications that are toxic to the liver (e.g., acetaminophen).

name: midazolam
uses: Sedation, anxiolytic, amnesia before procedure or induction of anesthesia, conscious sedation before diagnostic/radiographic procedure, continuous IV sedation of intubated or mechanically ventilated patients. Nasal: Acute seizure clusters that are distinct from patients’ usual seizure pattern.
action: Enhances action of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), one of the major inhibitory neurotransmitters in the brain. Result: Produces anxiolytic, hypnotic, anticonvulsant, muscle relaxant, amnestic effects.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to midazolam. Acute narrow-angle glaucoma, concurrent use of protease inhibitors (e.g., atazanavir, darunavir). Caution: Renal/hepatic/pulmonary impairment, impaired gag reflex, HF, treated open-angle glaucoma, concurrent CNS depressants, obesity, elderly, debilitated.
sideEffects: Decreased respiratory rate, tenderness at IM or IV injection site, pain during injection, oxygen desaturation, hiccups, hypotension, paradoxical CNS reaction, nausea.
adverseEffects: Inadequate or excessive dosage, improper administration may result in cerebral hypoxia, agitation, involuntary movements, hyperactivity, combativeness. Too-rapid IV rate, excessive doses, or single large dose increases risk of respiratory depression/arrest. Respiratory depression/apnea may produce hypoxia, cardiac arrest.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Resuscitative equipment, oxygen must be available. Obtain vital signs before administration. Assess level of consciousness. Question history of narrow-angle glaucoma, untreated or uncontrolled open-angle glaucoma. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor respiratory rate, oxygen saturation continuously during administration for underventilation, apnea. Monitor vital signs, level of sedation q3–5min during recovery period. Assess level of consciousness for effectiveness. Monitor for decrease of seizure activity.

name: midostaurin
uses: Adult patients with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who are FLT3 mutation-positive, as detected by an FDA-approved test (in combination with standard cytarabine and DAUNOrubicin induction and cytarabine consolidation chemotherapy). Adult patients with aggressive systemic mastocytosis (ASM), systemic mastocytosis with associated hematologic neoplasm (SM-AHN), or mast cell leukemia (MCL).
action: Inhibits multiple receptors including FLT3 receptor signaling, and cell proliferation. Result: Induces apoptosis in ITD and ITD mutant expressing leukemic cells.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to midostaurin. Caution: Baseline cytopenias. Caution: concomitant use of strong CYP3A inhibitors, strong CYP3A inducers. Caution: patients at risk for hemorrhage (e.g., history of GI bleeding, coagulation disorders, recent trauma. Caution: concomitant use of anticoagulants, NSAIDs, antiplatelet medication).
sideEffects: AML: Nausea, mucositis, stomatitis, laryngeal pain, vomiting, headache, petechiae, musculoskeletal pain.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (anemia, leukopenia, lymphopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia)isanexpectedresponseto therapy Hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis, angioedema, dyspnea, itching, flushing may occur. Infections including bronchitis, bronchopulmonary aspergillosis, colitis, cellulitis, device-related infection, erysipelas, fungal pneumonia, gastroenteritis, hepatic candidiasis, herpes zoster, nasopharyngitis, oral herpes, pneumonia, sepsis, sinusitis, splenic fungal infection, upper r.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain ANC, CBC, BMP, LFT; serum magnesium; vital signs. Ensure electrolytes are corrected prior to initiation. In females of reproductive potential, obtain pregnancy test within 7 days of initiation. Screen for active infection. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor ANC, CBC for myelosuppression. Monitor BMP for renal insufficiency, electrolyte imbalance (especially PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s taking QT interval-prolonging medications. Receive full medication history and screen for interactions. Question history as listed in Precautions. Confirm compliance of effective contraception.

name: milrinone
uses: Short-term decompensated HF with reduced ejection fraction.
action: Inhibits phosphodiesterase in Cardiac and vascular tissue. Increases cardiac output, decreases pulmonary capillary wedge pressure, vascular resistance. Result: Relaxes vascular muscle, causing vasodilation.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to milrinone. Caution: Severe obstructive aortic or pulmonic valvular disease, history of ventricular arrhythmias, atrial fibrillation/flutter, renal impairment. Caution: Not recommended in patients with acute MI.
sideEffects: Headache, hypotension, rare (< Angina, chest pain.
adverseEffects: Supraventricular/ventricular arrhythmias, nonsustained ventricular tachycardia, sustained ventricular tachycardia may occur. Ventricular fibrillation (0.2% of patients) has been documented.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain BN peptide. Assess BP, heart rate before treatment begins and during IV therapy. Assess lung sounds; observe for edema. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BP, heart rate, cardiac output, ECG, serum potassium, renal function, signs/symptoms of HF.

name: mirabegron
uses: Overactive bladder with symptoms of urinary incontinence, urgency, frequency as monotherapy or in combination with antimuscarinic agent. Neurogenic detrusor overactivity in patients 3 yrs of age and older and weighing 35 kg or greater.
action: Relaxes detrusor smooth muscle of bladder through beta3 stimulation during storage phase of urinary bladder fill-void cycle. Result: Increases bladder capacity, reduces symptoms of urinary urgency, increased voiding frequency, urge incontinence, nocturia.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to mirabegron. Caution: Bladder outlet obstruction, patients taking antimuscarinic medications (increases urinary retention), mild to moderate hepatic/renal impairment, patients at risk for QTc interval prolongation (congenital long QT syndrome, HF, medications that prolong QTc interval, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia). Caution: Not recommended in patients with severe uncontrolled hypertension (SBP equal to or > 180 mm Hg and/or DBP equal to or > 110 mm Hg).
sideEffects: Hypertension, headache, nasopharyngitis, rare (2%-Constipation, arthralgia, diarrhea, tachycardia, fatigue.
adverseEffects: Worsening of preexisting hypertension reported infrequently. UTI occurred in 6% of patients, influenza in 3%, and upper respiratory infection in 1.5%.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Receive full medication history, and screen for possible drug interactions. Monitor I&O (particularly in. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Obtain bladder scan and palpate bladder to monitor for urinary retention. Measure BP near end of dosing interval (determines whether BP is controlled throughout day). Monitor BP periodically especially in hypertensive. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Report urin.

name: mirtazapine
uses: Major depressive disorder (MDD).
action: Acts as antagonist at presynaptic alpha2-adrenergic receptors, increasing norepinephrine, serotonin neurotransmission. Has low anticholinergic activity. Result: Relieves depression.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to mirtazapine. Use of MAOIs to treat psychiatric disorders (concurrently or within 14 days of discontinuing either MAOI or mirtazapine), initiation of mirtazapine in patients receiving linezolid or IV methylene blue. Caution: Renal/hepatic impairment, elderly, seizure disorder, suicidal ideation or behavior, alcoholism, concurrent medications that lower seizure threshold, cardiovascular disease, patients at risk for QTc interval prolongation (congenital long QT syndro.
sideEffects: Drowsiness, dry mouth, increased appetite, constipation, weight gain, asthenia, dizziness, flu-like symptoms.
adverseEffects: Higher incidence of seizures than with tricyclic antidepressants (especially in patients with no history of seizures). Overdose may produce cardiovascular effects (severe orthostatic hypotension, dizziness, tachycardia, palpitations, arrhythmias). Abrupt discontinuation from prolonged therapy may produce headache, malaise, nausea, vomiting, vivid dreams. Agranulocytosis occurs rarely.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess mental status, appearance, behavior, speech pattern, level of interest, mood. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s on long-term therapy, renal function, LFT, CBC should be performed periodically. Supervise suicidal-risk.

name: mirvetuximab soravtansine-gynx
pharmacoClass: Folate receptor alpha (FRa)-directed antibody/microtubular inhibitor conjugate (ADC)
uses: Adults with folate receptor-alpha-positive, platinum-resistant epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer who have received one to three prior systemic treatment regimens.
action: An antibody/drug conjugate. Antibody is directed against folate receptor alpha (FR«), a protein highly expressed in ovarian cancer, and a conjugate (DM4), a microtubule inhibitor attached to the antibody. Result: Cell cycle arrest and apoptosis (cell death).
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to mirvetuximab soravtansine-gynx. Caution: Baseline cytopenias, mild hepatic impairment (avoid use in patients with moderate to severe hepatic impairment), interstitial lung disease (e.g., COPD, sarcoidosis, connective disease disease), conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds). Caution: History of peripheral neuropathy.
sideEffects: Blurred vision, vitreous floaters, reduced visual acuity, diplopia, accommodation disorder, keratitis, presbyopia, corneal deposits.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (anemia, leukopenia, lymphopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia) is an expected response to therapy. Ocular toxicities including corneal epithelial microcysts, dry eye, eye pain, keratopathy, photophobia, uveitis, visual impairment reported in 61% of patients. Median onset of ocular toxicities was 1.2 mos. Life-threatening interstitial lung disease, pneumonitis reported in 10% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, LFT; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Confirm compliance with effective contraception. Verify presence of folate receptor-alpha expression in tumor specimen. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s’s AIBW using formula per manufacturer guidelines. An ophthalmic examination with a slit lamp and visual acuity should be performed at.

name: mitoMYcin
uses: Disseminated adenocarcinoma of stomach, pancreas (in combination with other chemotherapy agents and as palliative treatment when other modalities have failed).
action: Alkylating agent, produces DNA cross-linking. Result: Inhibits DNA, RNA synthesis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to mitomycin. Coagulation disorders, other increased bleeding tendencies, thrombocytopenia. Caution: Myelosuppression, renal (serum creatinine > 1.7 mg/dL)/hepatic impairment, pregnancy, prior radiation treatment.
sideEffects: Fever, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, stomatitis, paresthesia, purple-colored bands on nails, rash.
adverseEffects: Marked myelosuppression results in hematologic toxicity manifested as leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and, to a lesser extent, anemia (generally occurs within 2–4 wks after initial therapy). Renal toxicity may be evidenced by increased serum BUN, creatinine levels. Pulmonary toxicity manifested as dyspnea, cough, hemoptysis, pneumonia.
