nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Question history of GI disease, ulcers, GERD. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Evaluate for therapeutic response (relief of GI symptoms). Monitor for symptoms of C. Difficile (abdominal pain, diarrhea, fever). PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Best if taken before breakfast. - Frequent, loose stool; fever, abdominal pain, blood-streaked stool may indicate infectious diarrhea and may be contagious to others.

name: paricalcitol
uses: Calcitriol: hypocalce-mia in patients with hypoparathyroidism or pseudohypoparathyroidism. Secondary hyperparathyroidism in patients with moderate to severe chronic kidney disease (CKD) not on dialysis. Hypocalcemia in patients on dialysis. (Topical): mild to moderate plaque psoriasis2 yrs and older. Doxercal-ciferol: secondary hyperparathyroidism in CKD on dialysis or in patients with stage 3 or 4 CKD not on dialysis.
action: Calcitriol: Binds to and activates the vitamin D receptor in kidney, parathyroid gland, intestine, and bone, stimulating intestinal calcium transport and absorption. Reduces parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels, improves calcium and phosphate homeostasis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to cholecalciferol, ergocalciferol. Vitamin D toxicity, hypercalcemia. Caution: Pts with malabsorption syndrome. Caution: Concurrent use with digoxin.
sideEffects: Frequencies not defined, calcitriol: Cardiac arrhythmias, headache, pruritus, hypercal-cemia, polydipsia, abdominal pain, metallic taste.
adverseEffects: Early signs of overdose manifested as weakness, headache, drowsiness, nausea, vomiting, dry mouth, constipation, muscle/bone pain, metallic taste. Later signs of overdose evidenced by polyuria, polydipsia, anorexia, weight loss, nocturia, photophobia, rhinorrhea, pruritus, disorientation, hallucinations, hyperthermia, hypertension, cardiac dysrhythmias.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain serum calcium, phosphate, PTH vitamin D level (if indicated). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor serum calcium, phosphate, PTH vitamin D level (if indicated); (therapeutic calcium level: 9–10 mg/dL). Estimate daily dietary calcium intake. Encourage adequate fluid intake. Monitor for signs/symptoms of vitamin D intoxication. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Adequate calcium intake should be maintained. - Dietary phosphorus may need to be restricted (foods high in phosphorus include beans, dairy products, nuts, peas, whole-grain products). - Oral formulations may cause hypersensitivity reactions. Avoid excessive doses. - Report signs/symptoms of hypercalcemia (h.

name: pegfilgrastim
brand: Fulphila, Neulasta, Neulasta Onpro, Nyvepria, Udenyca, Stimufend, Ziextenzo
uses: Decreases incidence of infection (as manifested by febrile neutropenia) in patients with nonmyeloid malignancies receiving myelosuppressive chemotherapy associated with febrile neutropenia. To increase survival in patients acutely exposed to myelosuppressive doses of radiation.
action: Stimulates production, maturation, and activation of neutrophils within bone marrow. Result: Increases phagocytic ability, antibody-dependent destruction; decreases incidence of infection.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to pegfilgrastim, filgrastim. Caution: Any malignancy with myeloid characteristics, sickle cell disease. Caution: The 6-mg fixed dose should not be used in infants, children, or adolescents weighing < 45 kg. Caution: Do not administer within 14 days before and 24 hrs after cytotoxic chemotherapy.
sideEffects: Bone pain, nausea, fatigue, alopecia, diarrhea, vomiting, constipation, anorexia.
adverseEffects: Capillary leak syndrome (hypoalbuminemia, hypotension, fluid overload, leukocytosis, hemoconcentration), glomerulonephritis, fatal splenic rupture may occur. Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) may occur in patients with sepsis. Serious hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis, skin rash, urticaria, erythema, flushing may occur. Fatal sickle cell crisis may occur in patients with sickle cell disease.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC prior to initiation and routinely thereafter. Question history of sickle cell disease, glomerulonephritis, splenic disease, hypersensitivity reaction to acrylic adhesive on body (injector uses acrylic adhesive). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor neutrophil count for treatment effectiveness. Monitor for hypersensitivity reactions. Assess for hypoalbuminemia, peripheral edema, respiratory symptoms (cough, dyspnea) if weight has increased by 5% (or greater) and. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s is hypotensive; may indicate capillary leak syndrome. Severe capillary leak syndrome should be treated with supportive measures (corticosteroids; monitoring of weight, BP, albumins levels) until.

name: pembrolizumab
uses: BCG-unresponsive NMIBC: Trealment of patients with Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG)-unresponsive, high-risk, nonmuscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) with carcinoma in situ (CIS), with or without papillary tumors, who are ineligible for or have elected not to undergo cystectomy. Biliary tract cancer (BTC): patients with locally advanced unresectable or metastatic BTC (in combination with gemcitabine and cisplatin). Cervical cancer: In combination with chemotherapy, with or without bevaciz.
action: Inhibits programmed cell death-1 (PD-1) activity by binding to PD-1 receptors on T cell, blocking PD-1 ligands from binding, which inhibits the negative immune regulation caused by PD-1 signaling. Induces antitumor responses. Result: Inhibits T-cell proliferation and cytokine production.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to pembrolizumab. Caution: Thyroid disease, hepatic/renal impairment, interstitial lung disease, electrolyte imbalance, hypertriglyceridemia.

name: penicillin G potassium
uses: Susceptible infections including sepsis, meningitis, endocarditis, pneumonia. Active against gram-positive organisms (except S. Aureus), some gram-negative organisms (e.g., N. Gonorrhoeae), and some anaerobes and spirochetes.
action: Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to one or more of the penicillin-binding proteins of bacteria. Result: Bactericidal.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to any penicillin. Caution: Renal/hepatic impairment, seizure disorder, hypersensitivity to cephalosporins, asthma.
sideEffects: Lethargy, fever, dizziness, rash, electrolyte imbalance, diarrhea, thrombophlebitis, seizures.
adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity reactions ranging from rash, fever, chills to anaphylaxis occur occasionally.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Question for history of allergies, particularly penicillins, cephalosporins. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Promptly report rash (hypersensitivity), diarrhea (with fever, abdominal pain, mucus, or blood in stool, may indicate antibiotic-associated colitis). Monitor I&O, urinalysis, electrolytes, renal function tests for nephrotoxicity.

name: penicillin V potassium
uses: Mild to moderately severe susceptible bacterial infections including upper respiratory tract, skin and soft tissues, Prophylaxis: rheumatic fever, pneumococcal infections (otitis media), odontogenic infection.
action: Inhibits cell wall synthesis by binding to bacterial cell membranes. Result: Bactericidal.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to any penicillin. Caution: Severe renal impairment, history of allergies (particularly cephalosporins), seizure disorder, asthma.
sideEffects: Mild hypersensitivity reaction (chills, fever, rash), nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, bleeding, allergic reaction.
adverseEffects: Severe hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, may occur. Nephrotoxicity, antibiotic-associated colitis, other superinfections (abdominal cramps, severe watery diarrhea, fever) may result from high dosages, prolonged therapy.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Question for history of allergies, particularly penicillins, cephalosporins. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor for rash (hypersensitivity), diarrhea (with fever, abdominal pain, mucus or blood in stool may indicate antibiotic-associated colitis). Be alert for superinfection: fever, vomiting, diarrhea, anal/genital pruritus, oral mucosal change (ulceration, pain, erythema). Monitor I&O, urinalysis, renal function tests for nephrotoxicity. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Continue antibiotic for full length of treatment. - Space doses evenly. - Report immediately if rash, diarrhea, bleeding, bruising, other new symptoms occur.

name: pertuzumab
uses: HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer in patients who have not received prior anti-HER2 therapy or chemotherapy for metastatic disease in combination with trastuzumab and DOCEtaxel. Neoadjuvant patients with HER2-positive, locally advanced inflammatory, or early-stage breast cancer in combination with trastuzumab and chemotherapy. Adjuvant HER2-positive early breast cancer at high risk of recurrence (in combination with trastuzumab and chemotherapy).
action: Targets human epidermal growth factor 2 (HER2), blocking ligand-initiated in-tercellular signaling, which can result in cell growth arrest and cell death. Result: Inhibits cell growth and metastasis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to pertuzumab. Caution: Cardiomyopathy, HF, history of infusion-related reaction. Caution: Prior anthracycline therapy or irradiation. Caution: Conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, immunocompromised patients, renal failure, open wounds), patients at risk for tumor lysis syndrome (high tumor burden).
sideEffects: Diarrhea, alopecia, nausea, fatigue, rash, peripheral neuropathy, anorexia, asthenia.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (anemia, leukopenia, neutropenia) is an expected response to therapy, but more severe reactions including febrile neutropenia may be life-threatening. Upper respiratory tract infection occurs in 17% of patients. Pleural effusion occurred in 5% of patients. Tumor lysis syndrome may present as acute renal failure, hypocalcemia, hyperuricemia, hyperphosphatemia.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC. Assess left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) by echocardiogram. Negative pregnancy test must be confirmed before initiating treatment. Obtain HER2 testing by an FDA-approved laboratory. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor ANC, CBC periodically. Assess LVEF at regular intervals. Monitor for symptoms of left ventricular dysfunction (arrhythmia, cough, dyspnea, peripheral edema). Monitor for infusion reactions, hypersensitivity reactions, anaphylaxis. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s closely for 60 min after.

name: pertuzumab/trastuzumab/hyaluronidase-zzxf with
uses: Neoadjuvant adults with human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive, locally advanced, inflammatory, or early-stage breast cancer (either > 2 cm in diameter or node positive) as a part of a complete treatment regimen for early breast cancer. Adjuvant adults with HER2-positive early breast cancer at high risk of recurrence. HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer (in combination with DOCEtaxel) in adults who have not received prior ant.
action: Pertuzumab targets the extracellular HER2 protein dimerization domain, in hibiting HER2 dimerization and block-ing HER downstream. Trastuzumab binds to the extracellular domain of HER2. Result: Inhibits proliferation of tumor cells overexpressing HER2 protein.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to pertuzumab, trastuzumab, hyaluronidase. Caution: Baseline cytopenias, hepatic impairment, cardiovascular disease, HF, pulmonary disease, patients at risk for interstitial lung disease (e.g., COPD, sarcoidosis, connective disease disease). Caution: conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds). Caution: treatment after anthracycline therapy.
sideEffects: Alopecia, nausea, diarrhea, asthenia, fatigue, stomatitis, myalgia, arthralgia.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (anemia, lymphopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia) is an expected response to therapy, but more severe reactions, including bone marrow depression, febrile neutropenia, may be life-threatening. May exacerbate chemotherapy-induced neutropenia. May cause cardiomyopathy, cardiac failure, and death. Other cardiac disorders may include arrhythmias, hypertension, asymptomatic decrease of LVEF.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BMP, LFT; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Confirm compliance with effective contraception. Verify presence of HER2 protein overexpression or HER2 gene amplification in tumor specimen. Administer in an environment equipped to monitor for and manage hypersensitivity reactions; verify emergency resuscitation equipment/medications are readily available. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s after completion of anthracycline therapy. Question history of cardiovascular disease, HF, pulmonary disease, prior hypersensitivity reactions. Screen for active infection. Offer emotional supp.

name: phenylephrine
uses: Nasal: Nasal congestion due to the common cold, hay fever (allergic rhinitis), or other upper respiratory allergies. Parenteral: hypotension, vascular failure in shock.
action: Acts on alpha-adrenergic receptors of vascular smooth muscle. Causes vasoconstriction of arterioles of nasal mucosa/conjunctiva; produces systemic arterial vasoconstriction. Result: Decreases mucosal blood flow, relieves congestion.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to phenylephrine. Injection: Severe hypertension, ventricular tachycardia. Oral: Use within 14 days of MAOl therapy. Caution: Injection: Elderly, hyperthyroidism, bradycardia, partial heart block, cardiac disease, HF, cardiogenic shock, hypertension. Caution: Oral: Asthma, bowel obstruction, cardiac disease, ischemic heart disease, hypertension, increased intraocular pressure, elderly, prostatic hyperplasia.
sideEffects: Nasal: Rebound nasal congestion due to overuse, especially when used longer than 3 days, mild CNS stimulation (restlessness, nervousness, tremors, headache, insomnia, particularly in those hypersensitive to sympathomimetics.
adverseEffects: Large doses may produce tachycardia, palpitations (particularly in patients with cardiac disease), dizziness, nausea, vomiting. Overdose in patients older than 60 yrs may result in hallucinations, CNS depression, seizures. Prolonged nasal use may produce chronic swelling of nasal mucosa, rhinitis. If phenylephrine 10% ophthalmic is instilled into denuded/damaged corneal epithelium, corneal clouding may result.
nursingConsiderations: INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BP, heart rate. For severe hypotension or shock states, monitor central venous pressure noninvasive hemodynamic monitoring systems. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Discontinue if adverse reactions occur. - Do not use for nasal decongestion for longer than 3 days (rebound congestion). - Discontinue if insomnia, dizziness, weakness, tremor, palpitations occur. - Nasal: Stinging/burning of nasal mucosa may occur. - Ophthalmic: Blurring of vision with eye instillation generally subsides with continued ther-.

name: phenytoin
uses: Generalized tonic-clonic seizures (grand mal), complex focal (partial) seizures, status epilepticus. Seizures following head trauma/neurosurgery. Trigeminal neuralgia.
action: Stabilizes neuronal membranes in motor cortex. Decreases influx of sodium during generation of nerve impulses. Result: Decreases seizure activity.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to phenytoin, other hydantoins. Concurrent use of delavirdine. History of acute phenytoin therapy-induced hepatotoxicity. IV (additional): Second-and third-degree AV block, sinoatrial block, sinus bradycardia, Adams-Stokes syndrome. Caution: Porphyria, diabetes, renal/hepatic impairment, patients at increased risk of suicidal behavior/thoughts, elderly, debilitated, hypoalbuminemia, cardiac disease, hypothyroidism, patients of Asian descent.
sideEffects: Drowsiness, lethargy, confusion, slurred speech, irritability, gingival hyperplasia, hypersensitivity reaction (fever, rash.
adverseEffects: Abrupt withdrawal may precipitate status epilepticus. Blood dyscrasias, osteomalacia (due to interference of vitamin D metabolism) may occur. Toxic phenytoin blood concentration (25 mcg/mL or more) may produce ataxia, nystagmus, diplopia. As level increases, extreme lethargy to comatose state occurs.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Anticonvulsant: Review history of seizure disorder (intensity, frequency, duration, LOC). Initiate seizure précautions. LFT, CBC should be performed before beginning therapy and periodically during therapy. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Repeat CBC 2 wks following initiation of therapy and 2 wks following administration of maintenance dose. Observe frequently for recurrence of seizure activity. Monitor ECG for cardiac arrhythmia. Assess for clinical improvement (decrease in intensity/frequency of seizures).

name: pioglitazone
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus as monotherapy or in combination. Insulin resistance.
action: Activates peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPAR-γ), a nuclear receptor that modulates genes for glucose and lipid metabolism. Increases peripheral insulin sensitivity in muscle and adipose tissue without stimulating insulin release.
precautions: Caution: heart failure risk (fluid retention, edema), bladder cancer risk (FDA warning with > 1 year use), osteoporosis/fracture risk (especially women), macular edema (eye changes), pregnancy.
sideEffects: Edema, weight gain, headache, myalgia, upper respiratory infection.
adverseEffects: Heart failure exacerbation (fluid retention — increase in HF hospitalizations). Bladder cancer risk (prolonged use > 1 year). Fractures (particularly distal extremities in women). Macular edema.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain LFT, weight, cardiac status, HbA1c. Assess for heart failure, bladder issues. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor weight, edema (fluid retention). LFT if symptoms. Blood glucose, HbA1c. Watch for signs of bladder cancer (hematuria). PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING Report rapid weight gain, shortness of breath, swelling (HF signs). Report blood in urine. Regular eye exams. Bone fracture risk — fall prevention important.

name: piperacillin/tazobactam
uses: Moderate to severe bacterial infections, including community-acquired/nosocomial pneumonia, intra-abdominal, pelvic, skin, and skin structure infections. Tazobactam ex-pands piperacillin activity to include beta-lactamase-producing strains of S. Aureus, H. Influenzae, Bacteroides, PsAg, Acinetobacter, Klebsiella pneumoniae, E. Coli.
action: Piperacillin: Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to penicillin-binding proteins, which inhibit the final step of peptidoglycan synthesis. Tazobactam: Inactivates bacterial beta-lactamase. Result: Bactericidal.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to piperacillin/tazobactam, any penicillin. Caution: History of allergies (especially cephalosporins, beta-lactamase inhibitors), renal impairment, seizure disorder.
sideEffects: Diarrhea, headache, constipation, nausea, insomnia, rash, vomiting, dyspepsia.
adverseEffects: Antibiotic-associated colitis, other superinfections (abdominal cramps, severe watery diarrhea, fever) may result from altered bacterial balance in GI tract. Overdose, more often with renal impairment, may produce seizures, neurologic reactions. Severe hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, occur rarely.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC; LFT in. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency; mild GI effects may be tolerable, but increasing severity may indicate onset of antibiotic-associated colitis. Be alert for superinfection: Fever, vomiting, diarrhea, anal/genital pruritus, oral mucosal changes (ulceration, pain, erythema). Monitor I&O, urinalysis. Monitor serum electrolytes, especially potassium, renal function tests. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s with hepatic impairment. Question for history of allergies, especially to penicillins, cephalosporins.

name: pomalidomide
uses: Multiple myeloma (in combination with dexAMETHasone) in patients who have received at least two prior therapies including lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor and who have demonstrated disease progression on or within 60 days of completion of the last therapy. Adults with AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma (KS) after failure of highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) or in patients with KS who are HIV negative.
action: Inhibits tumor cell proliferation and induces apoptosis (cell death) of hematopoietic cells. Enhances T-cell-and natural killer (NK) cellmediated immunity. Result: Inhibits tumor cell growth and metastasis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to pomalidomide. Pregnancy. Caution: Anemia, HF, hepatic/renal impairment, smoking, breastfeeding, or prior history of CVA, MI, DVT, PE.
sideEffects: Fatigue, constipation, nausea, diarrhea, dyspnea, back pain, peripheral edema, musculoskeletal chest pain.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (neutropenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia) is an expected outcome of therapy. May increase risk of infection such as pneumonia, upper respiratory tract infection, UTI. Neurologic events such as acute confusion, dizziness reported. Peripheral neuropathy occurred in 18% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BMP; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Receive full medication history. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, BMP. Obtain ECG for palpitations, chest pain, hypokalemia, hyperkalemia, hypocalcemia, bradycardia, ventricular arrhythmias. Immediately report dyspnea, chest pain, hypoxia, unilateral peripheral edema/pain (may indicate thromboembolic event). Perform routine neurologic assessments to screen for confusion, delirium.

name: ponatinib
uses: Adults with chronic phase (CP) chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) with resistance or intolerance to at least two prior kinase inhibitors. Accelerated phase (AP) or blast phase (BP) CML or Philadelphia chromosome-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph+ ALL) for whom no other kinase inhibitors are indicated. Adults with T315I-positive CML (chronic, accelerated, or blast phase) or T315I-positive ALL (Ph+ ALL). Not indicated for newly diagnosed chronic phase CML.
action: Inhibits viability of cells expressing native or mutant BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase, including T315I mutation, created by the Philadelphia chromosome abnormality. Result: Inhibits tumor cell growth and metastasis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ponatinib. Caution: Baseline cytopenias. Caution: conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, immunocompromised patients, open wounds), history of arterial/venous thrombosis (e.g., CVA, DVT, MI, PE), cardiac disease, cardiac conduction disorders, HF, hypertension. Caution: diabetes, electrolyte imbalance, glaucoma, hepatic impairment, hyperlipidemia, GI perforation, neuropathy (peripheral or cranial), ocular disorders, pancreatitis or alcohol abuse, history of ischemia.
sideEffects: Note: Percentages of side effects of chronic phase, accelerated phase, blast phase CML, ph+ ALL may vary, hypertension, abdominal pain, fatigue, asthenia.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (anemia, leukopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia) is an expected response to therapy, but more severe reactions including bone marrow failure, febrile neutropenia may be life-threatening. Fatal arterial occlusions including CVA, MI, stenosis of large arterial vessel of the brain, severe peripheral vascular disease requiring revascularization reported in 35% of patients. May occur within 2 wks of initiation (even at reduced doses of 15 mg/day). Coronary artery occlusion, MI occurred.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BMP, LFT, serum ionized calcium, phosphate, uric acid; vital signs; weight. Obtain pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Receive full medication history including herbal products and screen for interactions. Question history as listed in Precautions.

name: ponesimod
uses: Relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) in adults, including CLINICALly isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, and active secondary progressive disease.
action: Binds with high affinity to S1P receptor, blocking capacity of lymphocytes to move out from lymph nodes, reducing the number of lymphocytes available to the CNS. Result: May involve reduction of lymphocyte migration into the CNS, reducing inflammation.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ponesimod. Myocardial infarction, unstable angina, stroke, transient ischemic attack, decompensated heart failure requiring hospitalization, or Class III or IV heart failure in the last 6 mos. Sick sinus syndrome, Mobitz type II second-or third-degree AV block (unless patients has a functioning pacemaker). Caution: Conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, immunocompromised patients, renal failure, open wounds), baseline sinus bradycardia, hepatic impairm.
sideEffects: Hypertension, dyspnea, dizziness, cough, extremity pain, somnolence, pyrexia, vertigo.
adverseEffects: Life-threatening infections may occur. Fatal cases of cryptococcal meningitis, disseminated cryptococcal infections were reported. Herpes zoster infections reported in 5% of patients. Reactivation of herpes viral infection may cause herpes simplex encephalitis and varicella zoster meningitis.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, LFT, ECG. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s with QT interval prolongation > 500 msec; arrhythmias requiring treatment with Class Ia or Class III antiarrhythmics; unstable ischemic heart disease, HF, uncontrolled hypertension, history of cardiac arrest, CVA or TIA (> 6 mos); history of Mobitz type II second-or third-degree AV block, sick sinus syndrome, sinoatrial heart block. First-dose monitoring is recommended in.

name: potassium chloride
brand: Kaon-Cl, Klor-Con, Klor-Con M10, Klor-Con M20, Micro-K
uses: Potassium acetate, potassium bicarbonate/citrate: Treatment, hypokalemia when necessary to avoid chloride or acid/base imbalance (requires bicarbonate). Potassium chloride: Treatment, hypokalemia.
action: Necessary for multiple cellular metabolic processes. Primary action is intracellular. Result: Required for nerve impulse conduction, contraction of cardiac, skeletal, smooth muscle; maintains normal renal function, acid-base balance.
precautions: Contraindicated: Acetate: Severe renal impairment, adrenal insufficiency, hyperkalemia. Chloride: Renal failure, hyperkalemia, conditions in which potassium retention is present. Solid oral dosage form in patients in whom there is structural, pathologic cause for delay in passage through GI tract. Caution: Cardiac disease, acid-base disorders, potassium-altering disorders, digitalized patients, concomitant therapy that increases serum potassium (e.g., ACE inhibitors), renal impairment. Caution: Do not administe.
sideEffects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, flatulence, abdominal discomfort with distention, phlebitis with IV administration (particularly when potassium concentration of > 40 mEq/L is infused). Rash.
adverseEffects: Hyperkalemia (more common in ELDERLY, patients with renal impairment) manifested as paresthesia, motor weakness, cold skin, hypotension, confusion, irritability, paralysis, cardiac arrhythmias. Too-rapid infusion may cause cardiac arrhythmia, ventricular fibrillation, Cardiac arrest.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess for hypokalemia (weakness, fatigue, polyuria, polydipsia). PO form should be given with food or after meals with full glass of water, fruit juice (minimizes GI irritation). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor serum potassium, calcium, phosphate. If GI disturbance occurs, dilute preparation further or give with meals. Monitor for decreased urinary output (may be indication of renal insufficiency). Check IV site closely during infusion for evidence of phlebitis (heat, pain, red streaking of skin over vein, hardening of vein), extravasation (swelling, pain).

name: pralsetinib
uses: Non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC): adults with metastatic rearranged during transfection (RET) fusion-positive NSCLC. Thyroid cancer: adults and pediatric patients 12 yrs of age and older with advanced or metastatic RET-mutant medullary thyroid cancer (MTC) who require systemic therapy. Advanced or metastatic RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer in pediatric patients 12 yrs of age and older and adults who require systemic therapy and who are radioactive iodine-refract.
action: Inhibits wild-type RET, oncogenic RET fusions, and RET mutations Certain activating point mutations in RET or chromosomal rearrangements involving in-frame fusions of RET can result in constitutively activated chimeric RET fusion proteins, which may act as oncogenic drivers, promoting tumor cell line proliferation. Result: Demonstrates antitumor activity in cells harboring oncogenic RET fusions or mutations.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to pralsetinib. Caution: Baseline cytopenias, hepatic impairment, hypertension, conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, immunocompromised patients, renal failure, open wounds). Caution: patients at risk for bleeding (e.g., history of intracranial/GI/GU bleeding, coagulation disorders, recent trauma), interstitial lung disease (e.g., COPD, sarcoidosis, connective disease disease), tumor lysis syndrome (high tumor burden), poor wound healing (e.g., recent or planned.
sideEffects: Note: Frequency and occurrence of side effects may vary based on treatment as monotherapy or in combination with other therapies, musculoskeletal pain, constipation, hypertension, diarrhea, abdominal pain, dry mouth, stomatitis.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (anemia, lymphopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia) is an expected response to therapy. Life-threatening ILD/pneumonitis reported in 10% of patients. Grade 3 hypertension reported in 14% of patients. Serum ALT, AST elevation reported in 69% and 46% of patients, respectively.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BMP, LFT, BP; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Confirm compliance of effective nonhormonal contraception. Verify presence of a RET gene fusion (NSCLC, thyroid cancer) or specific RET gene mutation (MTC) in tumor specimens or plasma. Due to increased risk of tumor lysis syndrome, routinely assess hydration. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC for my.

name: pramipexole
uses: Mirapex: Parkinson’s disease, moderate to severe primary restless legs syndrome. Mirapex ER: Parkinson’s disease.
action: Stimulates DOPamine receptors in striatum and substantia nigra. Improves motor function. Result: Relieves signs/symptoms of Parkinson’s disease.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to pramipexole. Caution: History of orthostatic hypotension, patients at risk for hypotension, syncope, hallucinations, renal impairment (extended-release not recommended with CrCl < 30 mL/min), concomitant use of CNS depres-sants, preexisting dyskinesia, elderly patients.
sideEffects: Early Parkinson’s disease: Nausea, asthenia, dizziness, drowsiness, insomnia, constipation, advanced Parkinson’s disease: Orthostatic hypotension, extrapyramidal reactions.
adverseEffects: Vascular disease, atrial fibrillation, arrhythmias, pulmonary embolism, impulsive/compulsive behavior (pathological gambling, hypersexuality, binge eating) have been reported.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Parkinson’s disease: Assess for tremor, muscle weakness and rigidity, ataxia. Restless legs syndrome: Assess frequency of symptoms, sleep pattern. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Assess for clinical improvement. Assist with ambulation if dizziness occurs. Assess for constipation; encourage fiber, fluids, exercise. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Hallucinations may occur, especially in the elderly - Go from lying to standing slowly. - Avoid tasks that require alertness, motor skills until response to drug is established. - If nausea occurs, take medication with food. - Avoid abrupt withdrawal. - Avoid alcohol. - Report new or increased impulsive/compulsive behaviors (e.g., gamb.

name: pravastatin
uses: Adjunct to dietary therapy to reduce elevated total cholesterol (total-C), LDL-C, apoB, and triglyceride levels and to increase HDL-C in patients with primary hypercholesterolemia (heterozygous, familial and nonfamilial) and mixed dyslipidemia in adults. Adjunct to diet in children and adolescents aged 8 yrs of age and older with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia if LDL-C is 190 mg/dL or above or 160 mg/dL or above with family history of premature cardiovascular disease or presence of two or.
action: Interferes with cholesterol biosynthesis by preventing conversion of HMG-CoA reductase to mevalonate, a precursor to cholesterol. Result: Lowers LDL, VLDL cholesterol, plasma triglycerides; increases HDL.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to pravastatin. Active hepatic disease or unexplained, persistent elevations of LFT results. Pregnancy, breastfeeding. Caution: Hepatic impairment, substantial alcohol consumption. Caution: Withholding/discontinuing pravastatin may be necessary when patients is at risk for renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis, elderly.
sideEffects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, abdominal pain, headache, rhinitis, rash.
adverseEffects: Potential for malignancy, cataracts. Hypersensitivity, myopathy occur rarely. Rhabdomyolysis has been reported.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain lipid panel, LFT; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Obtain dietary history, especially fat consumption. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor serum cholesterol, triglycerides for therapeutic response. Monitor LFT. Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. Assess for rash, pruritus. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Follow special diet (important part of treatment). - Report promptly any muscle pain/weakness, especially if accompanied by - fever, malaise. - Use nonhormonal contraception. - Avoid direct exposure to sunlight. Pr.

name: prednisone
uses: Inflammatory conditions (asthma, COPD exacerbation, RA, IBD). Allergic reactions. Autoimmune diseases (SLE, multiple sclerosis). Organ transplant rejection prevention. Adrenal insufficiency.
action: Enters cells and binds to glucocorticoid receptors, modifying gene transcription. Suppresses inflammatory mediators (cytokines, prostaglandins), inhibits immune cell migration, and decreases vascular permeability.
precautions: Caution: diabetes (elevates blood glucose), peptic ulcer, hypertension, CHF, osteoporosis, infection risk (masks fever), psychiatric history, long-term use requires taper.
sideEffects: Hyperglycemia, mood changes (euphoria, irritability), increased appetite, weight gain, insomnia, fluid retention, GI upset.
adverseEffects: Long-term use: Cushing's syndrome (moon face, buffalo hump, purple striae). Adrenal suppression (HPA axis). Osteoporosis/fractures. Avascular necrosis.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain blood glucose, BP, weight, bone density. Screen for TB, infections. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor blood glucose closely. Weigh daily. BP monitoring. Watch for signs of infection (masked by steroid). PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING Do NOT stop abruptly — can cause adrenal crisis (taper required). Take with food to minimize GI upset. Report unusual weight gain, swelling, mood changes, fever. Avoid live vaccines.

name: pregabalin
uses: Lyrica: Adjunct for focal (partial) onset seizures1 mo and older. Neuropathic pain associated with diabetic peripheral neuropathy or spinal cord injury. Postherpetic neuralgia. Fibromyalgia. Lyrica CR: neuropathic pain associated with diabetic peripheral neuropathy, postherpetic neuralgia.
action: Binds to calcium channel sites in CNS tissue, inhibiting excitatory neurotransmitter release. Exerts antinociceptive, anticonvulsant activity. Result: Decreases symptoms of painful peripheral neuropathy; decreases frequency of partial seizures.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to pregabalin. Caution: HF, renal impairment, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, history of angioedema, history of suicidal ideation and behavior. Caution: Concurrent use of thiazolidine antidiabetics (e.g.
sideEffects: Dizziness, drowsiness, ataxia, peripheral edema, weight gain, blurred vision, dplopia, difficulty with concentration.
adverseEffects: Abrupt withdrawal increases risk of seizure frequency in patients with seizure disorders. Withdraw gradually over a minimum of 1 wk. May increase risk of suicidal thoughts and behavior.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Seizure: Review history of seizure disorder (type, onset, intensity, frequency, duration, LOC). Pain: Assess onset, type, location, and duration of pain. Question history of suicidal ideation and behavior. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Assess for seizure activity. Assess for clinical improvement; record onset of relief of pain. Assess for peripheral edema. Question for changes in visual acuity. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Do not abruptly stop taking drug; seizure frequency may be increased. - Avoid tasks that require alertness, motor skills until response to drug is established. - Avoid alcohol. - Seek immediate medical attention if thoughts of suic.

name: propofol
uses: Induction/maintenance of anesthesia. Continuous sedation in intubated and respiratory controlled adult patients in ICU.
action: Causes CNS depression through agonist action of GABA receptors. Result: Produces hypnosis rapidly.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to propofol, eggs, egg products, soybean or soy products. Caution: Hemodynamically unstable patients, hypovolemia, severe cardiac/respiratory disease, elevated ICP, impaired cerebral circulation, preexisting pancreatitis, hyperlipidemia, seizure disorder, elderly, debilitated. Caution: peanut allergy.
sideEffects: Involuntary muscle movements, apnea (common during induction, often lasts longer than 60 sec), hypotension, nausea, vomiting, IV site burning/stinging, twitching.
adverseEffects: Continuous infusion or repeated intermittent infusions of propofol may result in extreme drowsiness, respiratory depression, circulatory depression, delirium. Too-rapid IV administration may produce severe hypotension, respiratory depression, involuntary muscle movements. Pt may experience acute allergic reaction, characterized by abdominal pain, anxiety, restlessness, dyspnea, erythema, hypotension, pruritus, rhinitis, urticaria. May cause propofol infusion syndrome, a collection of metabolic d.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Resuscitative equipment, suction, O2 must be available. Obtain vital signs before administration. Screen for hypersensitivity to egg or soy products. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Observe for signs of wakefulness, agitation. Monitor respiratory rate, BP, heart rate, O2 saturation, depth of sedation, serum lipid, triglycerides (if used longer than 24 hrs). May change urine color to green. If continuous high-dose infusions do not properly induce sedation, consider additional sedatives (e.g., opioids, hypnotics, benzodiazepines) to achieve desired response.

name: propranolol
brand: Hemangeol, Inderal LA, Inderal XL, InnoPran XL
uses: Angina pectoris, control supraventricular arrhythmias, (e.g., atrial fibrillation/flutter), essential tremors, hypertension, ventricular tachycardia, symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, migraine headache prophylaxis, pheochromocytoma, myocardial infarction (early treatment, secondary prevention). Hemangeol: proliferating infantile hemangioma needing systemic therapy.
action: Blocks beta1-, beta2-adrenergic receptors. Result: Slows heart rate; decreases BP, myocardial contractility, myocardial oxygen demand.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to propranolol. Bronchial asthma, severe sinus bradycardia, cardiogenic shock, sick sinus syndrome, heart block > first-degree (unless patients has functional pacemaker), uncompensated HF. Hemangeol (Additional): Premature infants with corrected age younger than 5 wks, infants weighing < 2 kg; history of bronchospasm, bradycardia (< 80 beats/min), BP < 50/30 mm Hg, pheochromocytoma. Caution: Diabetes, renal/hepatic impairment.
sideEffects: Diminished sexual function, drowsiness, difficulty sleeping, unusual fatigue/weakness, bradycardia, depression, sensation of coldness in extremities, diarrhea.
adverseEffects: Overdose may produce profound bradycardia, hypotension. Abrupt withdrawal may result in diaphoresis, palpitations, headache, tremulousness. May precipitate HF, MI in patients with cardiac disease, thyroid storm in patients with thyrotoxicosis, peripheral ischemia in patients with existing peripheral vascular disease. Hypoglycemia may occur in patients with previously controlled diabetes.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess renal function, LFT. Assess BP, heart rate, immediately before administering drug (if pulse is 60/min or less or systolic BP is < 90 mm Hg, withhold medication, contact physician). Angina: Record onset, quality, radiation, location, intensity, duration of anginal pain, precipitating factors (exertion, emotional stress). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Assess pulse for quality, regularity, bradycardia. Monitor ECG for cardiac arrhythmias. Assess fingers for color, numbness (Raynaud’s). Assess for evidence of HF (dyspnea [particularly on exertion or lying down], night cough, peripheral edema, distended neck veins).

name: propylthiouracil
uses: Hyperthyroidism (preferred in first trimester of pregnancy over methimazole). Thyroid storm. When methimazole is not tolerated.
action: Inhibits thyroid peroxidase (same as methimazole). Additionally inhibits peripheral conversion of T4 to the more active T3 (by inhibiting deiodinase) — making it preferred in thyroid storm.
precautions: Caution: hepatic disease.
sideEffects: Rash, fever, arthralgia, nausea, GI upset.
adverseEffects: Hepatotoxicity including fatal liver failure (black box — more risk than methimazole, especially in adults). Agranulocytosis. ANCA-positive vasculitis. Hypothyroidism.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT LFT, CBC, TFTs. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor LFT closely. CBC for agranulocytosis. TFTs regularly. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING Report jaundice, dark urine, abdominal pain (hepatotoxicity), sore throat, fever (agranulocytosis). Do NOT use in 2nd/3rd trimester. Regular monitoring essential.

name: pyrazinamide
uses: Active TB — part of the standard 4-drug initial therapy (HRZE: INH + Rifampin + Pyrazinamide + Ethambutol) for the first 2 months.
action: Prodrug — converted to pyrazinoic acid by mycobacterial pyrazinamidase. Lowers intracellular pH to disrupt membrane transport and energy metabolism in M.
precautions: Caution: renal impairment, diabetes (impairs glucose control), alcohol use, elderly.
sideEffects: Arthralgia/myalgia, nausea, anorexia, hyperuricemia (gout risk), elevated LFTs, photosensitivity.
adverseEffects: Hepatotoxicity (most serious — potentially fatal). Severe gout exacerbation. Sideroblastic anemia (rare). Thrombocytopenia.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain LFT, uric acid, BMP. Gout history. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor LFT monthly. Uric acid levels. Watch for arthralgia (hyperuricemia). Jaundice, abdominal pain — hepatotoxicity signs. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING Take with food to reduce GI upset. Report joint pain, yellowing of eyes/skin, dark urine. Avoid alcohol. Protect from sun (photosensitivity).

name: pyRIDostigmine
uses: Myasthenia gravis.
action: Prevents destruction of acetylcholine by inhibiting the enzyme acetylcholin-esterase, enhancing impulse transmission across neuromuscular junction. Result: Produces miosis; increases intestinal, skeletal muscle tone; stimulates salivary, sweat gland secretions.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to pyRIDostigmine. Mechanical, intestinal or urinary obstruction. Caution: Bronchial asthma, COPD, bradycardia, seizure disorder, hyperthyroidism, cardiac arrhythmias, peptic ulcer, renal impairment.
sideEffects: Miosis, increased Gl/skeletal muscle tone, bradycardia, constriction of bronchi/ureters, diaphoresis, increased salivation, headache, rash.
adverseEffects: Overdose may produce cholinergic crisis, manifested as increasingly severe descending muscle weakness (appears first in muscles involving chewing, swallowing, followed by muscle weakness of shoulder girdle, upper extremities), respiratory muscle paralysis, followed by pelvis girdle/leg muscle paralysis. Requires withdrawal of all cholinergic drugs and immediate use of 1–4 mg atropine sulfate IV for adults, 0.01 mg/kg for infants and CHILDREN younger than 12 yrs.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Larger doses should be given at time of greatest fatigue. Assess muscle strength before testing for diagnosis of myasthenia gravis and following drug administration. Avoid large doses in. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Have facial tissues readily available at. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s with megacolon, reduced GI motility.

name: quetiapine
uses: Schizophrenia. Bipolar disorder (manic and depressive episodes). MDD (adjunctive). Generalized anxiety disorder.
action: Antagonizes dopamine D2, serotonin 5-HT2A, histamine H1, and adrenergic alpha-1 receptors. Broad receptor profile accounts for antipsychotic, sedative, and mood-stabilizing effects.
precautions: Caution: elderly dementia patients (black box), metabolic effects (diabetes, dyslipidemia), QT prolongation, cataracts (slit lamp exam advised), cardiovascular disease, seizures.
sideEffects: Somnolence (significant — major side effect), dizziness, dry mouth, constipation, weight gain, orthostatic hypotension.
adverseEffects: Tardive dyskinesia. Metabolic syndrome (new-onset diabetes, dyslipidemia, weight gain). QT prolongation. Cataracts (lens changes).
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Weight, BMI, fasting glucose/lipids, BP, ECG. Eye exam for cataracts. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor metabolic parameters regularly. Assess for EPS, NMS. Fall precautions (sedation + orthostasis). Annual eye exam. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING Take with or without food. XR tablets: take without food. Rise slowly. Avoid driving until tolerance to sedation established.

name: quinapril
uses: Hypertension. Used alone or in combination with other antihypertensives. Adjunct for HE.
action: Suppresses renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, preventing conversion of Angiotensin I to angiotensin II, a potent vasoconstrictor. Lower angiotensin II causes an increase in plasma renin activity and decreased aldosterone secretion. Result: Reduces peripheral arterial resistance, BP.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to quinapril. History of angioedema from previous treatment with ACE inhibitors, concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with diabetes. Concomitant use with neprilysin inhibitor (e.g., sacubitril) or within 36 hrs of switching to or from neprilysin inhibitor. Caution: Renal impairment, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with outflow tract obstruction, major surgery, HF, hypovolemia, unstented bilateral renal artery stenosis, hyperkalemia, concurrent potassium suppleme.
sideEffects: Fréquent: Headache, dizziness, fatigue, vomiting, nausea, hypotension, chest pain, cough.
adverseEffects: Excessive hypotension (“first-dose syncope”) may occur in patients with HF, those who are severely salt/volume depleted. Angioedema, hyperkalemia occur rarely. Agranulocytosis, neutropenia may occur in patients with collagen vascular disease (scleroderma, systemic lupus erythematosus), renal impairment. Nephrotic syndrome may occur in patients with history of renal disease.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain renal function test. Obtain BP immediately before each dose in addition to regular monitoring (be alert to fluctuations). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BP for hypotension; renal function, serum potassium, WBC. Assist with ambulation if dizziness occurs. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s with prior renal disease, urine test for protein by dipstick method should be made with first urine of day before beginning therapy and periodically thereafter.

name: raloxifene
uses: Prevention/osteoporosis in postmenopausal women. Reduces risk of invasive breast cancer in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis and postmenopausal women at high risk for invasive breast cancer.
action: Selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) that binds to estrogen receptors, increasing bone mineral density. Blocks estrogen effects in breast/uterus. Result: Reduces bone resorption, increases bone mineral density, reduces incidence of fractures.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to raloxifene. Active or history of venous thromboembolic events, such as deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), retinal vein thrombosis; women who are or may become pregnant, breastfeeding. Caution: Cardiovascular disease, renal/hepatic impairment, patients at risk for thrombosis (immobility, indwelling venous catheter/access device, morbid obesity, genetic hypercoagulable conditions), unexplained uterine bleeding, elevated triglycerides in response.
sideEffects: Hot flashes, flulike symptoms, arthralgia, sinusitis, weight gain, nausea, myalgia, pharyngitis.
adverseEffects: Thromboembolic events (DVT, pulmonary embolism, superficial thrombophlebitis) may occur, especially in patients with immobility. May increase risk of uterine bleeding, hypertriglyceridemia. Death due to stroke.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain lipid panel. Question history of thrombosis (CVA, DVT, PE). Question for possibility of pregnancy. Drug should be discontinued 72 hrs before and during prolonged immobilization (postop recovery, prolonged bed rest). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor serum total cholesterol, total calcium, phosphate, total protein, albumin, bone mineral density, platelet count. Diligently monitor for CVA (aphasia, blindness, confusion, paresthesia, hemiparesis, syncope), DVT (arm/leg pain, swelling), pulmonary embolism (chest pain, dyspnea, hypoxia, tachycardia). PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Avoid prolonged restrict.

name: ramelteon
uses: Insomnia in patients who experience difficulty with sleep onset.
action: Selectively targets melatonin receptors thought to be involved in maintenance of circadian rhythm underlying normal sleep-wake cycle. Result: Prevents insomnia characterized by difficulty with sleep onset.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ramelteon. Concurrent fluvoxaMlNE therapy, history of angioedema with previous ramelteon therapy. Caution: Depression, other psychiatric conditions, alcohol consumption, other CNS depressants, moderate hepatic impairment, severe sleep apnea, COPD. Caution: concomitant strong CYP1A2 inhibitors (e.g., fluvoxaMINE).

name: ramipril
uses: Hypertension. Used alone or in combination with other antihypertensives. HF following MI. Reduce risk of heart attack, stroke at increased risk of developing major cardiovascular events.
action: Suppresses renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system. Blocks conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II, increases plasma renin activity, decreases aldosterone secretion. Result: Reduces peripheral arterial resistance, decreasing BP.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ramipril, other ACE inhibitors. History of ACE inhibitor-induced Angioedema, concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with diabetes. Concomitant use or within 36 hrs of switching to or from a neprilysin inhibitor (e.g., sacubitril). Caution: Renal impairment, elderly, collagen vascular disease, hyperkalemia, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with outflow tract obstruction. Caution: unstented unilateral, bilateral renal artery stenosis. Caution: severe aortic stenosis. Caution: before, during.
sideEffects: Cough, headache, dizziness, fatigue, nausea, asthenia, palpitations, insomnia.
adverseEffects: Excessive hypotension (“first-dose syncope”) may occur in patients with HF, severely salt or volume depleted. Angioedema, hyperkalemia occur rarely. Agranulocytosis, neutropenia may occur in patients with collagen vascular disease (scleroderma, systemic lupus erythematosus), renal impairment. Nephrotic syndrome may occur in patients with history of renal disease.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain BP immediately before each dose, in addition to regular monitoring (be alert to fluctuations). Renal function tests should be performed before beginning therapy. Question history of hypersensitivity reaction, angioedema. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s with prior renal disease, urine test for protein (by dipstick method) should be made with first urine of day before beginning therapy and periodically thereafter.

name: ramucimmab
uses: Gastric/gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma: As a single agent or in combination with PACLitaxel, for advanced or metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma with disease progression on or after prior fluoropyrimidine-or platinum-containing chemotherapy. Non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC): In combination with DOCEtaxel, for metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer with disease progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy. In combination with.
action: Binds vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) receptor 2 and blocks binding of VEGF ligands, VEGF-A, VEGF-C, and VEGF-D. Result: Inhibits/reduces tumor vascularity and growth.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ramucirumab. Caution: History of arterial/venous thromboembolism (e.g., MI, cardiac arrest, CVA, cerebral ischemia), hepatic cirrhosis, electrolyte imbalance, hypertension, GI bleeding/perforation, chronic/unhealed wounds. Caution: baseline neutropenia, thrombocytopenia.
sideEffects: Hypertension, diarrhea, headache. Liainucirumab plus PACLitaxel: Fatigue, peripheral edema, stomatitis.
adverseEffects: Fatal hemorrhagic events including GI bleeding occurred in 3.4% of patients receiving single agent and in 4.3% of patients receiving combo therapy. GI perforations occurred in 0.7% of patients receiving single agent and in 1.2% of patients receiving combo therapy Thromboembolic events including arterial thromboembolism, CVA, MI reported in 1.7% of patients. Severe hypertension occurred in 8% of patients receiving single agent and in 15% of patients receiving combo therapy despite medical management. Severe infusion-related reacti.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BMP, vital signs; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Question history of CVA, hepatic impairment/cirrhosis, hypertension, MI, prior hypersensitivity reaction. Offer emotional support. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, serum electrolytes, vital signs. Persistent diastolic hypertension may indicate hypertensive emergency. Obtain ECG for arrhythmia, chest pain, palpitation. Consider RPLS in. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s with altered mental status, confusion, headache, seizure, visual disturbances. Screen for GI bleeding, GI perforation. Notify physician if any CTCAE toxicities occur. Monitor for hypersensitivity reaction.

name: rasagiline
uses: Signs/symptoms of Parkinson’s disease as initial monotherapy or as adjunct therapy with or without levodopa.
action: Irreversibly and selectively inhibits monoamine oxidase type B, an enzyme that plays a major role in catabolism of DOPamine. Inhibition of DOPamine depletion reduces symptomatic motor deficits of Parkinson’s disease. Result: Reduces symptoms of Parkinson’s disease; appears to delay disease progression.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to rasagiline. Concurrent use with methadone, traMADol, meperidine, MAOIs within 14 days of rasagiline, cyclobenzaprine, dextromethorphan, or St. John’s wort. Caution: Hepatic impairment (avoid use in moderate to severe impairment). Caution: cardiovascular, cerebrovascular disease, baseline hypotension. Caution: Avoid foods high in tyramine. Caution: Do not use within 5 wks of stopping FLUoxetine.
sideEffects: Headache, nausea, orthostatic hypotension, weight loss, dyspepsia, dry mouth, arthralgia, depression.
adverseEffects: Increase in dyskinesia (impaired voluntary movement), dystonia (impaired muscular tone) occurs in 18% of patients, angina occurs in 9%. Gastroenteritis, conjunctivitis reported in 3% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain LFT, BP. Receive full medication history and screen for interactions. Question history of severe hepatic impairment, cardiovascular disease. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BP Assess for clinical reversal of symptoms (improvement of tremor of head/hands at rest, mask-like facial expression, shuffling gait, muscular rigidity). If hallucinations or dyskinesia occurs, symptoms may be eliminated if levodopa dosage is reduced. Hallucinations generally are accompanied by confusion and, to a lesser extent, insomnia. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Orthostatic hypotension may occur more frequently after starting therapy. - Avoid tasks that require alertness, mot.

name: rasburicase
uses: Initial uric acid levels in patients with leukemia, lymphoma, and solid tumor malignancies who are receiving chemotherapy expected to result in tumor lysis and subsequent elevation of plasma uric acid.
action: A urateoxidase enzyme that converts uric acid into allantoin (an inactive metabolite of uric acid). Does not inhibit formation of uric acid. Result: Decreases uric acid levels.
precautions: Contraindicated: History of anaphylaxis or severe hypersensitivity to rasburicase. Prior rasburicase-associated drug reactions including hemolysis, methemoglobinemia. History of G6PD deficiency. Caution: Pts at high risk for G6PD deficiency (e.g. Caution: Mediterranean, or Southeast Asian descent).
sideEffects: Vomiting, fever, nausea, headache, abdominal pain, constipation, diarrhea, mucositis.
adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity reactions occurred in 4.3% of patients including injection irritation, peripheral edema, urticaria, pruritus. Anaphylaxis, hemolysis, methemoglobinemia occurred in < 1%. Pulmonary hemorrhage, respiratory failure, supraventricular arrhythmias, ischemic coronary artery disorders, sepsis, abdominal, gastrointestinal infections occurred in > 2% of patients. Anti-rasburicase antibodies reported.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain uric acid level; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Question for history of prior hypersensitivity reactions. Assess G6PD deficiency risk in potential candidates. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor uric acid levels. If hypersensitivity reaction occurs, stop infusion and immediately notify physician. Screen for clinical tumor lysis syndrome, hemolysis, methemoglobinemia. Follow strict procedure when collecting uric acid levels. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Report any allergic reaction, bronchospasm, chest pain or tightness, cough, difficulty breathing, dizzin.

name: regorafenib
uses: Colorectal cancer: metastatic colorectal cancer in patients who have been previously treated with fluoropyrimidine/oxaliplatin/irinotecan-based chemotherapy, anti-VEGF or anti-eGFR therapy GI stromal tumors: Locally advanced, unresectable, or metastatic GI stromal tumor previously treated with imatinib and SUNItinib. Hepatocellular carcinoma: hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) previously treated with sorafenib.
action: Inhibits tyrosine kinase activity involved with tumor angiogenesis, oncogenesis, and maintenance of tumor microenvironment. Result: Inhibits tumor cell growth and metastasis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to regorafenib. Caution: Mld to moderate hepatic impairment (not recommended with severe hepatic impairment), hypertension (not recommended with severe or uncontrolled hypertension), recent surgical/dental procedures, chronic open wounds/ulcers, hemoptysis, concomitant warfarin therapy, cardiovascular disease, recent MI.
sideEffects: Asthenia/fatigue, anorexia, diarrhea, mucositis, weight loss, hypertension, dysphonia, generalized pain.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (lymphopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia) is an expected response to therapy. May cause GI perforation, GI fistula formation. Hemorrhaging of respiratory, GI, genitourinary tracts reported in 21% of patients. Hypertension (30% of patients) may lead to hypertensive crisis.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BMP, LFT; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Assess recent surgical/dental procedures. Obtain full medication history including herbal products. Question for history of hypertension, hepatic impairment, cardiovascular disease. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BP, CBC, serum electrolytes, urinalysis. Monitor LFT q2wks for 2 mos, then monthly; or every wk if elevated. Persistent diastolic hypertension may indicate hypertensive emergency. Obtain ECG for palpitation, chest pain, hypokalemia, hyperkalemia, hypocalcemia, bradycardia, ventricular arrhythmias.

name: remdesivir
uses: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) in adults and pediatric patients (28 days of age and older and weighing at least 3 kg) with positive results of direct SARS-CoV-2 viral testing, who are hospitalized, or who are not hospitalized and have mild-to-moderate COVID-19 and are at high risk for progression to severe COVID-19.
action: Inhibits SARS-CoV-2 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, essential for viral replication. Distributes into cells and metabolizes into active nucleoside triphosphate metabolite, which competes for incorporation into RNA chains, resulting in chain termination. Result: Inhibits viral replication of coronavirus associated with COVID-19.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to remdesivir. Caution: Renal impairment, hepatic disease. Caution: Avoid concomitant use of chloroquine phosphate, hydroxychloroquine.
sideEffects: Nausea, injection site erythema.
adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis, angioedema, bradycardia, diaphoresis. Dyspnea. Fever. Hypertension, hypotension, hypoxia, nausea, rash, shivering, tachycardia wheezing have occurred. Grade 1 or 2 transaminase elevations were reported. Seizure activity, acute kidney occur rarely.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain vital signs, renal function test (BUN, serum creatinine; CrCl, eGFR), LFT, prothrombin time. Confirm positive test for SARS-CoV-2. Question history of renal impairment, hepatic disease. Auscultate lung sounds. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor vital signs, eGFR, LFT, prothrombin time. Assess for hypersensitivity reactions, especially during initial doses. Monitor I&Os. Assess for acute kidney injury, especially in critically ill. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s (decreased urinary output, edema, flank pain, seizures); hepatic injury (abdom.

name: reslizumab
uses: Add-on maintenance patients with severe asthma, aged 18 yrs and older, and with an eosinophil phenotype.
action: Inhibits signaling of interleukin-5 cytokine, reducing production and survival of eosinophils responsible for asthmatic inflammation and pathogenesis. Decreases number of asthma exacerbations, . Result: Prevents inflammatory process.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to reslizumab. Caution: History of helminth (parasite) infection. Caution: long-term use of corticosteroids. Caution: Not indicated for treatment of other eosinophilic conditions. Caution: relief of acute bronchospasm, status asthmaticus, exercise-induced bronchospasm.
sideEffects: Oropharyngeal pain, myalgia.
adverseEffects: Life-threatening anaphylaxis reported in < 1% of patients. Hypersensitivity reactions including bronchospasm, dyspnea, hypoxia, rash, urticaria, vomiting usually occurred during infusion or within 20 min after completion. < 1% of patients reported at least one malignant neoplasm within 6 mos of initiation. Unknown if treatment will influence the immunologic response to helminth (parasite) infection. Immunogenicity (auto-reslizumab antibodies) reported in 5% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain serum CPK. Verify presence of eosinophil phenotype. Question History of hypersensitivity reaction. Therapy should be administered in a healthcare setting by medical professionals who are trained and prepared to readily manage anaphylaxis.

name: rezafungin
uses: Treatment who have limited or no alternative options for the candidemia and invasive candidiasis.
action: Inhibits synthesis of glucan (vital component of fungal cell formation), damaging fungal cell membrane. Result: Causes lysis of fungal cells.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to rezafungin or other echinocandins. Caution: Hepatic impairment, patients with serious underlying medical conditions taking multiple concomitant medications. Caution: Not studied in patients with endocarditis, osteomyelitis, meningitis due to Candida.
sideEffects: Pyrexia, diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, abdominal pain, constipation, tremors.
adverseEffects: Infusion reactions, including chest tightness, flushing, nausea, urticaria, warming sensation, were reported. May cause photosensitivity. May increase hepatic enzymes. Pts with serious underlying medical conditions taking multiple concomitant medications may be at risk for clinically significant hepatic abnormalities.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain LFT. Obtain specimen culture and other laboratory data (e.g., histopathology, nonculture diagnostics) prior to initiation. Treatment may be initiated before cultures have resulted; however, antifungal therapy should be adjusted after specimen culture and laboratory data have resulted. Assess occurrence of infusion reactions prior to each dose. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor LFT as clinically indicated. Check results of specimen culture and laboratory data to verify if continued treatment is warranted. Monitor for rea.

name: ribavirin
uses: Chronic hepatitis C virus infection in patients with compensated hepatic disease in combination with other medications.
action: Inhibits replication of viral RNA, DNA, influenza virus RNA polymerase activity; interferes with expression of messenger RNA. Result: Inhibits viral protein synthesis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ribavirin. Hemoglobinopathies (e.g., sickle cell anemia), men whose female partner is pregnant, women of childbearing age who are pregnant or may become pregnant. Concomitant use of didanosine. Caution: Baseline anemia, cardiac/pulmonary disease, elderly, renal impairment, history of sarcoidosis, psychiatric illness.
sideEffects: Hemolytic anemia, dizziness, headache, fatigue, fever, insomnia, irritability, depression.
adverseEffects: Cardiac arrest, apnea, ventilator dependence, bacterial pneumonia, pneumonia, pneumothorax occur rarely. If treatment exceeds 7 days, anemia may occur.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC with differential, pretreatment and monthly pregnancy test for women of childbearing age. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor Hgb, Hct, platelets, LFT, I&O, fluid balance carefully. Check hematology reports for anemia due to reticulocytosis when therapy exceeds 7 days. Assess skin for rash. Monitor BP, respirations; Assess lung sounds. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Report immediately any difficulty breathing, itching/swelling/redness of eyes, severe abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea, unusual bleeding/bruising. - Female.

name: ribociclib
uses: Adults with hormone receptor (HR)-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer in combination with an aromatase inhibitor as initial endocrine-based therapy. Or with fulvestrant as initial endocrine-based therapy or following disease progression on endocrine therapy in men or postmenopausal women.
action: Blocks retinoblastoma protein phosphorylation and prevents progression through cell cycle, resulting in arrest of G1 phase. Result: Inhibits tumor growth.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ribociclib. Caution: Baseline cytopenias, hepatic impairment. Caution: Avoid concomitant use of strong CYP3A inhibitors, strong CYP3A inducers, QTc interval-prolonging medications. Caution: Avoid use in patients with or at risk for QTc prolongation (e.g., congenital long QT syndrome, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia. Caution: uncontrolled, significant cardiac disease including MI, HF, unstable angina, bradyarrhythmias).
sideEffects: Nausea, fatigue, diarrhea, alopecia, vomiting, constipation, headache, back pain.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (anemia, leukopenia, lymphopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia) is an expected response to therapy, but more severe reactions, including febrile neutropenia, may be life-threatening. CTCAE Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia reported in 60% of patients. Severe hepatotoxicity reported in 10% of patients. QTc interval prolongation, infections including UTI may occur.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain ANC, CBC, BMP, LFT, vital signs, weight; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Obtain ECG (note QTc interval). Initiate treatment only in. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor ANC, CBC for myelosuppression; LFT for hepatotoxicity q2wks for the first 2 cycles, then prior to each subsequent cycle, then as clinically. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s with QTc interval < 450 msec. Question history of cardiac disease, cardiac conduction disorders, hepatic impairment. Receive full medication history including herbal products and screen for interactions. Screen for risk of bleeding, QTc interval prolongation, active infection.

name: rifampin
uses: Active TB (always in combination). Latent TB with isoniazid. Meningococcal prophylaxis. Staphylococcal infections (combination). Leprosy (combination).
action: Inhibits bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, blocking bacterial RNA synthesis and causing cell death. Bactericidal against M.
precautions: Caution: hepatic disease, alcohol use. Caution: Potent CYP3A4 inducer — causes multiple drug interactions (oral contraceptives, warfarin, HIV drugs, corticosteroids).
sideEffects: Red-orange discoloration of urine, sweat, tears, saliva, feces (harmless but expected). Nausea, GI upset, headache.
adverseEffects: Hepatotoxicity. Flu-like syndrome with intermittent dosing. Thrombocytopenia. Renal failure (rare).
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain LFT, CBC. Review all medications for CYP interactions. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor LFT monthly. Watch for jaundice, elevated bilirubin. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING Body fluids (urine, sweat, tears) will turn orange-red — this is normal and harmless. Soft contact lenses will be permanently stained. Oral contraceptives become ineffective — use alternative contraception. Take on empty stomach.

name: rimegepant
uses: Migraines with or without aura in adults. Preventive episodic migraine in adults.
action: Binds to and inhibits calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) receptor. Result: Relieves migraine headache.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to rimegepant. Caution: Not indicated for prevention of migraine.
sideEffects: Nausea.
adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity reactions including dyspnea, severe rash reported in < 1% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Question characteristics of migraine headaches (onset, location, duration, possible precipitating symptoms). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Evaluate for relief of migraine headaches (photophobia, phonophobia, nausea, vomiting, pain, dizziness, fogginess). Monitor for hypersensitivity reactions. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Allergic reactions such as difficulty breathing, severe rash may occur. If allergic reaction occurs, seek immediate medical attention. - There is a high risk of interactions with other medications. Do not take newly prescribed medications unless approved by prescriber who originally started therapy.

name: ripretinib
uses: Adults with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) who have received prior treatment with three or more kinase inhibitors (including imatinib).
action: Inhibits KIT proto-oncogene receptor tyrosine kinase and platelet-derived growth factor receptor A (PDGFRA) kinase signaling, including wild-type, primary, secondary mutations of KIT and PDGFRA. Result: Inhibits tumor growth.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ripretinib. Caution: Baseline hematologic cytopenias, hepatic impairment, dermatologic disease, cardiovascular disease, hypertension, HF. Caution: conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, immunocompromised, open wounds). Caution: recent surgical incision, poorly healed wounds. Caution: Do not initiate in patients with uncontrolled hypertension.
sideEffects: Alopecia, fatigue, nausea, abdominal pain, constipation, myalgia, diarrhea, decreased appetite.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (anemia, neutropenia) is an expected response to therapy. PPES, a chemotherapy-induced skin condition that presents with redness, swelling, numbness, skin sloughing of the hands and feet, reported in 21% of patients. New primary malignancies including cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, keratoacanthoma were reported. Grade 1–3 hypertension reported in 14% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC; BP; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Verify use of effective contraception. Question history of cardiovascular disease, hypertension, HF, dermatologic disease, hepatic impairment. Assess LVEF by echocardiogram. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, BP throughout therapy. Assess for drug toxicities if discontinuation or dose reduction of concomitant CYP3A inhibitor is unavoidable.

name: risankizumab-rzaa
uses: Moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy. Active psoriatic arthritis in adults. Moderately to severely active Crohn’s disease in adults.
action: Selectively binds to p19 subunit of inter-leukin-23 (IL-23) and inhibits interaction with IL-23 receptor. IL-23 is a cytokine that is involved in inflammatory and immune response. Result: Alters biologic immune response; reduces inflammation of psoriatic lesions.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to risankizumab. Caution: Conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, immunocompromised patients, renal failure, open wounds), prior exposure to tuberculosis or use in patients who reside or travel to areas where TB is endemic. Caution: Avoid use during active infection. Caution: Concomitant use of live vaccines not recommended.
sideEffects: Headache, tension Headache, sinus headache, fatigue, asthenia, injection site reactions (bruising, erythema, extravasation.
adverseEffects: Upper respiratory tract infections (bacterial, viral, unspecified) including nasopharyngitis, pharyngitis, rhinitis, sinusitis, tonsillitis reported in 13% of patients. Tinea infections reported in 1% of patients. Serious infections including cellulitis, herpes zoster, osteomyelitis, sepsis occurred in < 1% of patients. Immunogenicity (auto-risankizumab antibodies) reported in 24% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Consider completion of age-appropriate immunizations prior to initiation. Pts should be evaluated for active tuberculosis and tested for latent infection prior to initiation and periodically during therapy. Induration of 5 mm or greater with tuberculin skin testing should be considered a positive test result when assessing if treatment for latent tuberculosis is necessary. Screen for active infection or chronic infections. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Assess skin for improvement of lesions. Monitor for symptoms. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s’s willingness to self-inject medication. Teach proper injection techniques.

name: risedronate
uses: Actonel: Paget’s disease of bone. Treatment/osteoporosis in postmenopausal women, glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (daily dose 7.5 mg predniSONE or greater). Osteoporosis in men. Atelvia: osteoporosis in postmenopausal women.
action: Inhibits bone resorption by action on osteoclasts or osteoclast precursors. Paget’s disease: Inhibition of bone resorption causes a decrease (but more normal architecture) in bone formation. Result: Osteoporosis: Decreases bone resorption (indirectly increases bone mineral density).
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to risedronate, other bisphosphonates (e.g., alendronate); inability to stand or sit upright for at least 30 min; abnormalities of esophagus that delay esophageal emptying; hypocalcemia. Caution: GI diseases (duodenitis, dysphagia, esophagitis, gastritis, ulcers [drug may exacerbate these conditions]), severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min).
sideEffects: Arthralgia, rash, diarrhea, constipation, nausea, abdominal pain, dyspepsia, flulike symptoms.
adverseEffects: Overdose produces hypocalcemia, hypophosphatemia, significant GI disturbances, osteonecrosis of jaw.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess symptoms of Paget’s disease (bone pain, bone deformities). Hypocalcemia, vitamin D deficiency must be corrected before therapy begins. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Check serum electrolytes (especially calcium, ionized calcium, phosphorus, alkaline phosphatase levels). Monitor I&O, BUN, creatinine in. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Expected benefits occur only when medication is taken with full glass (6–8 oz) of plain water first thing in the morning and at least 30 min before first food, beverage, medic.

name: risperidone
uses: Schizophrenia (adults and adolescents ≥13 yrs). Bipolar disorder mania. Irritability associated with autism spectrum disorder.
action: Blocks dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT2A receptors. Antagonism at D2 reduces positive symptoms; 5-HT2A blockade reduces negative symptoms and EPS.
precautions: Caution: elderly with dementia-related psychosis (black box — increased mortality risk), QT prolongation, cardiovascular disease, diabetes risk, seizures, renal/hepatic impairment.
sideEffects: Weight gain, sedation, orthostatic hypotension, EPS (tremor, akathisia), hyperprolactinemia, constipation, dizziness.
adverseEffects: Tardive dyskinesia (long-term use). Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS — hyperthermia, rigidity, altered consciousness). Metabolic syndrome (glucose dysregulation, dyslipidemia). Stroke in elderly (black box warning for dementia patients).
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain weight, BMI, fasting glucose, lipids, BP. Assess mental status, suicide risk. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor vital signs. Assess for EPS (involuntary movements) and NMS (fever, rigidity, altered consciousness). Monitor metabolic panel, weight, blood glucose regularly. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING Rise slowly to avoid falls from orthostatic hypotension. Report fever, muscle stiffness, confusion immediately (NMS). Do not abruptly stop. Medication may take weeks for full effect.

name: rivaroxaban
uses: Reduce risk of stroke/systemic embolism in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation. Deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE). Reduce risk of recurrence of DVT/PE. Prophylaxis: DVT, which may lead to PE, in patients undergoing knee or hip replacement surgery. Prophylaxis: venous thromboembolism (VTE) in acutely ill medical patients. Reduce risk of cardiovascular events in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) or peripheral artery disease (PAD), including patients after revascularization.
action: Selectively and reversibly blocks active site of factor Xa, a key factor in the intrinsic and extrinsic pathway of blood coagulation cascade. Inhibits platelet activation and fibrin clot formation. Result: Inhibits blood coagulation.
