name: tucatinib
uses: Adults with advanced unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer (in combination with trastuzumab and capecitabine), including patients with or without brain metastases, who have received one or more prior anti-HER2-based regimens in the metastatic setting. Adults with RAS wild-type HER2-positive unresectable or metastatic colorectal cancer (in combination with trastuzumab) that has progressed following treatment with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinoteca.
action: Highly selective for HER2 kinase domain. Inhibits HER2 phosphorylation, causing downstream inhibition of MAPK and AKT signaling and cell proliferation. Result: Shows antitumor activity in HER2-expressing tumor cells and inhibits the growth of HER2-expressing tumors.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to tucatinib. Caution: Baseline anemia, hepatic/renal impairment, dehydration, conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds). Caution: concomitant use of CYP3A substrates, P-glycoprotein substrates, moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors. Caution: Avoid concomitant use of strong CYP2C8 inhibitors.
sideEffects: Note: Frequency and occurrence of side effects may vary based on combination regimen, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, stomatitis, oropharyngeal pain/discomfort, oral ulceration/blistering, decreased appetite.
adverseEffects: Anemia is an expected response to therapy. Life-threatening diarrhea may cause dehydration, electrolyte imbalance, hypotension, acute kidney injury, and death. Median onset of diarrhea was 12 days. Severe hepatotoxicity may occur Palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia syndrome (PPES), a chemotherapy-induced skin condition that presents with redness, swelling, numbness, skin sloughing of the hands and feet, reported in 63% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BMP, LFT; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Confirm compliance of effective contraception. Confirm HER2-positive status. Question history of hepatic/renal impairment. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor LFT q3wks (or more frequently in. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s with hepatotoxicity). Monitor CBC, renal function, electrolytes periodically. An increase of serum creatinine > 0.4 mg/dL from.

name: ublituximab-xiiy
uses: Adults with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS), to include clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, and active secondary progressive disease.
action: A CD20-directed cytolytic antibody that targets CD20-expressing B cells (plays a role in pathogenesis of MS) and binds to them, triggering a series of immunological reactions that ultimately lead to cell death, removing them from circulation. Result: Reduces progression of MS.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ublituximab-xiiy. Active hepatitis B virus (HBV) confirmed by positive test for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and anti-HBV tests. Caution: Prior treatment-related infusion reactions. Caution: Pts who test positive for hepatitis B core antibody (HBcAb+) or are carriers of HBV (HBsAg+). Caution: Not recommended in patients with active infection.
sideEffects: Extremity pain, insomnia, fatigue.
adverseEffects: Life-threatening infections, including bacterial, fungal, viral infection, upper and lower respiratory tract infections, herpes virus infection, have occurred. Infections reported in 56% of patients. Infusion reactions, including anaphylaxis, chills, erythema, headache, influenzalike illness, nausea, pyrexia, tachycardia, throat irritation, may be life-threatening. HBV reactivation may occur, which may result in fulminant hepatitis, hepatic failure, death.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Confirm compliance with effective contraception. Obtain HBV screening, quantitative serum immunoglobulin prior to initiation. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s who are negative for HBsAg and positive for hepatitis B core antibody (HBcAb+) or are carriers of HBV (HBsAg+), consult hepatology prior to and during treatment.

name: ubrogepant
uses: Migraines with or without aura in adults.
action: Exact mechanism of action unknown. Binds to and inhibits calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) receptor. Result: Relieves migraine headache.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ubrogepant. Concomitant use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Caution: Hepatic/renal impairment. Caution: Not indicated for prevention of migraine. Caution: Avoid concomitant use of strong CYP3A4 inducers.
sideEffects: Nausea, somnolence, dry mouth.
adverseEffects: None known.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Question characteristics of migraine headaches (onset, location, duration, possible precipitating symptoms). Receive full medication history and screen for interactions. Question history of hepatic/renal impairment. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Evaluate for relief of migraine headaches (photophobia, phonophobia, nausea, vomiting, pain, dizziness, fogginess). PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - There is a high risk of interactions with other medications. Do not take newly prescribed medications unless approved by prescriber who originally started therapy. Do not take herbal products (especially John’s wort) or ingest grapefruit products. - Avoid tasks that require alertness,.

name: umeclidinium
uses: Long-term, once-daily maintenance airflow obstruction in patients with COPD.
action: Inhibits muscarinic M3 receptor in lungs, resulting in relaxation of bronchial smooth muscle. Result: Relieves bronchospasm, reduces airway resistance, improves bronchodilation.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to umeclidinium. Severe hypersensitivity to milk proteins or any drug components. Caution: Bladder neck obstruction, myasthenia gravis, narrow-angle glaucoma, prostatic hypertrophy, urinary retention. Caution: Not recommended in patients with acutely deteriorating COPD requiring emergent relief of acute symptoms.
sideEffects: Nasopharyngitis, upper respiratory tract infection, cough, arthralgia, viral respiratory tract infection, pharyngitis, myalgia, abdominal pain.
adverseEffects: Life-threatening asthma-related events, bronchospasm, worsening of COPD-related symptoms have been reported. Hypersensitivity reactions may occur (especially in patients with undiagnosed severe milk protein allergy or allergy to products containing lactose). Worsening of narrow-angle glaucoma (eye pain, blurry vision, visual halos, colored images in association with red eyes from conjunctival congestion and corneal edema) may occur. May cause worsening of urinary retention, especially in patients with prostatic hyper.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain O2 saturation, vital signs; pulmonary function test, if applicable. Assess respiratory rate, depth, rhythm. Assess lung sounds for wheezing. Screen for concomitant use of anticholinergic medications. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Routinely monitor O2 saturation, vital signs. Auscultate lung sounds and monitor for symptom improvement. Recommend discontinuation of short-acting beta2-agonists while on long-term therapy. Monitor for COPD deterioration, narrow-angle glaucoma, u. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s with narrow-angle glaucoma.

name: upadacitinib
uses: Active non-radiographic axial spondy-loarthritis: adults with active non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis with objective signs of inflammation who have had an inadequate response or intolerance to TNF blocker therapy. Ankylosing spondylitis: active ankylosing spon-dylitis in adults who have had an inadequate response or intolerance to one or more TNF blockers. Atopic dermatitis: refractory, moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis12.
action: Inhibits JAK enzymes, which are intra-cellular enzymes involved in stimulating hematopoiesis and immune cell function via signaling pathway. Result: Reduces inflammation, tenderness, swelling of joints; slows or prevents progressive joint destruction in rheumatoid arthritis (RA).
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to upadacitinib. Caution: Baseline cytopenias, hepatic/renal impairment, elderly, uncontrolled hyperlipidemia. Caution: history of arterial or venous thrombosis (CVA, DVT, MI, PE). Caution: patients at risk for thrombosis (immobility, indwelling venous catheter/access device, morbid obesity, underlying atherosclerosis, genetic hypercoagulable conditions), recent travel or residence in TB-or mycosis-endemic areas. Caution: history of chronic opportunistic infections (bacterial, invasive fung.
sideEffects: Nausea, cough, pyrexia.
adverseEffects: Neutropenia, lymphopenia may increase risk of infection. Serious and sometimes fatal infections (bacterial, mycobacterial, invasive fungal, viral, other opportunistic infections) may occur. Serious infections may include cellulitis, cryptococcosis, esopha-geal candidiasis, herpes zoster, pneumonia, pneumocystosis, TB. Upper respiratory tract infections (laryngitis, nasopharyngitis, pharyngitis, pharyngotonsillitis, rhinitis, sinusitis, tonsillitis, viral infection) reported in 14% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, LFT, lipid panel; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Confirm compliance of effective contraception. Evaluate for active TB and test for latent TB infection. An induration of 5 mm or greater with purified protein derivative (PPD) is considered a positive result when assessing for latent TB. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s with latent TB. Screen for active infection. Question history of arterial/venous thrombosis, hepatic/renal impairment; chronic infections including HIV, hepatitis B or C virus, herpes zoster. Assess risk of GI perforation.

name: ustekinumab
uses: Adults, children 6 yrs or older with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy. Adults, children 6 yrs or older with active psoriatic arthritis. Adults with moderate to severe active Crohn’s disease. Adults with moderate to severe active ulcerative colitis.
action: Binds to and interferes with proinflammatory cytokines, interleukin-12, and interleukin-23, reducing these proinflammatory signalers. Result: Shows clinical improvement of psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to us-tekinumab. Caution: Prior malignancies (especially skin cancer), patients who resided or traveled to endemic areas. Caution: conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds), history of chronic opportunistic infections (especially bacterial, invasive fungal, mycobacte-rial, protozoal, viral infections including herpes zoster, TB). Caution: Avoid use of live vaccines.
sideEffects: Nasopharyngitis, upper respiratory tract infection, headache, fatigue, diarrhea, back pain, dizziness, pruritus.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Conduct dermatological exam; record characteristics of psoriatic lesions. Assess degree of abdominal pain, cramping; usual bowel movement patterns, stool characteristics in. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING Evaluate for active TB and test for latent infection. An induration of 5 mm or greater with purified protein derivative (PPD) is considered a positive result when assessing for latent TB. Screen for active infection; history of chronic, opportunistic infections. Question history of prior malignancies.

name: valACYclovir
uses: Herpes zoster (shingles) in immunocompetent adults. Initial and recurrent genital herpes in immunocompetent adults. Recurrent genital herpes and transmission of genital herpes in immunocompetent adults. Suppression of genital herpes in HIV-infected patients. Herpes labialis (cold sores)12 yrs and older. Chickenpox in immunocompetent children 2–17 yrs of age.
action: Converted to acyclovir by intestinal/hepatic metabolism. Competes for viral DNA polymerase; inhibits incorporation into viral DNA. Result: Inhibits DNA synthesis and viral replication.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to acyclovir, valACYclovir. Caution: Renal impairment, dehydration, elderly. Caution: concomitant use of nephrotoxic medications.
sideEffects: Herpes zoster: Nausea, headache, genital herpes: Headache, herpes zoster: Vomiting, diarrhea, constipation (50 yrs and older), asthenia, dizziness (50 yrs and older). Genital herpes: Nausea.
adverseEffects: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura/hemolytic uremic syndrome (TTP/HUS) was reported in patients with advanced HTV-1 disease and also allogenic bone marrow or renal transplant. Acute renal failure reported in elderly. Patients with dehydration. History of renal impairment.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Tissue cultures for herpes zoster, herpes simplex should be obtained before giving first dose (therapy may proceed before results are known). Assess medical history, especially HIV infection, bone marrow or renal transplantation, renal/hepatic impairment. Assess characteristics, frequency of lesions. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, LFT, renal function in. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Drink plenty of fluids. - Do not touch lesions w.

name: valproic acid
brand: Apo-Divalproex Depakote, Depakote ER, Depakote Sprinkle
uses: Depakote: manic episodes associated with bipolar disorder. Mono-therapy and adjunctive therapy of complex focal (partial) seizures and simple and complex absence seizures. Adjunct for patients with multiple seizure types including absence seizures. Prophylaxis: migraine headaches. Depakote ER: Acute manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar disorder, with or without psychotic features.
action: Directly increases concentration of inhibitory neurotransmitter gamma-ami-nobutyric acid (GABA). Result: Decreases seizure activity, stabilizes mood, prevents migraine headache.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to val-proic acid. Active hepatic disease, urea cycle disorders, known mitochondrial disorders caused by mutation in mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma (POLG). Children under 2 yrs of age suspected of having POLG-related disorder. Migraine prevention in pregnant women and women of reproductive potential who are not using effective contraception. Caution: Children younger than 2 yrs. Caution: Hepatic impairment, patients at risk for hepatotoxicity (e.g., cirrhosis, concomit.
sideEffects: Epilepsy: Abdominal pain, irregular menses, diarrhea, transient alopecia, indigestion, nausea, vomiting, tremors.
adverseEffects: Thrombocytopenia-associated bleeding, hyperammonemia, hypothermia were reported. Fatal hepatic failure may occur (particularly within the first 6 mos of treatment) and may be preceded by anorexia. Facial edema, lethargy malaise, weakness. Vomiting. Life-threatening pancreatitis may occur, which may include hemorrhage with rapid deterioration from initial symptoms to death. May increase risk of suicidal ideation and behavior.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, LFT. Question history of suicidal ideation and behavior. Anticonvulsant: Review history of seizure disorder (intensity, frequency, duration, level of consciousness). Initiate safety measures, quiet dark environment. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, LFT, serum ammonia. Monitor for symptoms of DRESS. Diligently assess for suicidal ideation and behavior; new onset or worsening of anxiety, depression, mood disorder.

name: valsartan
uses: Hypertension alone or in combination with other antihypertensives1 yr and older. HF (NYHA Class II-IV). Reduce mortality in high-risk patients (left ventricular failure/dysfunction) following MI.
action: Directly antagonizes angiotensin II receptors. Blocks vasoconstrictor, aldo-sterone-secreting effects of angiotensin II, inhibiting binding of angiotensin II to AT1 receptors. Result: Produces vasodilation, decreases peripheral resistance, decreases BP.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to val-sartan. Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with diabetes. Caution: Concurrent use of potassium-sparing diuretics or potassium supplements, mild to severe hepatic impairment, unstented bilateral/unilateral renal artery stenosis, renal impairment, significant aortic/mitral stenosis, elderly.
sideEffects: Insomnia, fatigue, heartburn, abdominal pain, dizziness, headache, diarrhea, nausea.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain renal function test; pregnancy in females of reproductive potential. Obtain BP prior to each dose. Assess medication history (especially diuretic). Question for history of hepatic/renal impairment, renal artery stenosis, severe HF. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor renal function, serum electrolytes periodically. Monitor BP. Assess for for hypotension (dizziness, nausea, tachycardia, syncope, weakened pulse). Ensure adequate hydration. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Use effective contraception to avoid pregnancy - Report heart problems (difficulty breathing, palpitations, swelling of extremities), symptoms of low blood pressure (cold, clammy skin; dizziness, fa.

name: vancomycin
uses: Systemic: sever infections (e.g., bloodstream, bone, lower respiratory tract, skin, and skin structure) caused by susceptible strains of methicillin-resistant staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Empiric therapy of infections when MRSA is suspected. Infective endocarditis: Treatment due to Corynebacteria (diphtheroids), Enterococcal, Staphylococcal, Streptococcal organisms. PO: C. Difficile-associated diarrhea. Enterocolitis caused by S. Aureus (including MRSA).
action: Binds to bacterial cell walls, altering cell membrane permeability, inhibiting RNA synthesis. Result: Bactericidal.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to vancomycin. Caution: Renal impairment, elderly, dehydration, patients at risk for extravasation (e.g., peripheral IV catheters, midline catheters, elderly, poor peripheral vasculature), concomitant use of other ototoxic, nephrotoxic medications.
sideEffects: PO: Bitter/unpleasant taste, nausea, vomiting, mouth irritation (with oral solution). Parenteral: Phlebitis, thrombophlebitis, pain at peripheral IV site, dizziness, vertigo.
adverseEffects: Nephrotoxicity (acute kidney injury, acute tubular necrosis, renal failure), ototoxic-ity (temporary or permanent hearing loss) may occur. Too-rapid infusion may cause red man syndrome, a common adverse reaction characterized by pruritus, urticaria, erythema, angioedema, tachycardia, hypotension, myalgia, macu-lopapular rash (usually appears on face, neck, upper torso). Cardiovascular tox-icity (cardiac depression, arrest) occurs rarely. Onset usually occurs within 30 min of start of infusion, r.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Avoid other ototoxic, nephrotoxic medications if possible. Obtain culture, sensitivity test before giving first dose (therapy may begin before results are known). Consider placement of central venous line/PICC line. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor serum renal function tests, I&O. Assess skin for rash. Check hearing acuity, balance. Monitor BP carefully during infusion.

name: vandetanib
uses: Symptomatic or progressive medullary thyroid cancer in patients with un-resectable locally advanced or metastatic disease.
action: Inhibits tyrosine kinases including epidermal growth factor (EGF) and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF). Blocks intracellular signaling, angiogenesis, and cellular proliferation. Result: Inhibits tumor cell growth and survival.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to vandetanib. Congenital long QT syndrome. Caution: Baseline cytopenias, patients at risk for QTc interval prolongation (congenital long QT syndrome, HF, medications that prolong QTc interval, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia), hy-pothyroidism, cerebrovascular disease, moderate to severe renal/hepatic impairment, hypertension, uncompensated HF, history of torsades de pointes.
sideEffects: Diarrhea/colitis, rash, dermatitis acneiform/acne, nausea, headache, fatigue, anorexia, abdominal pain.
adverseEffects: Prolonged QT interval resulting in torsades de pointes, ventricular arrhythmias, sudden cardiac death have been reported. Frequent diarrhea may result in electrolyte imbalances. Severe skin reactions, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, have been reported. Interstitial lung disease (ILD) or pneumonitis reported (may result in respiratory-related death).
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BMP, LFT; ECG; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Question for history of congenital long QT syndrome, HF, arrhythmias, hepatic/renal impairment, seizures, CVA, hemor-rhagic events, HTN. Obtain full medication history and screen for interactions. Offer emotional support. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, serum electrolytes. Obtain ECG during wks 2–4, wks 8–12, then every 3 mos thereafter. Obtain ECG for palpitations, chest pain, hypokale-mia, hyperkalemia, hypocalcemia, bra-dycardia, ventricular arrhythmias, syncope. Report any respiratory changes including dyspnea, cough (may indicate ILD).

name: varenicline
uses: PO: Aid to smoking-cessation treatment. Nasal spray: dry eye disease.
action: Prevents nicotine stimulation of meso-limbic dopamine system associated with nicotine addiction. Result: Decreases desire to smoke.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to va-renicline. Caution: Renal impairment, history of suicidal ideation or preexisting psychiatric illness, bipolar disorder, depression, schizophrenia, patients at risk for seizures (e.g., head trauma, seizure disorder).
sideEffects: Nausea, insomnia, headache, abnormal dreams, constipation, abdominal discomfort, fatigue, dry mouth.
adverseEffects: Abrupt withdrawal may cause irritability, sleep disturbances in 3% of patients. Hypertension, angina pectoris, arrhythmia, bradycardia, coronary artery disease, gingivitis, anemia, lymphade-nopathy occur rarely. May cause bizarre behavior, suicidal ideation. May increase risk for seizure activity.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Screen, evaluate for coronary heart disease (history of MI, angina pec-toris), cardiac arrhythmias, suicidal ideation. Assess smoking pack/day history. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Discontinue use if cardiovascular symptoms occur or worsen. Monitor for psychiatric symptoms (changes in behavior, mood, level of interest, appearance). Assess for cravings, noncompliance with cessation. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Initiate treatment 1 wk before quit-smoking date. - Take with food and with full glass of water. - Report persistent nausea, insomnia. - Seek immediate medical attention if thoughts of suicide, new onset or worsening of anxiety, depression, or changes in mood.

name: vasopressin
uses: Vasoconstriction: To increase blood pressure in adults with vasodilatory shock who remain hypotensive despite fluids and catecholamines. Central diabetes insipidus, cadaveric organ recovery.
action: Stimulates a family of arginine vaso-pressin (AVP) receptors. Result: Increases systemic vascular resistance and mean arterial BP; increases water permeability at renal tubules, causing a decreased urine volume and increased osmolality; causes smooth muscle contraction in GI tract.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to vasopressin. Caution: Seizure disorder, migraine, asthma, vascular disease, renal/cardiac disease, goiter (with cardiac complications), arteriosclerosis, nephritis, elderly.
sideEffects: Pain at injection site (with vasopressin tannate). Abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dizziness, diaphoresis, pale skin, circum-oral pallor.
adverseEffects: Anaphylaxis, MI, water intoxication have occurred. Elderly, very young are at higher risk for water intoxication. May increase risk of ischemia (cardiac, mesenteric, limb, skin). Extravasation may cause tissue necrosis.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain serum electrolytes; urine specific gravity in. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor I&O closely, restrict intake as necessary to prevent water intoxication. Weigh daily if indicated. Check BP, pulse frequently. Monitor serum electrolytes, urine specific gravity. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Report headache, chest pain, shortness of breath, other symptoms. - Stress importance of I&O. - Avoid alcohol. - Report symptoms of water intoxi.

name: vedolizumab
uses: Moderate to severe active ulcerative colitis, active Crohn’s disease.
action: Binds to T-lymphocyte integrin receptors and blocks the interaction with mucosal addressin cell adhesion molecule-1 (MAdCAM-1). Inhibits migration of memory T-lymphocytes across the en-dothelium into inflamed GI parenchymal tissue. Result: Reduces chronic inflammation of colon.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to vedoli-zumab. Caution: Hepatic impairment, patients who resided or traveled to endemic areas. Caution: conditions predisposing to infection (eg., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds), history of chronic opportunistic infections (especially bacterial, invasive fungal, mycobacterial, protozoal, viral infections including herpes zoster, TB), prior malignancies. Caution: Preexisting or recent-onset CNS demye-linating disorders including multiple sclerosis.
sideEffects: Nasopharyngitis, headache, arthralgia, nausea, pyrexia, upper respiratory tract infection, fatigue, cough.
adverseEffects: Infusion-related reactions, including anaphy-laxis, characterized by bronchospasm, dyspnea, flushing, hypotension, laryngeal edema, nausea, pyrexia, tachycardia, wheezing, vomiting, reported in < 1% of patients. May increase risk of severe infections such as anal abscess, cytomegaloviral colitis, giardiasis, Listeria meningitis, Salmondla sepsis, TB, UTI, which may lead to fatal sepsis. PML (weakness, paralysis, vision loss, aphasia, cognition impairment) has occurred rarely. However, immunoc.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, LFT; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Screen for active infection; history of chronic, opportunistic infections. Question history of prior malignancies. Consider completion of age-appropriate immunizations prior to initiation.

name: vemurafenib
uses: Unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a BRAF V600E mutation as detected by FDA-approved test. Erdheim-Chester disease (ECD) in patients with a BRAF V600E mutation.
action: Inhibits kinase activity of certain mutated forms of BRAF. Result: Blocks tumor cell proliferation in melanoma with the mutation.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to vemurafenib. Caution: Hepatic impairment, patients at risk for QTc interval prolongation (congenital long QT syndrome, HF, medications that prolong QTc interval, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia), elderly, prior radiation therapy.
sideEffects: Arthralgia, alopecia, fatigue, rash, nausea, diarrhea, hyperkeratosis, headache.
adverseEffects: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cuSCC) and keratoacanthomas reported in 24% of patients. Pts at increased risk of cuSCC include elderly patients, patients with prior skin cancer, chronic sun exposure. Hypersensitivity reactions including erythema, hypotension, anaphylaxis reported. Mild to severe photosensitivity was reported.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain BMP;ECG; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Confirm presence of BRAF V600E mutation. Review history for previous radiation therapy. Assess skin for moles, lesions, papilloma, and perform full dermatologic exam. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor ECG 15 days after initiation, then monthly for first 3 mos, then q3mos thereafter. Routinely assess skin during treatment and for 6 mos after discontinuation. Immediately report any new skin lesions. Obtain ECG for palpitations, chest pain.

name: venetoclax
uses: Monotherapy or in combination with riTUXimab for patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) or small lymphocytic leukemia (SLL) with or without 17p deletion who have received at least one prior therapy. Newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) (in combination with azaciti-dine, decitabine, or low-dose cytarabine) in patients 75 yrs of age or older, or with co-morbidities precluding use of intensive induction chemotherapy.
action: Selectively binds to and inhibits anti-apop-totic protein BCL-2 overexpressed in CLL cells and AML cells, restoring process of apoptosis. Result: Inhibits tumor cell growth and metastasis.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to venetoclax. Concomitant use of strong CYP3A inhibitors at initiation and during ramp-up phase. Caution: Baseline cytopenias, concomitant use of moderate CYP3A inhibitors, P-gp inhibitors. Caution: conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompro-mised patients, open wounds), hepatic/renal impairment, electrolyte imbalance. Caution: history of gout. Caution: patients at high risk for tumor lysis syndrome (high tumor burden).

name: venlafaxine
uses: Depression. Generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), social anxiety disorder (SAD). Panic disorder, with or without agoraphobia.
action: Potentiates CNS neurotransmitter activity by inhibiting reuptake of serotonin, nor-epinephrine, and, to lesser degree, DO-Pamine. Result: Relieves depression.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to venlafaxine. Use of MAOIs intended to treat psychiatric disorders concurrently or within 14 days of discontinuing MAOI. Initiation of MAOI to treat psychiatric disorder within 7 days of discontinuing venlafaxine, initiation in patients receiving line-zolid or IV methylene blue. Caution: Seizure disorder, renal/hepatic impairment, patients at high risk for suicide, recent MI, mania, volume-depleted patients, narrow-angle glaucoma, HF, hyperthyroidism, abnormal platelet fu.
sideEffects: Nausea, drowsiness, headache, dry mouth, dizziness, insomnia, constipation, diaphoresis.
adverseEffects: Sustained increase in diastolic BP of 10–15 mm Hg occurs occasionally. Serotonin syndrome (agitation, confusion, hallucinations, hyperreflexia), neuroleptic malignant syndrome (muscular rigidity, fever, cognitive changes), suicidal ideation have occurred.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain weight, BP. Assess appearance, behavior, speech pattern, level of interest, mood. Assess risk of suicide. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor signs/symptoms of depression, BP, weight. Assess sleep pattern for evidence of insomnia. Check during waking hours for drowsiness, dizziness, anxiety; provide assistance as necessary. Assess appearance, behavior, speech pattern, level of interest, mood for therapeutic response. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Take with food to minimize GI distress. - Do not increase, decrease, suddenly stop medication. - Avoid tasks that require alertne.

name: verapamil
uses: Parenteral: supraventricular tachyarrhythmias (SVT, rapid conversion to sinus rhythm), temporary rapid ventricular rate in atrial flutter/fibrillation. PO: angina at rest (e.g., vasospastic angina, unstable angina, chronic stable angina). Ventricular rate at rest and during stress in chronic atrial flutter and/or fibrillation. Hypertension. Prophylaxis: repetitive paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT).
action: Inhibits calcium ion entry across cardiac, vascular smooth-muscle cell membranes, dilating coronary arteries, peripheral arteries, arterioles. Decreases total peripheral vascular resistance by vasodilation. Result: Decreases heart rate, myocardial contractility;slows SA, AV conduction.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to verapamil. Atrial fibrillation/flutter in presence of accessory bypass tract (e.g., Wolff-Parkinson-White, Lown-Ganong-Levine syndromes), severe left ventricular dysfunction, cardiogenic shock, second-or third-degree heart block (except with pacemaker), hypotension (SBP < 90 mm Hg), sick sinus syndrome (except with pacemaker). IV (additional): Current use of IV beta-blocking agents, ventricular tachycardia. Caution: Renal/hepatic impairment, concom.

name: vibegron
uses: Overactive bladder in adults with symptoms of urge urinary incontinence, urgency, and urinary frequency.
action: Relaxes detrusor smooth muscle during bladder filling, increasing bladder capacity. Result: Relives urinary incontinence, urgency, frequency.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to vibegron. Caution: Pts at risk for urinary retention (e.g., bladder outlet obstruction, concomitant use of muscarinic antagonists). Caution: Concomitant use of digoxin.
sideEffects: Headache, diarrhea, nausea, dry mouth, hot flush.
adverseEffects: Urinary retention may occur, especially in patients with bladder outlet obstruction or taking concomitant muscarinic antagonist. Upper respiratory tract infection, including nasopharyngitis, may occur.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain digoxin level in. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor for symptoms of urinary retention (abdominal pain, bladder distension, hesitancy). Obtain bladder scan in. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Treatment may cause retention of urine. Report symptoms of urinary retention (abdominal pain, bladder distension, hesitancy). - Pts taking digoxin may require more frequent monitoring of digoxin levels. - Notify prescriber if symptoms.

name: vilazodone
uses: Major depressive disorder.
action: Enhances serotonergic activity in CNS by selectively inhibiting reuptake of serotonin. Result: Relieves depression.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to vilazodone. Use of MAOIs intended to treat psychiatric disorders (with or within 14 days of stopping vilazodone or MAOI), starting vilazodone in patients receiving linezolid or methylene blue. Caution: Seizure disorder, patients at risk for suicide (history of ideation and behavior. Caution: depression), hepatic impairment, elderly.
sideEffects: Diarrhea, nausea, dizziness, dry mouth, insomnia, vomiting, decreased libido, abnormal dreams.
adverseEffects: Serotonin syndrome (agitation, confusion, hallucinations, hyperreflexia), neuroleptic malignant syndrome (fever, muscular rigidity, cognitive changes).
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Assess behavior, appearance, emotional status, response to environment, speech pattern, thought content, risk of suicide. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BP, heart rate, weight. Monitor for suicidal ideation (especially at initiation of therapy or changes in dosage). Assess for therapeutic response (greater interest in surroundings, improved self-care, increased ability to concentrate, relaxed facial expression). PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Avoid tasks that may require alertness, motor skills until response to drug is es-tablished(may cause dizziness). - Slowly go from lying to standing. - Take with food. - Do not suddenly stop taking medication; withdraw graduall.

name: viloxazine
uses: Attention deficit hyperac-tivity disorder (ADHD) in pediatric patients 6–17 yrs of age.
action: Blocks the reuptake of norepinephrine. The exact mechanism for the treatment of ADHD has not been fully elucidated. Result: Increases motor acuity, attention span, mental alertness.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to viloxa-zine. Use or within 14 days after MAOI therapy. Concomitant use of sensitive CYP1A2 substrates or CYP1A2 substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. Caution: Family history of suicide, psychiatric disorders. Caution: Personal history of hypertension, tachycardia, bipolar disorder, depression, psychosis, mania, other psychiatric illness. Caution: Pts at high risk for suicide ideation and behavior. Caution: concomitant use of CYP2D6 substrates, CYP3A4 substrates.
sideEffects: Somnolence, lethargy, headache (migraine, tension headache), decreased appetite, fatigue, abdominal pain, nausea.
adverseEffects: May increase risk of suicidal thoughts and behavior. Increased heart rate ≥ 20 bpm reported in 22%–34% of patients. Increased diastolic blood pressure ≥ 15 mm Hg reported in 13%–25% of patients. May cause manic or mixed episodes in patients with history of bipolar disorder.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain BP, heart rate, height/weight. Assess attention span, impulsivity, interaction with others, distractibility. Question for history of hepatic impairment, hyper-tension;anxiety, bipolar disorder, depression; family history of suicide, psychiatric disorder. Receive full medication history and screen for interactions (especially use of MAOIs, sensitive CYP1A2 substrates or CYP1A2 substrates with a narrow therapeutic index). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor BP, heart rate periodically and during titration. Assess height/weight periodically. Diligently monitor for new-onset or worsening of agitation, anxiety, depression, mood disorder, panic.

name: vinorelbine
uses: Single agent or in combination with CISplatin for unresectable, advanced or metastatic, non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
action: Binds to tubulin, inhibiting micro-tubule formation; may interfere with nucleic acid protein synthesis. Result: Prevents cellular division by disrupting formation of mitotic spindle.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to vinorelbine. Caution: Compromised marrow reserve due to prior chemotherapy/radiation therapy. Caution: hepatic impairment, neuropathy, pulmonary impairment.

name: vismodegib
uses: Adults with metastatic basal cell carcinoma, or with locally advanced basal cell carcinoma with recurrence after surgery, or patients who are not candidates for surgery or radiation.
action: Selectively inhibits Hedgehog pathway by binding to and inhibiting smoothened, a transmembrane protein involved in Hedgehog signal transduction. Hedgehog mutations associated with basal cell cancer can activate the pathway, resulting in proliferation of skin basal cells. Result: Inhibits tumor cell growth and survival.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to vis-modegib. Caution: Hepatic impairment.
sideEffects: Muscle spasm, alopecia, dysgeusia, weight loss, fatigue, nausea, amenor-rhea, diarrhea.
adverseEffects: Severe cutaneous reactions including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis. Drug reaction with eosino-philia and systemic symptoms (DRESS), also known as multiorgan hypersensitivity, has been reported. DRESS may present with facial swelling, eosinophilia, fever, lymphadenopathy, rash, which may be associated with other organ systems, such as hepatitis, hematologic abnormalities, myocarditis, nephritis.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Question history of hepatic impairment. Offer emotional support. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor for cutaneous toxicities; symptoms of DRESS. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Use effective contraception to avoid pregnancy. Do not breastfeed. - Do not donate blood for at least 2 yrs. Toxic skin reactions (necrosis, redness, sloughing) may occur. - Severe multi-organ hypersensitivity reaction (DRESS) may cause life-threatening organ dysfunction; report chest pain, decreased urinary output, facial swelling, fever, rash, swelling of lymph nodes. Vitamin D (vitamin D analogues).

name: voriconazole
uses: Invasive aspergillosis, esopha-geal candidiasis. Serious fungal infections caused by Scedosporium apiospermum, Fusarium spp. Candidemia in non-neutropenic patients. Disseminated Candida infections of skin and abdomen, kidney, bladder wall, and wounds2 yrs and older.
action: Interferes with fungal cytochrome P450 activity, decreasing ergosterol synthesis, inhibiting fungal cell membrane formation. Result: Damages fungal cell wall membrane.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to voriconazole. Concurrent administration of barbiturates (long acting), carBAMazepine, efavirenz (400 mg/day or greater), ergot alkaloids, pimozide, ivabradine, naloxegol, pimozide, quiNI-Dine (may cause prolonged QT interval, torsades de pointes), rifabutin, rifAMPin, ritonavir (800 mg/day or greater), siro-limus, St. John’s wort tolvaptan, veneto-clax (during initiation and titration in patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma).
sideEffects: Abnormal vision, fever, nausea, rash, vomiting, headache, chills, hallucinations.
adverseEffects: Hepatotoxicity (jaundice, hepatitis, hepatic failure), acute renal failure have occurred in severely ill patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain BMP, LFT; ECG. Correct electrolyte deficiencies prior to initiating treatment. Receive full medication history and screen for interactions. Question medical history as listed in Precautions. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor serum renal function, LFT. Monitor visual function (visual acuity, visual field, color perception) for drug therapy lasting longer than 28 days. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Take at least 1 hr before or 1 hr after a meal. - Avoid grapefruit products. - Report visual changes (blurred vision, photophobia, yellowing of skin/eyes). - Avoid performing hazardous tasks if changes in vision occur. - Avoid direct sunlight. - Women of childbear.

name: vortioxetine
uses: Major depressive disorder.
action: Blocks reuptake of neurotransmitter serotonin at CNS presynaptic membranes, increasing availability at postsynaptic receptor sites. Result: Relieves depression.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to vortioxetine. Use of monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) intended to treat psychiatric disorders concurrently or within 21 days of stopping vortioxetine; do not use vortioxetine within 14 days of stopping an MAOI. Initiation of vortioxetine in patients receiving linezolid or intravenous methylene blue. Caution: Dehydration, hepatic impairment, elderly, patients at risk for bleeding (e.g., history of intracranial/GI/genitourinary bleeding, coagulation disorders, rec.
sideEffects: Nausea, sexual dysfunction, diarrhea. Dizziness, dry mouth, constipation, vomiting, flatulence, abnormal dreams.
adverseEffects: Life-threatening serotonin syndrome may include mental status changes (agitation, hallucinations, delirium, coma), autonomic instability (tachycardia, labile blood pressure, dizziness, sweating, flushing, hyperthermia), neuromuscular symptoms (tremor, rigidity, myoclonus [localized muscle twitching], hyperactive reflexes, incoordination), seizures, GI symptoms (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea). May increase risk of bleeding events such as ecchymosis, hematoma, epistaxis (nosebleed), petechiae.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain serum electrolytes. Note serum sodium level. Assess appearance, behavior, speech pattern, level of interest, mood. Assess risk for bleeding. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor serum sodium levels. Screen for signs of SIADH (confusion, seizures). Diligently screen for suicidal ideation and behavior; new onset or worsening of anxiety, depression, mood disorder. Assess for improvement of depression (improved emotion, self-image, interest in activities; decreased agitation, loneliness, self-harm).

name: warfarin
uses: Prophylaxis and treatment of thromboembolic disorders. Prevention of embolic complications from atrial fibrillation or valve replacement. Risk reduction of systemic embolism following MI.
action: Interferes with hepatic synthesis of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors, resulting in depletion of coagulation factors II, VII, IX, X. Result: Prevents further extension of formed existing clot; prevents new clot formation, secondary thromboembolic complications.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to warfarin. Hemorrhagic tendencies (e.g., cerebral aneurysms, bleeding from GI tract), recent or potential surgery of eye or CNS, neurosurgical procedures, open wounds, severe uncontrolled or malignant hypertension, spinal puncture procedures, uncontrolled bleeding, ulcers, unreliable or noncompliant patients, unsupervised patients, blood dyscrasias, pericarditis or pericardial effusion, pregnancy (except in women with mechanical heart valves at high risk for thromboem.
sideEffects: GI distress (nausea, anorexia, abdominal cramps, diarrhea). Hypersensitivity reaction (dermatitis, urticaria), especially in those sensitive to aspirin.
adverseEffects: Hemorrhagic events including local ecchymoses to major hemorrhage (intra-cranial hemorrhage, GI/GU/nasal /oral /rectal bleeding) may occur. Hepatotoxic-ity, blood dyscrasias, necrosis, vasculitis, local thrombosis occur rarely. Antidote: Vitamin K. Amount based on INR, significance of bleeding.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, PT/INR. Obtain genotyping prior to initiating therapy if available. Screen for major active bleeding, contraindications. Question recent history of bleeding, recent trauma, surgical procedures, epidural anesthesia. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Obtain CBC, PT/INR daily until therapeutic level is achieved. When stabilized, follow with INR determination q4–6wks. Assess CBC for anemia; urine/stool for occult blood. Monitor for hypotension; complaints of abdominal /back pain, severe headache, confusion, seizures, hemipare-sis, aphasia (may be sign of hemorrhage).

name: zanamivir
uses: Uncomplicated acute illness due to influenza virus A and B in adults, children 7 yrs and older who have been symptomatic for < 2 days. Influenza A and B5 yrs and older.
action: Inhibits influenza virus enzyme neur-aminidase, essential for viral replication. Result: Prevents viral release from infected cells.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to zanamivir. Caution: Not recommended in pulmonary disease (e.g., COPD, asthma).
sideEffects: Diarrhea, sinusitis, nausea, bronchitis, cough, dizziness, headache, malaise.
adverseEffects: May cause neutropenia. Bronchospasm may occur in patients with history of COPD, bronchial asthma. Neuropsychiatric events (e.g., confusion, seizures, hallucinations) have been reported.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Pts requiring an inhaled bronchodilator at same time as zanamivir should use the bronchodilator before zanamivir administration. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Provide assistance if dizziness occurs. Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Follow manufacturer guidelines for use of delivery device. - Avoid contact with those who are at high risk for influenza. - Continue treatment for full 5-day course. - In.

name: zanubrutinib
uses: Adults with relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) who have received at least one prior therapy. Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia in adults. Adults with relapsed or refractory marginal zone lymphoma (MZL) who have received at least one anti-CD20-based regimen. Adults with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) or small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL).
action: Highly selective BTK inhibitor that forms a covalent bond with a cysteine residue in the BTK active site, inhibiting activity of BKT. BKT is a signaling molecule of pathways necessary for B-cell proliferation. Result: Inhibits malignant B-cell proliferation and reduces tumor growth.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to za-nubrutinib. Caution: Baseline cytopenias, hepatic/renal impairment, conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immunocompromised patients, open wounds), chronic opportunistic infections (e.g., herpesvirus infection, hepatitis B virus [HBV] infection, fungal infections), patients at risk for bleeding (e.g., history of intra-cranial/Gl/genitourinary bleeding, coagulation disorders, recent trauma, concomitant use of anticoagulants, antiplat.
sideEffects: Rash, diarrhea, bruising, mus-culoskeletal pain, myalgia, back pain, arthralgia, constipation.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (anemia, leukopenia, lymphopenia, neutropenia, thrombocyto-penia) is an expected response to therapy, but more severe reactions including febrile neutropenia, hemorrhagic thrombocytopenia may occur. Life-threatening hemorrhagic events including intracranial hemorrhage, GI bleeding, hematuria, hemothorax occurred in 2% of patients. Pe-techiae, purpura reported in 50% of patients. Life-threatening bacterial, invasive fungal, viral, other opportunistic infections.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC; PT/INR (if on anticoagulation therapy); pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Confirm compliance of effective contraception. Assess risk for bleeding. Question history of atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter, cardiac disease; intracra-nial/GI/genitourinary bleeding, coagulation disorders, recent trauma; previous skin cancers.

name: zavegepant
uses: Migraines with or without aura in adults.
action: Binds to and inhibits CGRP receptor. Result: Relieves migraine headache.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to zavegepant. Caution: Avoid concomitant use of organic anion transporting polypeptide 1B3 (OATP1B3) or sodium taurocholate co-transporting polypeptide (NTCP) transporters. Caution: Not recommended in patients with eGFR < 30 mL/min. Caution: Avoid use in patients with severe hepatic impairment. Caution: Not indicated for prevention of migraine.
sideEffects: Dysgeusia, ageusia, nausea, nasal discomfort, vomiting.
adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity reactions, including facial swelling and urticaria, reported in < 1% of patients.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Question characteristics of migraine headaches (onset, location, duration, possible precipitating symptoms). Receive full medication history and screen for interactions. Question history of renal impairment. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Evaluate for relief of migraine headache (photophobia, phonophobia, nausea, vomiting, pain, dizziness, fogginess). Monitor for hypersensitivity reactions. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Allergic reactions such as difficulty breathing, severe rash may occur. If allergic reaction occurs, seek immediate medical attention. - There is a risk of interactions with other medications. Do not take newly prescribed medications unless approved by.

name: zidovudine
uses: HIV infection in combination with other antiretroviral agents. Maternal/fetal HIV transmission.
action: Interferes with viral RNA-dependent DNA polymerase, an enzyme necessary for viral HIV replication. Result: Slows HIV replication, reducing progression of HIV infection.
precautions: Contraindicated: Potentially life-threatening allergic reactions to zidovudine or its components. Caution: Bone marrow compromise, renal/hepatic impairment. Caution: Combination with interferon with or without ribavirin in HIV/hepatitis C virus (HCV) coinfection.
sideEffects: Nausea, headache, abdominal pain, asthenia, rash, fever, acne, diarrhea.
adverseEffects: Anemia (occurring most commonly after 4–6 wks of therapy), granulocytopenia may occur in patients with pretherapy low baselines. Neurotoxicity (ataxia, fatigue, lethargy, nystagmus, seizures) may occur.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, CD4 cell count, HIV RNA level, viral load. Obtain specimens for viral diagnostic tests before starting therapy (therapy may begin before results are obtained). INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor CBC, CD4 cell count, HIV RNA levels. Monitor for bleeding. Assess for headache, dizziness. Monitor daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Treatment is not a cure for HIV infection, nor does it reduce risk of transmission to others. - Do not take any medications without physician’s app.

name: ziprasidone
uses: Oral: schizophrenia in adults. Acute mania or mixed episodes associated with bipolar disorder with or without psychosis as monotherapy Maintenance bipolar disorder as adjunct to lithium or valproic acid. Injection: Acute agitation in schizophrenic patients in adults. OFF-LA BEL: Major depressive disorder (adjunct to antidepressants). Monotherapy maintenance bipolar disorder, delerium/hyperactivity in ICU, delusion infestati.
action: Antagonizes alpha-adrenergic, DOPamine, histamine, serotonin receptors; inhibits reuptake of serotonin, norepinephrine. Result: Diminishes symptoms of schizophrenia, depression.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ziprasidone. Conditions associated with risk of prolonged QT interval, congenital long QT syndrome, concurrent use of other QT-prolongation medications (e.g., amiodarone, moxi-floxacin, tacrolimus, thioridazine). Uncompensated HF. Recent MI. Caution: Pts with bradycardia, hypoka-lemia, hypomagnesemia may be at greater risk for torsades de pointes. Caution: History of MI or unstable heart disease, seizure disorder, cardiac arrhythmias, disorders in which CNS depress.
sideEffects: Headache, drowsiness, dizziness, rash, orthostatic hypotension, weight gain, restlessness, constipation.
adverseEffects: Prolongation of QT interval (as seen on ECG) may produce torsades de pointes, a form of ventricular tachycardia.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain serum magnesium, potassium; ECG to assess risk for QT interval prolongation. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Assess for therapeutic response (greater interest in surroundings, improved self-care, increased ability to concentrate, relaxed facial expression). Monitor weight. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Avoid tasks that require alertness, motor skills until response to drug is established. - Avoid alcohol. - Report chest pain, shortness of breathing, irregular heartbeats, fainting, palpitations.

name: ziv-aflibercept
uses: Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) (in combination with 5-fluorouracil, leucovorin, irinotecan [FOLFIRI]) in patients resistant to or has progressed following an oxaliplatin-contain-ing regimen.
action: A recombinant fusion protein, comprising portions of binding domains of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) receptors. Acts as a decoy receptor that prevents VEGF receptor binding/activation. Result: Produces anti-angiogenesis/tu-mor regression.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to ziv-aflibercept. Caution: Baseline cytopenias, conditions predisposing to infection (e.g., diabetes, renal failure, immuno-compromised patients, open wounds), patients at risk for bleeding (e.g., history of intra-cranial/GI/GU bleeding, coagulation disorders, recent trauma. Caution: concomitant use of anticoagulants, antiplatelet medication, NSAIDs), hypertension, elderly, history of arterial/venous thrombosis (e.g., CVA, DVT, MI, pulmonary embolism), GI perforation or hemor.
sideEffects: Diarrhea, fatigue, stomatitis, abdominal pain, decreased appetite, asthenia, dyspnea, headache.
adverseEffects: Myelosuppression (leukopenia, neu-tropenia, thrombocytopenia) is an expected response to therapy, but more severe reactions including bone marrow depression, febrile neutropenia may be life-threatening. Severe, sometimes fatal, hemorrhagic events including intracra-nial/GI/GU/nasal/postprocedural hemorrhage may occur. GI perforations occurred in < 1% of patients. May cause impaired wound healing or wound de-hiscence requiring medical intervention, GI or non-GI fistula formation, severe hypert.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain CBC, BUN, serum creatinine, LFT; urine protein; vital signs. Obtain pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential. Question for recent surgeries, dental procedures. Question history of thromboembolism (CVA, DVT, MI, pulmonary embolism), hypertension, hemorrhagic events. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor ANC, CBC for myelosuppression prior to each cycle; renal function test, LFT, urine protein periodically. Monitor BP at least q.

name: zoledronic acid
uses: Zoniela: hypercalcemia of malignancy, bone metastases from solid tumors. Multiple myeloma osteolytic lesions. Reclast: Treatment and postmenopausal osteoporosis, glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis, Paget’s disease. Osteoporosis in men to increase bone mass.
action: Inhibits bone resorption by action on osteoclasts. Inhibits osteoclast activity/skeletal calcium release induced by tumors; inhibits osteoclast-mediated resorption. Result: Tumor: Increases urinary calcium, phosphorus excretion; decreases serum calcium, phosphorus levels.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to zoledronic acid, other bisphosphonates (e.g., alendronate, risedronate). Reclast only: CrCl < 35 mL/min, acute renal impairment, hypocalcemia. Caution: Oncology indications: History of aspirin-sensitive asthma, mild to moderate renal impairment. Caution: Non-oncology indications: Pts with disturbances of calcium and mineral metabolism (e.g., hypoparathyroidism, malabsorption syndrome).
sideEffects: Fever, nausea, vomiting, constipation, hypotension, anxiety, insomnia, flu-like symptoms (fever.
adverseEffects: Renal toxicity may occur if IV infusion is administered in < 15 min.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Obtain renal function test; serum calcium, phosphate. Assess hydration status (adequate hydration is essential to reduce renal injury). Obtain dental exam for. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Monitor renal function; serum calcium, phosphate. Assess vertebral bone mass (document stabilization, improvement). Assess for fever. Monitor food intake, daily pattern of bowel activity, stool consistency. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING s at risk for osteonecrosis.

name: zonisamide
uses: Adjunct for focal (partial) onset seizures.
action: May stabilize neuronal membranes, suppress neuronal hypersynchronization by blocking sodium, calcium channels. Result: Reduces seizure activity.
precautions: Contraindicated: Hypersensitivity to zonisamide. Allergy to sulfonamides. Caution: Renal/hepatic impairment, metabolic acidosis (e.g., severe respiratory disease). Caution: history of suicidal ideation and behavior.
sideEffects: Drowsiness, dizziness, anorexia, headache, agitation, irritability, nausea, fatigue.
adverseEffects: Overdose characterized by bradycardia, hypotension, respiratory depression, coma. Leukopenia, anemia, thrombocy-topenia occur rarely.
nursingConsiderations: BASELINE ASSESSMENT Review history of seizure disorder (intensity, frequency, duration, level of consciousness). Initiate seizure precautions. CBC, LFT should be performed before therapy begins and periodically during therapy. INTERVENTION/EVALUATION Observe frequently for recurrence of seizure activity. Assess for clinical improvement (decrease in intensity, frequency of seizures). Assist with ambulation if dizziness occurs. PATIENT/FAMILY TEACHING - Strict maintenance of drug therapy is essential for seizure control. - Avoid tasks that require alertness, motor skills until response to drug is established. - Avoid alcohol. - Report if rash, back/abdominal pain, blood in urine.
